// Phaladīpikā // (The Lamp of the Fruits)
The First Chapter:
Classification of the Zodiac Signs. [One should meditate upon] the God who wears white garments, who is moon-colored, and has four arms.
One should meditate upon him with a serene countenance for the pacification of all obstacles; he who bestows his vision upon the ancestors and gods,
and who ascends upwards by means of the months, years, days, and half-days.
May that singular Light, which at times moves to the left and at times to the right, grant us immeasurable prosperity. || 1 ||
Having bowed with devotion to the Goddess of Speech, my family deity, my gurus who bestow the knowledge of the Kālatantra, the Sun and other deities, the nine planets, Gaṇapati, and the Lord Īśvara;
and having abridged [the teachings] declared by Atri, Parāśara, and others, the master of mantras and knower of destiny [proceeds].
I shall proclaim the *Phaladīpikā*, which is perfectly pure, for the delight of those who know the luminaries.

In this context, the time of birth must first be specifically understood through instruments such as the *padābha* and others, along with the wall-measurements (*vighaṭikā-bhitti*) at that moment; then,
by means of mathematical calculations, its equality with the observed [time] is established according to the methods of the celestial wanderers.
Having understood that state, let them also declare the power and the fruit. || 3 ||
The head, face, neck, heart, belly, waist, bladder, genitals, thighs, the pair of knees, the shanks, and the pair of feet—
these are the limbs of Time [the zodiac] from Aries to Pisces.
Furthermore, others are renowned for their mastery of the *bha-sandhi* throughout all the worlds.
Wandering through forests, fields, dwellings,
natural groves, mountains, paths, lands rich with crops, terrifying deserts,
royal palaces, watered woods, and sacred abodes;
My residence is declared to be in Kulāla and Kīlāla from the sign of Aries. || 5 ||
Mars, Venus, Mercury, the Moon, Saturn, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn, and Jupiter are declared by me to be, in order, the lords of the signs beginning with Aries.
From the Sun, the exaltation signs are Aries, Taurus, Capricorn, Leo, Scorpio, Pisces, and Libra.
Their points of depression (astanīca) are, respectively, one-third of the degrees of the directions, and one-eighth, one-fourth, one-fifth, and one-ninth of those same degrees. || 6 ||

The signs of Leo, Taurus, Aries, Virgo, and Sagittarius are the domiciles of the Sun; those of Mercury and the Moon are Cancer, Gemini, Pisces, Aquarius, Scorpio, Libra, Capricorn, and Virgo respectively; and the human signs (Aquarius, Capricorn, and Libra) and Scorpio are the domiciles of Venus. The exaltation degrees for the Sun, Mercury, and the Moon are 15, 27, and 3 degrees respectively; for Venus, they are 27, 20, 15, 5, 27, 20, 15, and 5 degrees. For Mars, Saturn, and Jupiter, they are 28, 20, and 5 degrees respectively. The signs beginning with Sagittarius are each divided into two halves, and the human signs (Aquarius, Capricorn, and Libra) are likewise divided; Scorpio and Virgo are the remaining signs.
The aquatic animals, the karkamṛgas, those with hind legs shorter than the front, the śapharas, and the quadrupeds are the remainder. || 7 ||
The signs beginning with Taurus, Aries, Capricorn, and Aquarius, as well as Virgo and Pisces, are the signs that rise by their backs (pṛṣṭhodaya) and their navamshas;
Gemini and Libra rise by their sides (pārśvodaya); and the remaining signs, starting from Cancer, are said in sequence to be those that rise by their heads (śīrṣodaya).
These are designated as nocturnal (aindava) and diurnal (saura) respectively. Thus ends the third [chapter].
But having emerged from the house of the sun, it shines again, half-curved and slightly crooked.

Aries and the others are declared here as movable, fixed, and dual; the door, the inner chamber, the sign, the element, and the root are thus described. They know them to be cruel and gentle respectively; Aries and the others, along with their trines, are said to be the lords of the directions starting from the east in order.
The male sign, the bear (Capricorn), and the even signs are the right side; the female sign, the left (Cancer), and the others beginning with Libra are the left side. || 9 ||
The Ascendant (Lagna), the Hora, that which is called the rising of the auspicious body, the form, the head, and the current birth;
wealth, knowledge, one's own food and drink, enjoyment, the right eye, mouth, speech, and the family—these are [the significations]. (10)
The right ear of one who is difficult to pierce, as well as his army, fortitude, heroism, valor, brother, home, field, maternal uncle, nephew, kinsman, friend, vehicle, and mother. || 11 ||
The [first] house signifies kingdom, cattle, buffaloes, fragrant scents, garments, and ornaments; the fourth house signifies the netherworld (pātāla), happiness, water, bridges, and rivers;
the tenth house signifies the king, ministers, hands, one's own intellect, future events, life-force, children, the belly, the Vedas, and the legal codes (smṛtis). 12.

Debts, weapons, thieves, wounds, diseases, and enemies; kinsmen, strife, evil deeds, sin, fear, and contempt; intoxication arising from the minds of one's wife and friends, lust, gambling, travel, the world, the husband, the path, and the wife. (13)
The auspicious openings, the lords of the quarters, life, the afflictions, slander, death, impurity, obstacles, and servants;
the teachers, deities, and ancestors; and the merits of former auspicious lives—
[He bestowed] worship, austerity, merit, grandsons, recitation, and noble lineages.
[The Sun] bestows professional activity, honor, merit born of action, fame, sacrifice, livelihood, movement through the sky, virtuous conduct, progress, and commands;
as well as prosperity, gain, arrival, attainment, success, wealth, acquisition, existence, and praiseworthiness.
Hearing the pleasant words of his elder brother was like hearing the sweet sound from the ear-lotuses of the virtuous. || 15 ||
The houses are declared in order to indicate suffering, feet, eyes, emaciation, destruction, beauty, poverty, sin, sleep, loss, enemies, and bondage; then, the hidden...
The third, sixth, twelfth, and eighth signs are the positions of defeat for the planets. || 16 ||

They say that the eighth, sixth, and twelfth houses are ill-placed (duḥsthāna), while any other house is a well-placed (susthāna) and is declared to bestow auspicious results. They call the first, tenth, seventh, and fourth houses the "centers" (kendras); indeed, they are known as the four "angles" (kaṇṭakas). || 17 ||
The fourth house from the ascendant is called *paṇakara*; beyond that is the *kendras*, and then the *āpoklimas*.

Next are the *caturasras* (quadrants), then the *naidhanas*, followed by the house of kinsmen (*bandhubha*). Then follow the houses of increase (*samupacayas*): the tenth, the third, the sixth, and the eleventh.
The ninth, fifth, and fourth houses form a trine, which is highly auspicious. || 18 ||
Chapter Two:
The Classification of Planets (Grahabheda)
Copper and gold bring auspicious results for the ancestors, as well as personal happiness, majesty, fortitude, valor, victory in battle, royal service, and renown;
[the asterism] Śravaṇa brings success in undertakings, movement through forests and mountains, and engagement in fire-offerings (homa).
May the wise one describe the positions of the planets, their sharpness, and their vigor derived from the Sun.
A mother’s well-being, clarity of mind, bathing in the ocean,

a white chowrie, an umbrella, a fine fan, fruits, soft flowers, crops, agriculture, fame, pearls, bell-metal, silver, sweet milk and the like, clothing, water, and cattle— [these are obtained through the sight of a pregnant woman].
One should predict the acquisition of a woman, the enjoyment of pleasure, physical well-being, and beauty from the Moon.

One should declare from the Mahājā [sign] the following: courage, the ripening of the earth's fruits, qualities of siblings, cruelty, battle, rashness, enmity, as well as the kitchen, fire, kinsmen, weapons, thieves, and enemies; enthusiasm, dalliance with another's wife, and speaking untruths.
He lost his two-fold majesty, the loftiness of his mind, his turbid sovereignty over the army, and his honor. || 3 ||
[The ocean] is scholarship, eloquent speech, extreme proficiency in the arts, the praise of the learned, maternal uncles, cleverness of expression, skill in ritual services and the like,
logical reasoning in the sciences, intellect, sacrifice, Vaiṣṇava rites, truthful speech, pearls, and places of recreation.
He [obtained] craftsmanship from his kinsmen, the status of crown prince from his friends, and that [wisdom] from his nephew, Budha.

Knowledge, virtuous qualities, one’s own son as a minister, self-restraint, the status of a teacher, magnanimity, learning, sacred scriptures, wisdom, memory, intelligence, universal excellence, freedom from distress,
the path of the righteous, devotion to the gods and Brahmins, sacrifice, austerity, faith, and the treasury— these constitute the constituent parts [of the state].
Eloquence, mastery over the senses, the happiness of a husband, honor, and compassion for the praiseworthy.
Prosperity, vehicles, garments, ornaments, treasures, wealth, the three types of musical arts, the happiness of a wife, fragrant flowers, amorous activities,
beds, dwellings, majesty, the joy of poetry, union with many wives, luxury, and intoxication— [these are the results].
It describes the assistance [offered] by the son of Bhṛgu (Śukra) and the festival of the horse-sacrifice.
Longevity brings the fear of death; falling leads to suffering, humiliation, and disease;

poverty brings the impurity of being a servant and the reproach of others, as well as impurity, blame, and calamities; reliance on base people brings instability; and a buffalo brings lethargy and iron-like debt.
From the son of the Sun (Saturn), there is servitude, means for agriculture, imprisonment, and bondage.

The Sun has bone-marrow of the bile type, possesses sparse hair, and is reddish-black in appearance; he has honey-tawny eyes, wears saffron-colored garments, and has a square-shaped body; he is heroic, fierce, and has broad arms. (8)
Stout, youthful, and aged; white-complexioned with lovely eyes, or dark with fine hair;
having blood as his sole vital essence, soft-spoken, wearing white garments, fair-skinned, and gentle—such is the person whose nature consists of wind and phlegm (vātakaphātmaka). || 9 ||
One born under Mars is thin in the middle, with curled and radiant hair, cruel eyes, a bilious temperament, and fierce intelligence;
he wears red garments, has a reddish body, is impetuous, extremely generous, youthful, and possesses abundant marrow. 10.

One whose body is dark like a creeper, who possesses the three humors (dhātus), has prominent veins, is endowed with sweet speech, has red and long eyes, wears green garments, has skin as his only wealth, is wise, fond of laughter, and is well-proportioned; || 11 ||
He shall have a yellow luster, with tawny hair and eyes; he will possess a stout and elevated chest and a large body.
Being of a phlegmatic temperament, he will be of excellent intellect, worshipful to the gods, possessing the roar of a lion and a lotus, and preeminent in wealth. || 12 ||

Wearing variegated garments with curly black hair, possessing thick armlets and a nature dominated by phlegm and wind, resembling a blade of durva grass, charming, large-eyed, and having increased his white [semen] through practice—such is Bhrgu. (13)
Lame, with sunken eyes, thin-bodied and tall, marked by furrows, lazy, dark-limbed, composed of wind, extremely malicious,
consisting of sinews, pitiless, foolish, with large nails and teeth, with coarse hair on the body, impure, and characterized by darkness (tamas).
Fierce, devoted to wrath, aged and decrepit, clad in black garments, he is the son of the Sun.
The domain of the Dog (Śauva) is the exterior radiant region of the Sun; the eastern direction is the abode of Durgā, the location of dust, herbs, and honey, and the domain of the Moon.
The southern direction is declared to be the abode of the Thief (Cora), the Mleccha, Fire, and the battlefield of Mars.
They know the positions of the learned, Viṣṇu, the assembly, the wandering host, and the astrologer to be in the north. || 15 ||
The northeast direction is the abode of the Lord of the Gods (Indra), containing treasuries, holy fig trees, and temples for the twice-born;

it is the place for the paths of courtesans, the removal of obstacles, dancing, and the bedchamber. The southeast is the direction of Agni, containing low-caste quarters and impure places. The southwest is the direction of Varuṇa, the abode of the Teacher (Bṛhaspati) and of Saturn.
Ant-hills, termite mounds, the abodes of snakes and fire, and the directions guarded by the Rākṣasas. || 16 ||

A devotee of Śiva, a physician, a king, a performer of sacrifices, a leader, a hunter, a deer, the *cakravāka* bird of the sun, a teacher, a woman, a washerman, a harsh person, and those who frequent the water— these are said to be the [signs] of the Lord.
The hare, the deer, the crane, and the cakora bird [are the marks] of the moon. || 17 ||
Bhauma [Mars] is associated with those who carry weapons in the kitchen, goldsmiths, royal cocks, jackals, crows, vultures, thieves,
cowherds, artisans, astrologers, eminent men, and the servants of Viṣṇu.
The Tārkṣya, the Kikīdivi, the parrot, the hare, and the cat. || 18 ||
The foremost among those who know the stars, mantrins, gurus, brahmins, and ascetics;
the pigeon, the horse of the preceptor of the gods (Bṛhaspati), and the swan;
the singer, the wealthy man, the lecher, the merchant, the actor, and the weaver—
A courtesan, a peacock, and a buffalo belong to Venus; a parrot and a cow [belong to Venus]. (19)
The sellers of oil, hired laborers, low-caste people, Kirātas, artisans,
those who deal in ivory and elephants' tusks, cuckoos, Buddhists, snake-charmers, donkeys, kings, wolves, camels, and serpents belong to Saturn.
Darkness and so forth, mosquitoes, bedbugs, worms, and owls. || 20 ||
Mercury is friendly, while Saturn and Venus are neutral; the Sun and Moon are enemies of the Sun; the others (Jupiter and Mars) are neutral.
For Mars, Saturn and Venus are neutral, but Mercury is an enemy.
For Mercury, Jupiter is the enemy, while Venus and the Sun are the friends. || 21 ||
Mars is an enemy to Mercury and Jupiter; Saturn is neutral to them;
and Venus and Mars are friends to Mercury. Saturn and Mercury are neutral to Jupiter; Jupiter is neutral to Venus and Mercury; and Saturn is a friend to Venus.
The unmentioned planets, however, should be known to be otherwise than that. || 22 ||
Those who mutually possess the three kinds of happiness, self-patience, and are situated in the state of non-becoming (nirvāṇa) are friends at that time;
having observed this natural disposition, one should declare those to be very dear friends.
[In the matter of] valor and commands, Saturn and Jupiter, Jupiter’s son (Mercury), and Mars are [the lords] of the fourth and eighth [houses].
One sees the seventh [digit] as full; among these, all [digits] increase in sequence according to the growth of the blind spot (andhri). || 23 ||

The sun and other [planets] are said to be the *ayanam*, the *kṣaṇa*, the day, the season, the month, the fortnight, autumn, winter, Venus, Jupiter, the son of the Sun (Saturn), Mars, the Moon, Mercury, and finally Saturn;
they are also called *sattva*, *rajas*, and *tamas*, as well as the Moon, Jupiter, the Sun, Venus, Mercury, and the others.
In the summer season, the Sun, Mars, the Moon, Mercury, Jupiter, Saturn, and Venus [are the lords of the days]. || 24 ||
Father and mother are said to be the Sun and Venus by day, and the Sun and Moon by night; conversely, they are designated as paternal uncle and maternal sister respectively according to that order.
The left eye is the Moon and the right eye is the Sun; Mars is said to be the younger brother of the little finger.
Jīva, Jyeṣṭhasahodara, Śaśisuta, Dattātmaja, and Saṃjñita; || 25 ||
The body, the embodied soul, the moon, the sense organs, the wind, the sun, the enemy of the sun (Rahu), the pill (Gulika), and the fire—these are the afflictors.
The smell is lunar; the two tastes belong to Venus and the Moon; the two [qualities] belong to the Sun and Mars.
Form, sound, and the teacher (the Guru) are the first; thereafter, touch and its designation are proclaimed as the others. || 26 ||

The waning Moon, the Sun, Mars, Rāhu, Ketu, Saturn, and Jupiter are malefic planets; Venus is both malefic and neutral; Mercury and Ketu are eunuchs; the Moon, Rāhu, and Venus are female; and the others are male.
Their presiding deities are indeed Rudra, Ambā (Gaurī), Guha, Viṣṇu, Dhātṛ, Kamalā, Kālā, and Aja (Brahmā).
From the Sun [arise] the planets consisting of fire, water, fire, earth, ether, water, and air. || 27 ||
Wheat, rice, sesame, chickpeas, horse-gram, black gram, green gram, flat beans,
and kidney beans belong to Saturn, the Moon, Mars, Jupiter, the Sun, Rahu, Venus,
Mercury, the Moon, Ketu, and Venus respectively; [the products] of the planets beginning with the Sun are known as Ambarākhya and Kaliṅga.
[He conquered] Saurāṣṭra, Avanti, Sindhu, Sumagadha, Yavana, Parvata, and Kīkaṭa. || 28 ||
The ruby of the Sun is to be well-worn, the pure pearl of the Moon, coral of Mars, emerald of Mercury, the diamond of Jupiter,
the topaz of Venus, and the diamond of Saturn.
Nīla is pure; Gomedha and Vaidūryaka are said to be of the other two types.
Copper, bell-metal, and metallic copper; tin, gold, silver, and iron [are the metals] of the Sun and the other planets respectively.
Cloth should be of their respective colors, especially that which is worn out for Saturn and scorched by fire for Mars.

The taste of the Sun is pungent, that of Mars is bitter, and that of the Moon is salty; furthermore, the taste of Mercury is sweet, that of Jupiter is mixed, that of Venus is sour, and that of Saturn is astringent. (31)
The Sun, Moon, Jupiter, and Mars have their marks on the right side;
for the remaining planets, it is on the other side. From the Sun onwards, the signs are located on the waist, head, back, armpit, shoulder, face, and feet respectively.
O Lord, this is not the shore, nor the nail, nor the mountain, nor the one endowed with knowledge, nor the naked wanderer. || 32 ||

Rāhu has a dark-blue luster, a tall body, and an ugly complexion; he is afflicted with scabies, holds heretical views, and suffers from hiccups. He is a liar, deceitful, leprous, and censures others while lacking intelligence. (33)
With a body whose fierce gaze is red and full of poison, he is armed and fallen;
his luster is smoky, he constantly inhales smoke, his limbs are marked by wounds, and he is emaciated and cruel. (34)
Lead and worn-out clothing are assigned to Tamas;
a clay vessel and a multicolored cloth to Ketu;
and various white and dark-colored items are the friends of both Tamas and Rahu.
Bhauma (Mars) is declared to be neutral, and the remaining planets are enemies. || 35 ||

Even a dull-witted person, if the [malefic] planet is in a low sign, in an enemy's sign, or situated in the eighth, sixth, or twelfth house, is considered to be in an unfavorable state; otherwise, he would be well-situated. However, if the Moon is situated in the twelfth, first, sixth, fifth, or seventh house, [the result is different].
In this matter, it indicates an increase in water for the purpose of prosperity. || 36 ||
The planet Mars is said to be a red tree with internal sap and height, while Mercury is a creeper; Jupiter is a white moon, and Saturn is a thorny tree.
Venus is a bush, and Ketu is a serpent; the Lord of Speech (Jupiter) is a fruitful tree, and the son of the Moon (Mercury) is a fruitless tree that bears milk-like flowers.
The parrot, the moon, the Vidhura herb, Saturn, the Asārāga bird, and the Sāla tree. || 37 ||
Chapter Three:
Classification of Categories (Varga-vibhāga)
The third, ninth, tenth, eleventh, thirtieth, seventh, sixtieth, and sixty-fourth parts of a sign are known as the *daśavarga* divisions;
these, together with the twelfth part, constitute the ten-fold division (*daśavarga*). Among these, the ninth part within its own respective domicile is called *vargottama*.

Those seven divisions (saptavarga), diminished by one-tenth, one-sixtieth, and one-sixth parts respectively, are known as the six divisions (ṣaḍvarga); furthermore, some hold that the result of the ninth-part (navāṃśa) is equal to the results of the signs and the houses. || 2 ||
In the [astrological] fields, the fruit is full and increasing; in other groups, it is half, a sixteenth part, a tenth, and a sixtieth part;
and there are six states: infant, child, youth, adolescent, old age, and death.
The divisions follow the sequence in the even [pādas], while the reverse occurs in the odd; such are the positions. || 3 ||
In an odd sign, the *horā* consists of half the *kṣetra* (the sign) plus [half] the portion of the Sun and Moon; in an even sign, it is the reverse.

The lords of the *dreṣkāṇas* are the third-parts of the body, children, and benefics and malefics respectively. The *dvādaśāṃśa* from the ascendant consists of Mars, Saturn, Mercury, Jupiter, and Venus; indeed, in an odd sign, they are the first, third, and fifth parts, while in an even sign, it is the reverse.
In the reverse order, the lords of the thirty-degree portions (triṃśāṃśa) are Aries, Capricorn, and Libra; the nine-degree portions (navāṃśa) begin with Cancer. || 4 ||
Yajña, Ratna, Jana, Dhana, Naya, Paṭa, Rūpa, Śuka, Ciṭin, Nāga, Yoga, Khaga, Bala, Bhaga, Śilā, Dhūli, Nava, Prasvana,
Lābha, Viśva, Diva, Rama, and Dharma are the sixty parts (ṣaṣṭyaṃśaka) in the sign of Aja (Aries).
Those called cruel are in even signs; this is the reverse for the remaining ones, which are termed gentle.
From the [sign] itself, the periods for the seventh and tenth portions are determined; however, in an odd sign, they proceed from the fifth, the auspicious [the ninth], the self, and the lord.
In an even sign, the lords of the minute-portions (kalāṃśa) are Brahmā (1), Hari (2), Īśa (3), and Arka (12), or otherwise.
By those known as joined with angles (koṇa), trines, their own houses, exaltations, and the best of quadrants—
The groups are declared by others to be seven, ten, and thirteen in number. || 6 ||
One should apply thirteen groups of friends to their own signs and exaltations in sequence—
namely two, three, five, four, seven, eight, and six times— based on the sum of the Vargas.
These are declared as the Siṃhāsana and Gopura by the author of the Uttamapārijāta.
And he [attained] the worlds of Cetya, Airāvata, and Devaloka, as well as the portions of the world of the Suras and Pārāvata.

If a planet situated in its own sign of excellence (uttamāṃśa) bestows noble lineage, virtues, wealth, happiness, and power— being like a portion of the Pārijāta tree— and if that planet, possessing a virtuous mind, occupies the Gopura division of its own domain, it bestows a magnificent residence.
He who, seated upon the lion-throne, [beheld] a man beloved by the lord of kings, the son of a monarch.

If one presides over the splendor of excellent horses, elephants, vehicles, and so forth, together with the world of the gods, one possesses true fame; yet, if one presides over a portion of Airāvata, one becomes a sovereign of the earth’s circle,
worthy of being saluted by kings and equal to the Lord of the Gods.
The planet shall make the king possessed of good fortune and endowed with wealth, grain, and sons.
O weak one, since death occurs here within all the groups [of planets], I shall now describe in order their destruction,

suffering, misfortune, and adversity; however, that which is dear to kinsmen is better when the entire group is strongest— [yielding] a king’s favorite, a wealthy man, a ruler, or an excellent sovereign.
The physician [should consider] the king who is happy, as well as the results for childhood and other stages of life according to the diseases and the [relevant] immortality [treatises]. || 10 ||

If the six divisions (*ṣaḍvarga*) possess the superior qualities of benefic planets, the illustrious person lives for a long time; however, if they abound in malefic portions (*krūrāṃśa*), he is wretched, short-lived, and deceitful. If their lords are strong, there is a king; furthermore, the lord of the *navāṃśa* is the lord of the *dṛgāṇa*.
The lord of the ascendant, in due order, makes one happy, equal to a king, a sovereign of the earth, and fortunate. (11)

If a malefic planet has entered the Sun's horā, one born will be powerful, of cruel disposition, and wealthy; if it is the Moon's horā in a dual sign, he will possess splendor, modesty, pleasant speech, and good fortune. In the opposite case (a benefic), the results are reversed; when mixed, the results are said to be middling. Thus have been declared the effects based on the strength of the Ascendant and the Moon.
If its two lords are likewise, then one becomes long-lived, yet miserable and famous. || 12 ||
In the houses of Leo, Aries, Libra, and Gemini, the last [digit] is a horse; in Taurus and Virgo, the first is a goat;

in the two female signs (Cancer and Scorpio), the middle two are weapon-bearers; in Aquarius, the middle is a noose; in Capricorn, the first is a shackle; and in Leo and Aquarius, the first is a merchant and the middle is a merchant.
The bird with a vulture's face has the bull as its final [sign], while the one with a boar's face begins with Cancer. || 13 ||

Aquarius and the others ending with Cancer, Capricorn and the others ending with Leo, and Gemini and the others ending with Virgo constitute the four-footed signs; their results here are wealth, cruelty, blameworthiness, and poverty respectively.
In the dual signs, the results are inferior, middling, and auspicious according to the *dṛgāṇas*; and in the mutable signs, they occur in the reverse order.
Those who know it say that in fixed signs, the results in the ascendant are indeed neutral, being neither inauspicious nor auspicious. (14)
If the lord of the Drekkāṇa is in its own varga, joined by a benefic planet, or situated in its exaltation or a friendly sign;
and if likewise the lord of the Triṃśāṃśa, the lord of the Dvādaśāṃśa, or the lord of the Hora is strong, then [the native] possesses a multitude of all virtues and is eternally pure and proficient.
He shall be long-lived, compassionate, endowed with sons and wealth, possessed of fame, and enjoy royal luxuries. || 15 ||
They say the ascendant is the trine of the lord of the sign occupied by Māndi, the trine of the lord of the sign of its [Māndi's] degree,
and the trine of the sign of the degree of Gulika.
In the same way, one should know [the result] when the Moon is joined with strength in its own sign. || 16 ||
The Moon situated in the third, eleventh, or tenth house bestows virtuous qualities of an auspicious nature;
however, one born in the highest division (the *uttama-varga*) produces excellent results, while one born in another division produces qualities according to its lord.
Planets occupying their own or the thirty-degree divisions (*triṃśāṃśa*) produce the effects declared for them as being the makers (*kāraka*) of those respective houses.
In that case, even a single planet, if aspected by or conjoined with a benefic and situated in its exaltation, makes the king wealthy.
In its exaltation, a planet is radiant; in a trine, it is happy; in its own house, it is self-abiding; and in the house of a friend, it is joyful.
When joined with the divisions of benefic planets, it is considered peaceful; and when its mass of rays is clearly manifest, it is deemed powerful. (18)
Overpowered by planets, he would be oppressed; a wicked man indeed when situated in the division of malefic planets.
The lord of planets is extremely miserable in the house of an enemy, exceedingly terrified in its sign of debilitation, and distressed when set. (19)

Full planets bestow prosperity, while those that are combust or deficient bestow emptiness; through their proportional strength in the middle, they produce auspicious results in due order, and conversely, in reverse order, they produce inauspicious results—such being the fruits corresponding to their names.
Chapter Four:
The Strength of the Planets (Grahabala)

He states that the strength of the celestial bodies is sixfold, occurring respectively as: the strength born of time (*kālaja*), the strength born of the sign (*rāśija*), the strength born of its own exaltation (*svoccaja*), the directional strength (*digvīrya*), the strength arising from the solstice (*ayanodbhava*), and the strength arising from their position (*sthānodbhava*).
At night, Mars, the Moon, and Venus [are strong]; the others [Mercury, Jupiter, and Saturn] are always [strong] in heaven; and Mercury is auspicious during the bright fortnight.
In the case of Kṛṣṇa and others, [the calculation] proceeds respectively through their own years, months, days, and hours, increased by nine, eight, seven, and six. || 1 ||

The strength of the full moon is when it rises in the north; that of the sun is when it moves retrograde; and for planets situated in the northern hemisphere during battle, their strength is great and abundant when they are in their own exaltation.
The directional strength (*digvīrya*) belongs to the Sun and Mars in the tenth house, the Moon and Venus in the fourth, and Jupiter and Mercury in the ascendant.
If Mercury, Saturn, and the Moon are situated on the southern path, while the others are on the other, which is called the northern course (ayana). || 2 ||
Planets are strong when situated in their own exaltation, their own sign, or the house of a friend, or within their own vargas;
this is declared as the fourfold strength of position (sthānabala). In order, they possess full, half, and quarter [strength].
Planets are strong in sequence when they are in the middle, at the beginning, at the end, in the neutral zone, or when they are male or female.
Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, the Moon, and Saturn increase [their respective] strengths when in their own [signs]. || 3 ||
Even if that planet has gone retrograde, possesses beautiful rays, is full and peerless, and is associated with its sign of depression or an enemy's sign, it becomes like the moon—
possessing strength through its exaltation or its friend.
Even if situated in its own sign, it is powerless if its light has been eclipsed.

All [planets] situated in their exaltations are strong; indeed, the Moon possesses strength arising from its lunar phase (pakṣa), while the Sun possesses directional strength (digbala). Among the other planets, strength is declared for retrograde motion.
Cancer, Aries, Capricorn, Aquarius, Leo, Scorpio, Pisces, Taurus, Virgo, and Libra are the signs of weakness; [the Sun is weak] when it goes to the last quarter of these signs.
The conjunction of the Moon and the Sun at night is powerful when there is a halo, a pariveṣa, or a rainbow. || 5 ||
In the human sign (Aries), Cancer, and Scorpio, the strength of the body is half; in other signs, it is equal to the strength of its lord.
When the lord is in a house of increase, the strength is exceedingly intense.
If the lord is conjoined with or aspected by Jupiter and Mercury, or conjoined with Venus and aspected by others in an odd-numbered house, [the strength is likewise great].
The zodiac signs are said to be endowed with strength during the night in the former half [of the month] and during the day in the latter half.
In its exaltation, a planet’s field-strength is full; in its own trine, three-quarters; in its own sign, half; and in the sign of a friend, one-quarter.
In the sign of an enemy, it is slight; and when situated in its fall or even set, the field-strength of the planets becomes fruitless.
The strength of the planets that has arisen in the center [the tenth house] becomes present in the fourth, the seventh, and the first houses;
indeed, they calculate the increase of strength according to the sequence of the aforementioned positions, moving higher and higher. || 8 ||
The term "excellent" (śreṣṭhā) should always be understood as referring specifically to the seventh aspect (dṛṣṭi), and not to other aspects;
for while other aspects yield inferior results in practices such as yoga, this "special aspect" has not been mentioned by anyone else. || 9 ||
Natural enmity or friendship alone should be considered the valid authority for producing results correctly;
that temporary state of enmity or friendship, which arises by the force of circumstances, is indeed unstable.
In the removal of all defects without exception and in the increase of auspiciousness,
Jupiter possesses greater strength than all other planets;
Mercury and Venus possess the power of one-quarter and one-eighth of that strength respectively.
The lunar strength, however, is the seed of the power of all the planets.
One should divide the [values] derived from the moon's action and so forth, by means of the factors of knowledge and the non-planets associated with the birth asterism;
the results obtained are called the states of the moon's action, its position, and its time, and their respective fruits follow in order.
From the state of the results of the Moon's activity,
one is fallen from his position; he is devoted to another's wife, a gambler,
mounted upon a preeminent elephant, seated upon a throne as a king who destroys his enemies, a leader of the rod (punisher), and virtuous.
Lifeless, with his head severed, his hands and feet wounded, imprisoned and ruined,
the king studies the Vedas, sleeps, behaves virtuously, remembers [his duties], and performs righteous acts.

Born of a noble lineage, endowed with hidden treasures, of learned family, devoted to exposition, a slayer of enemies, yet afflicted by disease; having conquered his foes, he departs from his own country as a servant whose wealth is lost; without a fixed station, though possessing excellent counsel, he becomes a supreme lord of the earth together with his wife—such is the elephant.
Terrified, full of fear for the battle, and extremely afraid, he hid himself within the rising flames of the fire.
Afflicted by hunger, he wanders about eating food; wounded by weapons, he subsists on flesh; though married, he plays with dice, holding a ball, as a miserable king;
lying down, he is served by enemies; and accompanied by his wife, he becomes a yogi together with his friends.
And drinking milk as his sweet food, the doer of good deeds remains healthy and dwells in happiness. || 15 ||

The results of the Moon's positions, starting from its own house, are: exile, being honored by the king, servitude, loss of life, sovereignty, devotion to virtues befitting one's own lineage, illness, and holding a position of authority.

Fear, being afflicted by hunger, marriage with a young woman, attachment to a bed of straw, and eating only what is pure—these are the states of the moon, as established by the wise through the power of the Gītā’s injunctions. 16.
The fruit of the *candravelā* is the head; joy is the sacrifice; being established in happiness is the eye; and sporting with a woman is the state of being blissful.
Fierce fever is the golden ornament; shedding tears is the spitting of venom; sexual union is the disease of the belly. 17.
Playing in water, laughing, painting various pictures, wrestling, performing dances, eating ghee, sleeping,
giving gifts, toothache, and quarreling— these are the [omens] for a journey.
And madness, immersion in water, and hostility. || 18 ||

Personal bathing, fear of hunger, acquisition of scriptures, informal gatherings, battle, meritorious deeds, sinful conduct, cruel actions, and great joy—thus have the wise prescribed the lunar periods (candravelā). 19.
In horoscopes, at the time of birth, and in queries, the movements of the Moon and other planets yield results accurately; therefore, one should consider them with particular care. (20)
They say that the excellence of the Moon arises from its aspect,
while the strength arising from its position is superior even to others; when these are combined with other factors, it becomes increasingly greater.
There would be many other things similar to that which belong to you. || 21 ||

The powerful [Sun] has six hundred and a half degrees of strength; the Moon, however, has five hundred and six; the King of the Earth (Mars) has seven; the son of Indu (Mercury) is like the Sun; Jupiter has five and a half; and Venus shall be strong [at six hundred and a half]. || 22 ||
A weak planet indeed possesses only five [of the six] powers; otherwise, it would be different.
Thus, having carefully considered the strengths and weaknesses of the planets, one should correctly declare the results. (23)
They say that the strength-piṇḍa of the lord of the ascendant and other houses is the piṇḍa of those [planets] increased by one (rūpa).
For whichever house there is directional strength (digbala), that is added to the strength of the house through its aspect. || 24 ||
The fifth chapter: The Section on Livelihood through Action.
One should describe the attainment of wealth based on the strength of the planets in relation to the ascendant and the Moon.

Those who know the science declare that one's livelihood comes from the planets situated in the tenth house—such as those representing father, mother, enemy, friend, elder brother, and so forth—or from the wife's property, or from servants;
whichever among the lord of the day (the Sun), the ascendant, and the Moon is strongest, and then according to the sign and its ninth-part (navāṃśa) occupied by the lord of the tenth house. || 1 ||

In the portion of the Sun (the Lotus-Lover), one lives by fruit-bearing trees, the recitation of mantras, through deceit, gambling, falsehoods, blankets, medicines, and the like, or perhaps by means of trade, or by serving one honored by the king. || 2 ||

Through the buying and selling of aquatic products, through agricultural work and the produce of cows and buffaloes, or from visiting sacred fords, from resorting to women, or from the purchase of clothing during the period of the Moon's influence. || 3 ||
In the sub-period (aṃśaka) of Mars, one suffers from blows from weapons or minerals, or from gold obtained from a kitchen or due to the nature of the ground;
or else, through cruelty toward others, the use of weapons, rashness, taking refuge with barbarians, or by the livelihood of an informer or a thief.

One's engagement [in worldly affairs] occurs through poetry and scriptures, by means of writing and scripts, through the power of knowledge in astrology and mathematics, during the period of Mercury, by studying the Vedas for the sake of others, through the recitation of mantras, and under the pretext of being a domestic priest. || 5 ||
In the Jīva division, through the patronage of gods and Brahmins, by the favor of the sovereign,
by the path of conduct prescribed in the Purāṇas and scriptures, through instruction in dharma, or by the profession of usury— 6.

In the sub-period of Venus, there is gain through association with women, cattle, buffaloes, elephants, horses, the three types of musical arts (song, dance, and instrumental music), silver, perfumes, milk and other products, ornaments, fine cloth, and silk; and one attains the qualities of a minister due to poetic talent.

In the sub-period of Saturn, one gains through roots and fruits, through labor, through servants, through wicked people, and through base wealth; through inferior grains, by carrying burdens, by livelihoods on despicable paths, through crafts such as woodwork, and through killing and the like.

If the lord of the navāṃśa is strong, the attainment of results occurs without effort; if the lord of the navāṃśa is weak, the aforementioned result will be meager. From the rising sign, one should declare the results for the house of action (the tenth house) according to the portion [of the zodiac]. If the lord of the navāṃśa is conjoined with or aspected by its own lord, the result will manifest in one's native country.
If other [planets] are present, that [result] arises from a foreign land; if it is in its own sign and a fixed [sign], it belongs to the portion of its ruler.
Chapter Six:
The Chapter on Yoga (Yogādhyāya)
The Rucaka, Bhadraka, Haṃsaka, Mālava, and Śaśaka are proclaimed as the five [types of houses].
One should state these respectively when Mars and the other planets have ascended to the heights of their own houses within the four [houses]. || 1 ||

Long-faced, possessing the wealth of many thousands, a hero, slayer of enemies, powerful, most proud, renowned for his virtues in Rucaka, a leader of armies, victorious, long-lived, possessing a mind as sharp as the tip of kusha grass, stainless, and praised by learned men— Please note: This appears to be a description of a specific individual (likely a king or leader) rather than a standard Sanskrit verse, as it lacks a formal metrical structure. The translation provided reflects the literal meaning of the adjectives and nouns used.
The king, born under the Bhadraka yoga, possesses great wealth and causes a tumultuous clamor in the assembly hall. || 2 ||

The king born under Haṃsa is praised by the virtuous; his feet and hands are marked with the signs of the conch, lotus, fish, and goad; he possesses an auspicious body, eats pure food, and is righteous.
He has well-developed limbs, is steadfast, wealthy, endowed with the fortune of sons and daughters-in-law, and brings prosperity.
In Mālavya, one becomes an enjoyer of happiness, possessing excellent vehicles and fame, wise, and with serene senses. || 3 ||
Praised by all people, possessing excellent servants and strength, whether a village headman or a king, though perhaps ill-behaved, wealthy through another's wife, and endowed with happiness—
this fivefold yoga of the Ascendant and the Moon bestows the attainment of sovereignty.
Among those [categories] beginning with one, the fortunate king is equal [to the previous], while the lord of kings is superior. || 4 ||

In the case of the Moon, however, *sunaphā*, *anaphā*, *dhurudhurā*, and *svariḥpha* arise when the planets are situated in both [the fourth and eighth] houses; otherwise, there is *kemadruma*. Furthermore, if the Moon is joined by four planets, there is *kemadruma*.
Or else, it is said that [the Moon] is not [so], provided the planets are situated in the angles (kendras) from the Moon. || 5 ||
Indeed, when there is *sunaphā*, the king becomes one who has acquired wealth by his own effort, or he becomes equal to him; he is possessed of intelligence,
wealth, and renown, a lord with a healthy body, virtuous, and of celebrated fame.
In the Anaphā yoga, one is well-attired with the pleasures of the senses and is at ease.
In Kemadruma, one possesses wealth, vehicles, and the enjoyment of arisen pleasures; he is rich, endowed with generosity, born of a noble lineage, and accompanied by servants.
However, those in Kemadruma may also be filthy, miserable, base, and destitute.
Even those born of the king's own lineage become servants and wicked men.

Having pierced the Moon, those known as *śubha*, *aśubha*, and *śiva*—which are the *ubhayacaryā* configurations—are formed when benefics occupy both positions relative to the Sun; they are called *papasaṃjñā* (malefic-named) when the malefics occupy them. When situated on the side of a benefic, it is the *śubhakartarī*; however, if it occurs in the ascendant sign with malefics, it is called *pāpāhvaya* (named after the malefic).
If benefic planets are situated in the second house from the ascendant, it forms a very auspicious yoga, provided they are not aspected by malefics. || 8 ||

One born [under this configuration] shall be fortunate, happy, a treasury of virtues, steadfast, a righteous king, renowned, beloved by all, exceedingly handsome, a generous donor, dear to sovereigns,
possessed of beautiful limbs, fond of elaborate speech, eloquent, illustrious, and wealthy.
One should know [the mantras] here in the sequence of the quarters within the [sections] called Suveśī, Vāsī, and Ubhayacaryā. || 9 ||

One who acts unjustly, who reviles people, whose taste is destroyed, who has abandoned what is dear, who is wicked, deceitful, a slanderer of others, associated with the base, and excessively devoted to evil treatises—
such a person shall suffer ill-repute in the world, be troubled in mind, and be deprived of learning, wealth, and fortune.
And having been born in the inauspicious births, he proceeds through the stages in the sequence of the practices known as both [the auspicious and the inauspicious]. || 10 ||
One born in the Śubhakartari yoga becomes a long-lived person, free from fear, disease, and enemies; he possesses a sacrificial fire, is wealthy, and is endowed with prosperity.
Conversely, one born in the Niḥsva yoga is indigent, impure, devoid of happiness, wife, and children, and is physically impaired.
For one who commits evil deeds, existence will lead to a short lifespan. || 11 ||
Possessing proper conduct, intent on the Dharma, serene, and endowed with good fortune, he is honored by kings;
gentle by nature and speaking with a smile.
One born in Amala Yoga shall become wealthy. || 12 ||

In the case of a "suśubha" [house], such as the first house for one who performs auspicious deeds, or a "vesyā" [prostitute] house, and so forth, the results should be understood according to the sequence of auspicious planets; with malefic planets, the result is the opposite. (13)

If the Sun, Moon, and Ascendant are in odd signs at birth, it is a "Mahābhāgya" (Great Fortune) yoga for a male; for females, it occurs by the reverse of this. It is called "Kesarī" when the Moon is in a quadrant from Jupiter.
However, if the Moon is situated in the eighth or sixth house from Jupiter, it is a "Śakaṭa" (Cart) yoga; but if Jupiter is in a quadrant from the Ascendant, that [Śakaṭa] does not exist.
When the Moon is in a quadrant or similar house from the Sun, the well-known yogas called Adhama (inferior), Sama (neutral), and Variṣṭha (excellent) are formed. 14.
Born into great fortune, a source of delight to all eyes, generous, renowned, a sovereign of the earth, pure, and possessing a lifespan of eighty years—
one who, in this yoga, is endowed with wealth, excellent limbs, and auspiciousness for his wives.
Having practiced virtuous conduct, she attained auspiciousness through her sons and grandsons for a long time. || 15 ||
Like a lion, he is the destroyer of the host of enemies; possessing mature speech in the assembly, he conducts himself like a king.
Long-lived and of far-reaching fame, with a sharp intellect, he triumphs through his splendor in the Kesari-yoga.
Falling away from fortune here and there, he attains all good fortune again and again;
though unknown in the world, he has reached an unavoidable internal thorn, like a cart with a broken axle.
In the yogas named Kaṣṭa, Madhyama, and Vara, there is wealth, vehicles, fame, happiness, and prosperity;
likewise, there are the fruits resulting from knowledge, intellect, discipline, skill, learning, renunciation, and enjoyment. (18)

If the Moon is with eight planets and all the benefics are in the houses of increase from the ascendant, the yoga is called *Vyomni-mala*; it is also formed from the ascendant when benefics are so placed.
Furthermore, if the lord of the birth sign is conjoined with the lord of the ascendant and situated in a quadrant in the house of an exalted friend, [the yoga is formed].
If someone here observes the ascendant (lagna), there will be a powerful and abundant yoga.
One would always remain in one's own home with abundant wealth upon the earth; one would become a lord of the land, pure, wealthy, endowed with sons, fame, and prosperity, ethical, illustrious,
born of excellent yogas, honored by the best of kings, and renowned.
Adorned with garments and ornaments of his own choosing, possessing auspicious speech, he shall be the sovereign, the most excellent of all.
If all five, six, or seven auspicious planets are situated in a row in the houses of death, the sixth, the twelfth, and so forth, they are considered inauspicious here; however,
this is not the case if both Venus and the Lord of Fortune (Jupiter) are in their own signs, in their exaltation, or conjoined with a trine or a kendrāṣṭama (an angle or a quadrant).
Then, when the moon was in such a state and Jupiter was aspected by Venus, there was one named Lakṣmī. || 21 ||

One born in the yoga called Sumālā is an official over people, praised by kings, an enjoyer of pleasures, a donor, and a performer of others' tasks; he is dear to his kinsmen, endowed with virtuous sons and a wife, and possesses great fortitude. (22)

One born under the *Aśubhamālikā* yoga will follow an evil path, be miserable, a slayer of others, and ungrateful; he will be cowardly, devoid of devotion to the gods and Brahmins, censured by the world, and fond of quarreling. (23)
Always sporting with a woman of auspicious character, free from disease, wealthy, and radiant, he becomes an abode of the grace of Mahālakṣmī who well protects his kinsmen;
he travels in an excellent palanquin, mounted upon horses and elephants.
He is the bringer of joy to the worlds, the most excellent of kings, a donor, and the source of prosperity. || 24 ||
With beautiful limbs, a praiseworthy lineage, a friend to kings, and a son of virtuous qualities; with a lotus-like face, praised by the world, he shines forth, arisen from union with Gaurī. 25.

When Venus, Jupiter, and Mercury are situated in the angles (kendras), the trines (koṇas), or the second house, and when Jupiter is endowed with strength in its own sign, an exaltation, or a friendly house, Sarasvatī is attained. (26)
This wise man is proficient in the sciences of drama, prose, poetry, prosody, and rhetoric; he has reached the further shore of the meaning of the treatises on the composition of poetic works;
having pervaded the three worlds with his fame, he is exceedingly wealthy and accompanied by his wife and sons.
He may be born from a union with Sarasvatī, honored by the best of kings, and fortunate. || 27 ||
If the lord of the ascendant, the Sun, and the Moon occupy angles or trines,
and have not entered their exaltations, own signs, or the houses of their friends,
the Śrīkaṇṭha yoga occurs; likewise, if Venus, Jupiter, and Mercury are so situated, it is the Śrīnātha yoga.
If [the sequence] begins with Vāgīśa, Ātman, Pasu, and Sūryaja, then it is the Vairiñci yoga. || 28 ||

Adorned with rudrākṣa beads, his complexion white with sacred ash, that great-souled one meditates constantly on Śiva within himself; firmly restrained by the vows of Śiva and initiated into the Shaiva discipline,
he benefits the virtuous and harbors no malice toward the doctrines of others.
Radiant and delighted by the worship of Śiva, he was born from the yoga of Śrīkaṇṭha. || 29 ||
Prosperous, skilled in the art of charming and eloquent speech, marked by the sign of Nārāyaṇa,
and constantly reciting beautiful verses inscribed with His name before virtuous people;
with a serene countenance in honoring His devotees, he is endowed with a good wife and son.
He is beloved by the eyes of all, exceedingly fortunate, and born from the yoga of the Lord of Śrī. || 30 ||

Devoted to the knowledge of Brahman, possessed of great wisdom, preeminent in the Vedas, virtuous, and joyful, he does not deviate from the Vedic path; surrounded by a renowned multitude of disciples,
gentle in speech, with abundant wealth, wife, and sons, he blazes with the splendor of true Brahmanic luster.
The king of the Natas was Rghayu, who had conquered his senses and was born from the yoga of Brahmā. || 31 ||

The sixty-six yogas arising from the lords of the houses beginning with the ascendant up to the eleventh house of two birds situated in mutual houses have been described by people in their respective order; thirty [yogas] arising from the lords of the twelfth, sixth, and eighth houses are declared as "misery" (dainya).
Eight [types] of Śauryapati are declared to be wicked, while the remaining ones are remembered as being called "Great" (Mahā). || 32 ||
One born under Khala becomes a fool, a slanderer, constantly committing evil deeds, and perpetually tormented by rivals;
he speaks cruelly, is born of wretchedness, possesses a fickle mind, and his efforts in undertakings are severed.
Yet, even such a person may at times attain all-encompassing fortune.
And sometimes there is gentle speech such as this regarding inauspicious matters like poverty, suffering, and so forth. (33)

In the Mahākhyā yoga, the lord is a wealthy man whose abode is adorned with auspicious side-glances; he wears variegated garments and golden ornaments, possesses vehicles, wealth, and sons, and is cognizant of the pleasure derived from the great respect of kings.
If the lord of the sign occupied by the lord of the ascendant or the lord of the seventh house is situated in its own exaltation or own sign within the four angular houses (kendras),
that configuration is likewise celebrated as *Kahala*.
If the lord of the ascendant attains the seventh house, it is called Parvata.

Born from the yoga of Parvata, he is a lord of the earth who is wealthy, noble, wise, serene, a bringer of security, born of a noble lineage, honored by men, steadfast, noble, happy, and a performer of stable deeds. || 36 ||

When two planets, presiding over the houses of Dharma (the ninth) and Karma (the tenth), are conjoined and have attained a state of exaltation, that is likewise called Rājayoga here; Śaṅkha says it occurs when there is a conjunction in a quadrant or a trine.
Accompanied by the sounding of kettledrums and conchs, with an umbrella held aloft by soft silk ribbons,

and together with elephants, horses, palanquins, and other such conveyances, the protector of the earth— having commenced his journey from Magadha— shall become a king, entreated by virtuous men whose hands are adorned with various kinds of ornaments.
In the conjunction of Svāti and Śaṅkha, one will be filled with the perfection of enjoyments involving many excellent women. || 38 ||
The *saṃkhyāyoga* consists of seven [planets] situated in seven [asterisms], while the *vallakī*, *dāma*, and *pāśa* yogas decrease by one [asterism].
The *kedāra* is called the *śūla-yoga*, as are the *yuga* and *gola*; these, along with others previously mentioned, are excluded. (39)

One born under Vīṇā-yoga is fond of dance and song, seeks wealth, is generous with a cord (dāman), and is helpful toward prosperity; under Pāśa, one is an enjoyer of pleasures, a kinsman of noble character and purpose; and under the one called Kedāra, one is intent upon the field of auspicious agriculture. || 40 ||

In the Śūla yoga, one will be violent, prone to anger, poor, a heretic, and destitute of wealth; in the Yuga yoga, one is penniless, sinful, associated with barbarians, an inferior artisan, and born dull-witted with a short lifespan. (41)
If the benefic planets are situated in the seventh, sixth, or eighth houses from the Moon, or likewise situated from the Ascendant, there is an Adhiyoga;
the native will respectively become a leader, a minister, or a king—renowned, illustrious, long-lived, and wise.
One born in Adhiyoga becomes a lord of men, possessing stable wealth and nourishing many kinsmen;
by this yoga, enemies are utterly defeated, and one attains long life and renown. (43)

When the planets are conjoined with or aspected by benefics, their lords are situated in auspicious houses, and they are luminous, occupying their exaltations or own signs starting from the ascendant, twelve yogas arise in succession; their names are Amara, Dhenu, Śaurya, Jaladhi, Chatra, Astra, Kama, Asura, Vīra, Vaidya, Sārtha, and Nidhi. These are the twelve yogas. If the Moon is in the ascendant, the Sun is in the second house, Mars in the third, Mercury in the fourth, Jupiter in the fifth, Venus in the sixth, Saturn in the seventh, Rahu in the eighth, Ketu in the ninth, and the Sun again in the tenth, this is the *Amara* yoga. The native born in this yoga becomes a king. If the Moon is in the ascendant, the Sun in the second, Mars in the third, Mercury in the fourth, Jupiter in the fifth, Venus in the sixth, Saturn in the seventh, Rahu in the eighth, Ketu in the ninth, and the Sun in the tenth, this is the *Dhenu* yoga. The native born in this yoga becomes a wealthy man. If the Moon is in the ascendant, the Sun in the second, Mars in the third, Mercury in the fourth, Jupiter in the fifth, Venus in the sixth, Saturn in the seventh, Rahu in the eighth, Ketu in the ninth, and the Sun in the tenth, this is the *Śaurya* yoga. The native born in this yoga becomes a hero. If the Moon is in the ascendant, the Sun in the second, Mars in the third, Mercury in the fourth, Jupiter in the fifth, Venus in the sixth, Saturn in the seventh, Rahu in the eighth, Ketu in the ninth, and the Sun in the tenth, this is the *Jaladhi* yoga. The native born in this yoga becomes a lord of the earth. If the Moon is in the ascendant, the Sun in the second, Mars in the third, Mercury in the fourth, Jupiter in the fifth, Venus in the sixth, Saturn in the seventh, Rahu in the eighth, Ketu in the ninth, and the Sun in the tenth, this is the *Chatra* yoga. The native born in this yoga becomes a sovereign ruler. If the Moon is in the ascendant, the Sun in the second, Mars in the third, Mercury in the fourth, Jupiter in the fifth, Venus in the sixth, Saturn in the seventh, Rahu in the eighth, Ketu in the ninth, and the Sun in the tenth, this is the *Astra* yoga. The native born in this yoga becomes a great warrior. If the Moon is in the ascendant, the Sun in the second, Mars in the third, Mercury in the fourth, Jupiter in the fifth, Venus in the sixth, Saturn in the seventh, Rahu in the eighth, Ketu in the ninth, and the Sun in the tenth, this is the *Kama* yoga. The native born in this yoga becomes a master of love. If the Moon is in the ascendant, the Sun in the second, Mars in the third, Mercury in the fourth, Jupiter in the fifth, Venus in the sixth, Saturn in the seventh, Rahu in the eighth, Ketu in the ninth, and the Sun in the tenth, this is the *Asura* yoga. The native born in this yoga becomes a powerful demon-like leader. If the Moon is in the ascendant, the Sun in the second, Mars in the third, Mercury in the fourth, Jupiter in the fifth, Venus in the sixth, Saturn in the seventh, Rahu in the eighth, Ketu in the ninth, and the Sun in the tenth, this is the *Vīra* yoga. The native born in this yoga becomes a heroic king. If the Moon is in the ascendant, the Sun in the second, Mars in the third, Mercury in the fourth, Jupiter in the fifth, Venus in the sixth, Saturn in the seventh, Rahu in the eighth, Ketu in the ninth, and the Sun in the tenth, this is the *Vaidya* yoga. The native born in this yoga becomes a physician. If the Moon is in the ascendant, the Sun in the second, Mars in the third, Mercury in the fourth, Jupiter in the fifth, Venus in the sixth, Saturn in the seventh, Rahu in the eighth, Ketu in the ninth, and the Sun in the tenth, this is the *Sārtha* yoga. The native born in this yoga becomes a merchant leader. If the Moon is in the ascendant, the Sun in the second, Mars in the third, Mercury in the fourth, Jupiter in the fifth, Venus in the sixth, Saturn in the seventh, Rahu in the eighth, Ketu in the ninth, and the Sun in the tenth, this is the *Nidhi* yoga. The native born in this yoga becomes a possessor of hidden treasures. The above are the twelve yogas arising from the ascendant. The Moon in the ascendant, the Sun in the second, Mars in the third, Mercury in the fourth, Jupiter in the fifth, Venus in the sixth, Saturn in the seventh, Rahu in the eighth, Ketu in the ninth, and the Sun in the tenth constitute the *Amara* yoga. The native born in this yoga becomes a king. The Moon in the ascendant, the Sun in the second, Mars in the third, Mercury in the fourth, Jupiter in the fifth, Venus in the sixth, Saturn in the seventh, Rahu in the eighth, Ketu in the ninth, and the Sun in the tenth constitute the *Dhenu* yoga. The native born in this yoga becomes a wealthy man. The Moon in the ascendant, the Sun in the second, Mars in the third, Mercury in the fourth, Jupiter in the fifth, Venus in the sixth, Saturn in the seventh, Rahu in the eighth, Ketu in the ninth, and the Sun in the tenth constitute the *Śaurya* yoga. The native born in this yoga becomes a hero. The Moon in the ascendant, the Sun in the second, Mars in the third, Mercury in the fourth, Jupiter in the fifth, Venus in the sixth, Saturn in the seventh, Rahu in the eighth, Ketu in the ninth, and the Sun in the tenth constitute the *Jaladhi* yoga. The native born in this yoga becomes a lord of the earth. The Moon in the ascendant, the Sun in the second, Mars in the third, Mercury in the fourth, Jupiter in the fifth, Venus in the sixth, Saturn in the seventh, Rahu in the eighth, Ketu in the ninth, and the Sun in the tenth constitute the *Chatra* yoga. The native born in this yoga becomes a sovereign ruler. The Moon in the ascendant, the Sun in the second, Mars in the third, Mercury in the fourth, Jupiter in the fifth, Venus in the sixth, Saturn in the seventh, Rahu in the eighth, Ketu in the ninth, and the Sun in the tenth constitute the *Astra* yoga. The native born in this yoga becomes a great warrior. The Moon in the ascendant, the Sun in the second, Mars in the third, Mercury in the fourth, Jupiter in the fifth, Venus in the sixth, Saturn in the seventh, Rahu in the eighth, Ketu in the ninth, and the Sun in the tenth constitute the *Kama* yoga. The native born in this yoga becomes a master of love. The Moon in the ascendant, the Sun in the second, Mars in the third, Mercury in the fourth, Jupiter in the fifth, Venus in the sixth, Saturn in the seventh, Rahu in the eighth, Ketu in the ninth, and the Sun in the tenth constitute the *Asura* yoga. The native born in this yoga becomes a powerful demon-like leader. The Moon in the ascendant, the Sun in the second, Mars in the third, Mercury in the fourth, Jupiter in the fifth, Venus in the sixth, Saturn in the seventh, Rahu in the eighth, Ketu in the ninth, and the Sun in the tenth constitute the *Vīra* yoga. The native born in this yoga becomes a heroic king. The Moon in the ascendant, the Sun in the second, Mars in the third, Mercury in the fourth, Jupiter in the fifth, Venus in the sixth, Saturn in the seventh, Rahu in the eighth, Ketu in the ninth, and the Sun in the tenth constitute the *Vaidya* yoga. The native born in this yoga becomes a physician. The Moon in the ascendant, the Sun in the second, Mars in the third, Mercury in the fourth, Jupiter in the fifth, Venus in the sixth, Saturn in the seventh, Rahu in the eighth, Ketu in the ninth, and the Sun in the tenth constitute the *Sārtha* yoga. The native born in this yoga becomes a merchant leader. The Moon in the ascendant, the Sun in the second, Mars in the third, Mercury in the fourth, Jupiter in the fifth, Venus in the sixth, Saturn in the seventh, Rahu in the eighth, Ketu in the ninth, and the Sun in the tenth constitute the *Nidhi* yoga. The native born in this yoga becomes a possessor of hidden treasures. These are the twelve yogas arising from the ascendant.
Just as Bhāgya, Khyāti, Supārijāta, Musala, and Astajña have been proclaimed by those who know them. || 44 ||
One born of a cow becomes like the beautiful moon in the bright fortnight, increasing daily with lofty virtue;
he becomes a lord of people, possessed of fame, long-lived, and a treasury of prosperity. (45)

Abounding in food and drink, possessing all branches of knowledge, with a vast and flourishing family, and enriched with gold, jewels, wealth, and grain—he shines like the King of Kings (Kubera) through the gift of a cow. (46)
Praised by illustrious younger brothers, cherished, and endowed with honored valor, he becomes like Rāma—born of heroism, devoted to the affairs of state, and exceedingly famous. (47)

One born in the Ambu Yoga attains a residence resplendent with cattle, wealth, and grain; it is filled with kinsmen and possesses excellent women, jewels, garments, and ornaments; he reaches a highly honored position, the most supreme of all, and enjoys stable happiness through elephants, horses, vehicles, and cattle.
That king who is devoted to the service of the twice-born and the gods, and who constructs wells, water-stations, and roads; 48.

In the Chatra yoga, one becomes a minister of the sovereign, highly honored, wealthy, and possessed of sharp, flashing intelligence; he is illustrious, speaks auspiciously, is wise, and is the abode of the fortune that perpetuates the good luck of the world.

Having subdued the most powerful enemies by force, he is arrogant and engaged in cruel activities; his body is marked by wounds, he is prone to quarreling, and through the yoga of weapons, he possesses firm limbs. (50)
A son born of desire who turns away from the wives of others, who relies upon his own excellent wife, children, and kinsmen,
and who excels his father in auspicious virtues, attains exalted prosperity.

Devoted to his own interests, the slanderer destroys the affairs of others; being poor and stubborn, he is afflicted by a succession of misfortunes brought about by his own actions, a doer of evil deeds born from demonic associations. (52)
Having attained an eternal fortune characterized by the dense sound of waving chowries and musical instruments, and being honored by great men, he remains established on the path of Dharma;
he gratifies his ancestors, the gods, and the hosts of twice-born with various offerings dear to each.
One who possesses good conduct, upholds his own lineage, and has a kind heart arises through the conjunction of fortune. || 53 ||
Practicing hospitality esteemed by all the world, the king protects his subjects;
possessing the fortune of sons, friends, wealth, and a wife, he becomes famous and renowned throughout the world. (54)

Always endowed with auspiciousness, a lord of the earth, possessing accumulated stores of wealth, having a virtuous family, knowing how to appreciate and listen to noble stories, the progenitor of the Pārijāta tree, he is a source of welfare. || 55 ||

One who has acquired wealth with great difficulty, who is stingy, and whose nature is to spend even his modest fortune out of greed—such a base and fickle person, born of a commoner, attains heaven only in this state [of death]. 56.

When the lords of the houses are situated in malefic signs and are conjoined with or aspected by malefics, the states resulting from the respective houses are said to be, in order: *avayoga*, *niḥsva*, *mṛti*, *kuhū*,
*pāmara*, *harṣa*, *duṣkṛti*, *sarala*, *nirbhāgya*, and *duryogaka*.
O poor man, those twelve yogas have been declared by wise people to be stainless. || 57 ||

In this world, even during the Avayoga, one suffers from lack of renown, unbearable wretchedness, a very short lifespan, and contempt from the wicked; moreover, such a person will be joined with evil conduct, a deformed body, and an unstable livelihood. (58)
A community of wicked people is empty of pleasant speech and fruitless for its household; it has the eyes of evil reputation.
Devoid of wisdom, sons, learning, and wealth, with its riches stolen by enemies, such a group prevails only when one is destitute. (59)

In the yoga of death (mṛtiyoga), one becomes despised by enemies, deprived of innate qualities, mentally ashamed, robbed of strength and wealth, exhausted by the toil of unsuitable labors, and possessed of deformed characteristics. || 60 ||

Deprived of mother, vehicle, friends, happiness, ornaments, and kinsmen, and devoid of stability, he will resort to a place that is ruined; being devoted to a wicked woman, he will meet with misfortune during the *kuhu* conjunction.
In the Pāmarayoga, one leads a miserable life, speaks untruths, lacks discrimination, is deceitful, and remains childless even after losing children;
such a person is an atheist, associates with the wicked, and becomes a gluttonous consumer.

One born under Harṣaja is endowed with the fortune of enjoying happiness, possesses a firm body, and has conquered his enemies; he is fearful of sin, beloved by eminent and renowned people, and possesses wealth, splendor, friends, fame, and sons. || 63 ||

One should predict separation from one's own wife, a desire for the pleasure of another's wife, travel along difficult paths, suffering from urinary disorders and other secret ailments, oppression by the king, and grief due to the reproach of kinsmen when [the Moon] is in a malefic sign. (64)

One born under Sarala is long-lived, firm-minded, fearless, and illustrious; endowed with learning, sons, and wealth, he achieves success in his undertakings, conquers his enemies, remains stainless, and becomes renowned by name. 65.
He destroys fields, houses, and other property inherited from his father; devoid of righteousness, he reviles holy men and teachers;
wearing extremely tattered garments, he is impoverished and, through the conjunction of ill fortune, becomes a vessel for manifold suffering. (66)
Whatever action is performed through physical exertions shall become fruitless and bring lightness among people;
one who harms others will merely fill his own belly, remaining a constant traveler, born of ill fortune. (67)
In the yoga known as Daridra, one becomes burdened by debt, fierce, foremost among the poor, afflicted with ear disease, and devoid of brothers;
he is intent on improper acts, speaks of false sentiments, and becomes a servant to others.
With only slight expenditure, this [year] leads to an increase of abundant wealth and favor from all people;
one shall be happy, independent, of noble conduct, esteemed for virtues, and possessed of stainless prosperity. (69)
If the lords of the sixth, eighth, and twelfth houses are strong and occupy angles or trines,
while the lords of the ascendant, the tenth, the fourth, and the ninth are situated in the sixth, eighth, or twelfth houses,
they are devoid of strength and luster; in that case, it is known as a *duryoga* (an evil configuration).
When that [planet] is in its own division, the practitioner of yoga becomes a lord of wealth, a king, happy, and righteous. || 70 ||
Chapter Seven: Rājayoga (The Yoga of Kings)
If three or more planets are situated in their exaltations, placed in the angles (kendras), or in their own signs, one becomes a king; such is the established rule.
Even one born of another lineage may become a lord of the earth, endowed with elephants and horses, if five or more such planets are present. || 1 ||

If they are born in a royal lineage and not subject to an unfavorable planetary configuration (duryoga), they shall indeed become kings; for even those born from the rays of the sun shine forth if they are situated in angles (kendras) with three or more planets, joined with their own exaltations. Those born of royal descent thus become sovereigns.
But mortals born of other lineages may at times become kings equal to a sovereign. || 2 ||

If even a single planet, though situated in its sign of debilitation, is well-placed in a dignified position and aspected by a multitude of radiant planets, it makes one equal to a king; and if two or three planets do so,
they likewise produce a sovereign provided they are situated in auspicious signs and degrees.
And if many [people] likewise [speak], [they see] the king with his crown, parasol, and shimmering fly-whisks.
If two, three, or more planets are endowed with directional strength (digbala), one born in such a configuration will be a king in a royal lineage and possess a nature for victory;
provided that Saturn is excluded and five planets are endowed with directional strength.
Or he may become a king, even if born of another lineage. || 4 ||

When the Moon arises in the ninth division of a *gaṇottama* sign, or when it is in a *gaṇottama* itself, and is aspected by four planets excluding the Sun, then the king born shall be of low origin. || 5 ||
If the lord of the ascendant is in a quadrant during the period of the Sun (tapasi), occupying a Vargottama division, its own exaltation, or its own sign, and if Jupiter is likewise situated there,
[the native shall travel] upon the shoulder of an elephant in an exceedingly beautiful celestial chariot fashioned of gold.
It produces a king seated comfortably with a pair of shimmering chowries. || 6 ||

Even the moon, possessing a lofty nature, when observed by planets situated in high positions and radiant with a mass of white luster, produces a Niṣāda king; yet the moon, having abandoned its physical form and flashing with the full splendor of its digits, remains [supreme].
Situated in the four [houses], it produces a king endowed with elephants and horses.
If Venus, having risen in the asterism Aśvinī, is aspected by the lords of the planets (the Sun and Moon), it produces a king who has conquered his enemies; provided that,
having abandoned its sign of debilitation or exaltation, it is situated in the second house.
The lord of the ascendant, together with Venus, [placed] outside [the kendras], [indicates] a king. || 8 ||
If Mars is situated in Aries, Leo,

or Sagittarius at the ascendant and is aspected by a friendly planet, it makes one a lord of the earth; likewise, the lord of the tenth house situated in the ninth, and the lord of the ninth house [in the tenth], [bestows similar results].
The king who remains impartial is praised by his people.

If the Lord of a Thousand Rays (the Sun) is in the mid-arc, the Lord of Stars (the Moon) is in that very same [ascendant], and the Son of the Earth (Mars), endowed with great prowess, is in its exaltation at the ascendant;
if this occurs, the lord of the earth, having heard [of the danger], flees far away out of fear.
His enemies, scorched by the fire of his majesty, bow down only out of terror.

If the moon, beautified by a discus resembling nectar and a lotus stalk, is in its own Navāṃśa, and the lord of the earth is filled with many elephants, and the benefics are in the Kendras unassociated with malefics; || 11 ||
When three birds, free from the group of base enemies, have reached their own divisions, are endowed with strength, and are graced by the aspect of benefics;
and [the Moon] is white as cow's milk or a conch shell and marked by the deer.
He under whose birth [this occurs] shall be a lord of the earth who has conquered his enemies. || 12 ||
If a sky-walker endowed with strength, situated in the house of the rising sign, beholds the most excellent portion that has attained the friend of the *kumuda* grove (the Moon),
yet is not designated as malefic, [it is auspicious].
He becomes a lord of men, a sovereign of the whole earth, possessing an excellent body. || 13 ||
If at the time of birth, Jupiter, Mercury, Venus,
or the Moon— possessing pure bodies and clearly manifest networks of rays—
are aspected by or conjoined with their own friends, [the native will be fortunate].
They bring about great calamity for the king, which is like that of a god. || 14 ||
Venus was in the sign of Leo, the Sun’s child [Mercury] was in Gemini, and the Moon was full in its own exaltation;

he was gazed upon by the fierce-eyed one (Rahu) at the rising of Aries. When the sun entered [the sky], the king [ascended the throne] due to the movement of his army and the masses of dust it raised.
Agitated by the delusion of darkness, the lotus plant undergoes contraction. || 15 ||
When the benefics are situated in the seventh or ninth houses from the ascendant, or in the sixth or third houses,
having reached their own exaltation or their highest degree, or when they are in the angles;
and when the Moon, being in Cancer, has entered the Viśākhā nakṣatra, the king issues his command.
He under whose single umbrella this triple world stands is the lord of the Kṣatriyas.
If the full Moon is situated in a Vargottama division,
it makes one a lord of the earth, delightful with unprecedented fame,
such that he is obscured by the dust raised by the hoof-strikes of his multitude of horses.
The sun emulates the form of the moon at dawn.
If Jupiter and the Moon are situated in the ascendant at birth and are aspected by Venus,
that person becomes a king of incomparable fame.
If no one here were to go to a low state. || 18 ||

When the Moon is in a watery sign and a watery navāṃśa in the house of the body (the ascendant), occupying its own varga and being auspicious, it indeed causes inauspiciousness if devoid of kaṇṭakas; yet such a person becomes a king, a lord of many elephants. || 19 ||
Venus, when aspected by Jupiter, produces one born of royalty who becomes a king;
Jupiter, excluding the sign of Mṛga (Capricorn), makes one a king endowed with intoxicated elephants in the first house;
and the lord of the birth ascendant, joined with superior strength in a quadrant, makes one the lord of the earth.
When Mercury is aspected by Jupiter, even kings submit to his command.

Even a single planet situated in a high house and aspected by a friend makes one a king through the yoga of friendship, provided it is endowed with strength; when the Sun is in its own division and the Moon is in its own sign—
It ordains the lord of the region along with his horses and elephants. || 21 ||
If the Moon is in Pisces, full of light, and aspected by the planet Jupiter,
one becomes a chief among kings who brings joy to the world; if that full-light Moon is situated in its own exaltation— then [the result is even greater].
He who excels in renunciation, who is praised as the creator, the Lord of the World. || 22 ||
If the Moon is in its exaltation degree and aspected by Venus, the king shall be endowed with prosperity;
likewise, if it is situated thus and aspected by Jupiter, he shall protect the entire earth. (23)
If the three malefics are situated in the third, sixth, and eighth houses from the lord of the birth [ascendant],
Mars and Mercury are in the second house from the ascendant, and the Sun and Venus are in the fourth house;
and if Mars, Saturn, and Jupiter are joined with the tenth, eleventh, and ascendant houses respectively—
The knowers of that declare there to be four types of Rājayoga here.
If even one among the lords of the eleventh, ninth, and second houses is situated in a quadrant from the Moon or a planet, and Jupiter is the lord of the fifth and the eleventh,
one attains the status of an emperor with unbroken sovereignty.

If a planet situated in its sign of debilitation at birth is the lord of that sign, and the lord of its exaltation is the Moon or the Ascendant and occupies a quadrant (kendravarti), one shall become a righteous universal monarch (cakravartin). This is the "Nīcabhaṅga Rājayoga. (26)
If one planet is in its sign of debilitation while its lord is in exaltation in a quadrant,
that person becomes a universal monarch whose feet are worshipped by all kings.
If a planet situated in a certain sign is aspected by the lord of that sign, it makes one a famous ruler of the earth; how much more so if it is well-placed! (28)

If the lord of the house occupied by that [planet] is situated in its sign of debilitation from the ascendant or from the Moon, or if it is the lord of the exaltation sign of a planet located in debilitation,
yet stands in a quadrant (kendram), then the person shall be a sovereign emperor, possessed of complete wealth.
