He was most righteous, his feet were worshipped by other lords of the earth, and he possessed splendor, fame, and good fortune. || 29 ||

If both the lord of the depression sign (nīca) and the lord of the exaltation sign (ucca) for that [planet], or even just one of them, is situated in a quadrant (kendrastha), the native shall be a sovereign emperor honored by kings. || 30 ||

One born in the Jāmitra (seventh) house of Libra will be afflicted by poverty and deprived of his children. || 1 ||
The Sun, when situated in the second house, produces one who is free from ignorance, skilled in discipline, and possesses eloquent speech;
when in the third house, one endowed with strength, valor, and noble prosperity; and when in the fourth house, one who treats kinsmen as enemies;
while in the fifth house, he produces one who is a friend to his own people and possesses happiness and allies.
Service to a king is said to be a source of worldly existence and brings about the depletion of one's paternal wealth.

Deprived of happiness, wealth, longevity, and sons, though wise and renowned as a lord of the earth, he— possessing a wealth of virtues that leads to victory— is now an enemy dwelling within his own body.
Opposed to kings, possessing a wretched form, devoid of a wife, and humiliated, he has become a traveler on the path of death.
The Sun, situated in the eighth house, devoid of its aspect, destroys wealth, lifespan, and friends. || 3 ||
When the Sun is in Aries (Meṣa), the king is devoid of people; in Taurus (Vṛṣabha), he is a friend of his subjects; in Gemini (Mithuna), he is devoted to gods and Brahmins;
in Cancer (Karka), he possesses sons, vehicles, praise, intelligence, prosperity, strength, and fame; in Leo (Siṃha), he is a lord of the earth;
and when the Sun has reached Virgo (Kanyā), the ruler of men possesses abundant wealth and long life and is free from sorrow.
If [the Moon] is in the twelfth house, there will be enmity with one's father, impaired eyesight, and loss of wealth and sons. || 4 ||
If the Moon is in the ascendant, one becomes firm-bodied, long-lived, fearless, powerful, and prosperous; if it has entered its period of decline, the opposite occurs.
One becomes wealthy, learned, and possessed of sensual pleasures, yet deficient in speech.
Together with his brothers, women, and forces, he was exceedingly pitiable despite his valor. || 5 ||

When the Moon is in the *sutagata* (fifth house), one is happy, enjoys pleasures, is generous, possesses friends, vehicles, and fame, and has good sons; he is intelligent and his minister is mild-paced.
When it is in the *kṣata* (sixth house), one is short-lived; when in the *candra* (seventh house), one lacks intellect, suffers from stomach disease, and is subject to humiliation.
The Moon, beloved by young women and exceedingly handsome, is auspicious when seen during the Smara (Sthira) period. || 6 ||
In the year of death (Mṛti), one suffers from disease and has a short life; in the year of austerity (Tapas), one possesses auspicious dharma, a virtuous self, and sons;

in the year of victory (Jaya), undertakings are successful; in the year of the sky (Nabhas), one performs auspicious deeds and acts kindly toward the virtuous; and in the year of existence (Bhava), one becomes wise, long-lived, and endowed with wealth, sons, and servants.
In the twelfth house, one is hated, miserable, despised, and extremely lazy when the Moon is there. || 7 ||
When Mars is in the body [the first house], one has a wounded body, is exceedingly cruel, short-lived, and possesses wealth through violence;
in speech, he is mute, devoid of purpose, and resorts to wicked people.
When Mars is in the younger [houses], one possesses good qualities and wealth, is brave, invincible, happy, and has younger brothers.
He who has friends, enemies, mother, earth, abode of happiness, and vehicles. || 8 ||
The son of Visukha is mostly devoid of wealth; the son of Pisuna is of little intellect and possesses powerful passion;
the son of Śrīmān is famous and victorious over enemies;
the son of Ripu is unrighteous in his actions, afflicted by disease, addicted to women, and a liar.
If Mars is in the eighth house, one has a deformed body, is destitute, short-lived, and censured by people.
When Mars is in the ascendant, one becomes a friend of kings yet hateful to them, lacking a father, a destroyer of auspicious people, cruel toward the sovereign, a donor praised by eminent men,
endowed with wealth and happiness, free from sorrow, heroic, and of virtuous character.
One with deformed eyes is cruel, stingy, malicious, and base. || 10 ||

If Mercury is in the birth ascendant, one will have a long life, possess sweet and clever speech, understand the meaning of all scriptures, acquire wealth through the intellect, be a poet with pure eloquence; if in the tenth house, one will be an eater of sweet foods;
if in the eleventh house, one will be brave, live a full lifespan, be well-born, and endowed with effort; if in the seventh house, one will be possessed of wretchedness.
He is skilled in calculation, speaks flattering words, possesses good friends, and enjoys the fruits of his fields, grain, and wealth. || 11 ||
When [Saturn] is in the fifth house, one possesses the splendor of knowledge and happiness, is endowed with many sons, and is a practitioner of mantras;
yet he is prone to anger, engaged in disputes, hostile toward enemies, lazy, and harsh in speech.
When it is in the seventh house, one is wise, possesses a handsome appearance, and attains a wife along with wealth and full majesty.
When Mercury is in the eighth house, one becomes famous by name, long-lived, a sustainer of the family, a lord, and a leader of the staff (punisher).

If Venus is in the eleventh house, one will be proficient in the conduct and duties pertaining to learning, as well as in asceticism; he will be wise, highly eloquent, successful in his undertakings, endowed with the power of excellent knowledge, great intelligence, happiness, virtuous deeds, and truthfulness;
he will possess long life, be true to his word, enjoy abundant wealth and comfort, and be accompanied by servants.
He is wretched, devoid of knowledge, beset by humiliation, base, cruel, and lazy. || 13 ||
In the *lagna* (ascendant), one is handsome, virtuous, long-lived, fearless, and possesses two gods;
with his son, he is eloquent and has excellent food. In the second house (*dhana*), he is fair-faced and wealthy;
in the third (*sahaja*), he is wise, yet contemptuous and miserly. In the fourth (*sūrya*), he is a doer of evil and wicked-minded.
He will possess relatives, maternal friends, attendants, sons, women, happiness, grain, and wealth. || 14 ||

If Jupiter is in the sixth house, the king’s minister will be wise but afflicted by sons; he will be indolent yet a destroyer of enemies, skilled in spells and sorcery, possessed of a virtuous wife and sons,
exceedingly fortunate in youth, noble toward his father, and preeminent.
If Jupiter is in the eighth house, one lives in misery through service, is burdened by sins, yet possesses a long life.

If Jupiter is in the tenth house, one becomes famous as a minister, possesses auspicious wealth and sons, is eager for religious duties, well-conducted, highly renowned, very wealthy, and beloved by the king.
If Jupiter is in the eleventh house, one is a possessor of great wealth, free from fear, has few children, and travels in vehicles.
An object of hatred, one who utters words of reproach, one who is devoid of a son, O virtuous one, and a lazy servant—[these are the six]. || 16 ||
The planet Jupiter, when situated in the fifth house, bestows a son who is healthy, beloved by his eyes, happy, and long-lived;
when in the tenth house, it makes a poet endowed with manifold wealth;
and when in the eleventh house, it grants the fortune of the joy of knowledge, while in the sixth house, it makes one miserly and disliked.
Excellent vehicles, beautiful palaces, ornaments, garments, and perfumes [are found] in happiness. || 17 ||
One sees a king whose wealth is undiminished, a wise man with his son, one who has conquered enemies and possesses no wealth, one who is distressed and defiled by a young woman,
one with a virtuous wife who delights in unchaste women, and one who is wealthy yet intoxicated by his dancing wife.
Situated in the eighth house, it makes one long-lived, lord of the Ilā (earth), and wealthy.

In the auspicious month of Nabhasya, the lord shall be endowed with his wife, friends, and sons; he will attain royal fortune, possess a reputation for great fame, be engaged in a life of happiness with his companions,
be wealthy, take pleasure in other women, and experience manifold joys.
Bhṛgu (Venus), situated in the twelfth house, produces happiness from travel, wealth, and luster.
If Saturn is in its exaltation or its own house at the ascendant, one becomes equal to a protector of the earth;
if it is at the ascendant, one becomes the lord of a country or a city.
In other positions during childhood, one is indeed afflicted by suffering.
He is subject to the suffering of poverty, defiled, and indolent. || 20 ||
One who is averse to wealth and unrighteous in his purpose, yet later established in another region and endowed with vehicles, enjoyments, and wealth;
one of vast intellect and noble character, possessing the happiness of a wife and valor— [such a person is described].
The son of the Sun (Saturn) produces one who is lazy and dejected. || 21 ||

If [Mars] is in the house of the intellect (the fifth house), one will be miserable, separated from home, vehicle, and mother in childhood, afflicted by disease, wandering among kinsmen, devoid of knowledge, sons, wealth, and joy, deceitful, and dull-witted.
If it is in the house of the enemy (the sixth house), one is a great eater, endowed with riches, struck by enemies, audacious, and proud toward foes.
If the son of the Sun (Saturn) is situated in the house of desire (the seventh house), one is devoted to a wicked wife, devoid of wealth, a traveler on the road, and distressed. || 22 ||
When Saturn is situated in the eighth house, one becomes soiled, ill-fated, destitute,
fierce-minded, hungry, and insulted by friends.
When Mercury is auspicious, one is devoid of fortune, wealth, sons, and that [specific] dharma; yet he may be a minister to a king, wealthy, devoted to agriculture, brave, famous, long-lived,
possessed of stable prosperity and iron, brave, free from disease, and rich.
The son born in the Artha Dasa is shameless; in the Vyaya Dasa, he is physically impaired, foolish, and driven out by enemies. || 24 ||

If the Sun is in the ascendant, one has a short life, possesses wealth and power, suffers from diseases of the upper body, speaks with a hidden meaning, has facial ailments, is loathsome, yet is wealthy through royal favor.
If he is in the second house, one is prone to anger, happy, honorable, antagonistic toward brothers, and firm-minded. If he is in the third house, one is long-lived and wealthy.
A fool causes suffering in the home; one with few friends may sometimes be happy.
If Mercury is not present, one is speechless and childless; if Rahu is in the fifth house, the heart is hard;
if afflicted by malefic planets, there is pain in the stomach, enmity, and suffering from cruel influences. If Mars is there, one is wealthy but short-lived;
if Saturn, one is poor due to association with women and is distressed. If Mercury is there, one is independent but of little intelligence.
One born in a *randhra* (ninth) house will have a short lifespan, be impure in conduct, physically impaired, afflicted by wind-related diseases (*vātāmaya*), and have few offspring. || 26 ||

If Dharmastha is situated in the tenth house, one becomes a leader of a group, a city, or a village; he is unrighteous yet famous, has few sons, is intent on the affairs of others, devoid of virtuous deeds, and fearless.
If it is in the ninth house, one is prosperous, possesses many sons, enjoys long life, and suffers from ear ailments.
If [Saturn] is in the twelfth house, one delights in secret sins, incurs great expenditure, and is afflicted by water-born diseases.
If the Ascendant is occupied by [Mars], one becomes ungrateful, unhappy, treacherous, pale, displaced from one's position, physically impaired, and associated with the company of the wicked;
devoid of learning and wealth, possessed of base speech, and having evil vision.
Situated in the second house, it makes one devoted to the food of others at dawn.

When Ketu is in the third house, there is longevity, strength, wealth, fame, happiness from women and food, but the loss of siblings; and [there is] happiness from land, fields, vehicles, and one's mother, as well as one's birthplace.
It brings about destruction in happiness and causes one to dwell in another's house. || 29 ||
The loss of sons, the torment of the demon of abdominal disease, evil-mindedness, and the nature of wickedness within oneself—
these are the falls; whereas nobility, supreme virtue, steadfastness, and renown— these are the gains.
In the sixth [house], there is sovereignty, the subduing of enemies, and the attainment of desired goals.
In the seventh house, there is humiliation, unchaste women, excessive pride, disease, downfall, separation from one's own wife, loss of wealth and vital fluids,
short lifespan, separation from loved ones, and quarrels; and in the eighth house, [these same misfortunes].
A wound from a weapon is indeed an obstacle to all undertakings. || 31 ||
He declares that poverty is an engagement in evil, inauspicious, devoid of paternal fortune, and a reproach to noble people;
it is an obstacle to virtuous deeds, impurity, and a source of blameworthy actions.
Resplendent in the sky, his valor was exceedingly renowned. || 32 ||
In the matter of gain, [one may encounter] the accumulation of wealth with manifold virtues, excellent enjoyments, noble goods along with their implements, and the accomplishment of all aims;
or [one may encounter] hidden sin, base expenditure, and the destruction of wealth.
In the Riphā yoga, there is adverse movement and eye disease, as well as a fall.
Residing in a degree equal to the degrees of the rising asterism (ascendant), Rāhu bestows full results;
Ketu is declared here to be a giver of results like Mars and Saturn. || 34 ||
Those situated in the exact degree of a house bring about the full fruit of that house;
however, based on whether the degrees are deficient or excessive, an increase or decrease in the result should be declared. (35)
Chapter Nine:
The Results of the Zodiical Signs (Rāśiphala)

One born in the sign of Aries (Kriya-bha) has squinting eyes, weak knees, and is fierce; he is timid regarding water, eats little, is lustful, constantly on the move, fickle, speaks untruths, and has limbs marked by scars. || 1 ||
One with broad thighs and a broad face will be a practitioner of agriculture; he will experience happiness in his middle and later years, be beloved by women,
and be a singer, patient, enduring of hardships, and a possessor of cattle.
The *pṛṣa* [meter] arises from the *pṛṣṭha* [meter] when it is joined with an *aṇka* [syllable]. || 2 ||
With dark eyes and curly hair, devoted to playing with women and skilled in perceiving the gestures of others;
possessing a prominent nose and fond of song and dance, he always dwells within his own house in pairs. (3)

One born in Cancer is conquered by women, has a thick neck, possesses many friends, lives in many houses, is wealthy, short in stature, crooked, and quick-moving; he is endowed with intelligence, delights in water, and has few sons. (4)
He will have tawny eyes, a thick jaw, and a broad face; he will be proud and full of prowess.
He becomes angry over trivial matters, frequents forests and mountains, is obedient to his mother, and possesses a steady mind when facing lions. || 5 ||

With shoulders drooping and arms hanging down, he is honored for his wealth and houses belonging to others; he is devoted to truth, speaks kindly, has eyes languid with modesty, is fond of sexual pleasure, is a knower of the meaning of the scriptures, and has few sons through his wife.
In the sign of Libra (Tulā), one is of moving and slender limbs, has few children, is devoted to gods and the twice-born,
travels about, possesses two names, is tall, skillful in buying and selling, resolute, merciless, and a mediator in disputes.
One with rounded thighs and knees, broad eyes and chest, who becomes ill in childhood, is abandoned by his elders,
and is of cruel deeds, will seek the favor of the royal court.
His hands and feet are marked with lines resembling insects and lotuses. || 8 ||
One with a long face and neck, broad ears and nose, intent on action, hunchbacked in body, yet beloved by kings, endowed with boldness, eloquence, and generosity, is a destroyer of enemies.
The son of the Aśvins is to be won over by conciliation alone; he is a bestower of strength. || 9 ||
One born with a weak Jupiter is emaciated, endowed with courage, firm in his word, lazy, fond of women who are unapproachable due to age, a hypocrite in righteousness, fortunate, and a wanderer.
Afflicted by wind, born of a crocodile, and devoid of shame. || 10 ||

A hidden sinner, with a body like a jar, skilled in causing obstacles, enduring the road, possessing little wealth, greedy, seeking the interests of others, and subject to decline and increase— The provided text consists of a single Sanskrit verse fragment describing a specific type of person (likely a servant or messenger). Here is the translation: One who is a hidden sinner, whose body is like a water-jar, who is skillful at causing obstacles, capable of enduring the road, possessing little wealth, greedy, seeking the welfare of others, and subject to both decay and growth.
Ghaṭodbhava is one who possesses beloved fragrant flowers. || 11 ||
One who drinks water while standing, whose body is well-proportioned and symmetrical, who approaches his own wife, who enjoys wealth acquired through water,
and who is learned and grateful, overcomes his enemies.
Śubhekṣaṇa, endowed with good fortune, is in the twelfth house. || 12 ||
Having understood the results corresponding to the nature, location, form, and strength of the zodiac sign,
one should declare the result for the ascendant here by means of logical reasoning.
Whatever is to be said regarding the Moon in the ascendant, that very same thing should be declared [regarding the other planets]. || 13 ||
When Mercury is in its own sign or its exaltation, one becomes a lord of jewels,
praised by kings, an abode of honored prosperity,
and endowed with noble virtues— just like Vikramārka, who is ever victorious.
In policy, fame, valor, generosity, fortitude, and skill. || 14 ||
When a planet is situated in the *svāmīndra* (the lord of its own sign), through the favor of its ruler,
one attains noble status or even sovereignty, as well as a stable state of household life; at its own time, the world becomes new and the earth becomes fertile.
Furthermore, one gains great wisdom regarding people, as well as all lost objects. || 15 ||
A planet situated in a friendly sign brings success in one's undertakings through friends, new friendships,
and the fortune of virtuous sons, a wife, wealth, and grain.
This one bestows favor toward all people. || 16 ||
When Jupiter enters the house of an enemy, there is degradation, subsistence on the food of others, dwelling in another's mansion, poverty,
and constant affliction by enemies.
Even one who is affectionate toward him may incur extreme enmity. || 17 ||

They say that when a planet is in its sign of debilitation (nīca), there is a downward fall from one's own conduct, wretchedness, misconduct, and the incurrence of debt; furthermore, there is reliance on the base, residence in the land of Kīkaṭa, death, wandering on roads, and fruitless undertakings. (18)
If a planet has reached its state of debilitation (mauḍhya), it brings death before long, loss of wife, sons, and wealth, as well as futile quarrels, slander, and humiliation; indeed,
a planet situated in its own asterism does not produce such specific (inauspicious) results.
It produces either pleasure or pain, as before, yet remains unshakable. (19)
A planet, even if situated in its enemy's or debilitation sign, shall produce its exaltation results if it has attained its retrograde motion;
so too does a planet situated in a *vargottama* division.
The results for one situated in its own *kṣetra* are likewise as stated. || 20 ||
Chapter Ten:
Arising from the Consort (Kalatrabhava)

If the houses of the fifth and seventh [from the ascendant] are conjoined with or aspected by benefics, or from the ascendant or the Moon, there is auspiciousness for those two; otherwise, there is no success for them.
When malefics are situated in the twelfth, sixth, fourth, or eighth houses from Venus and the others, they do not cause harm.
Furthermore, if the seventh house (the house of the wife) is aspected by or conjoined with malefic planets, there is the death of the wife. || 1 ||

If the lord of the seventh house is in the fifth house, one is either devoid of a wife or childless; or if the lord of the ninth house is in the seventh or the eighth house, he certainly causes the destruction of the wife.
When the waning Moon is in the fifth house along with malefic planets in the twelfth, second, and first houses, one is without a wife and children.
One should predict the loss of wealth due to association with women for Madaga; and for Svarbhānu and Bhānu, one should predict [the same]. || 2 ||

If Venus is in the seventh house (the house of passion), there is death from a woman; if Mercury is in the seventh house while Jupiter is in its sign of debilitation, there is likewise destruction of the wife;
and if Saturn or Mars is situated in the seventh house, there is the death of the wife.
If Venus and Mercury are in the seventh house from the Moon-sign and Mars and Saturn are in the seventh house from the Sun-sign, the wife will be beautiful.

If Venus is situated in the seventh house, conjoined with or aspected by malefic planets, or is placed between malefics, in its sign of debilitation, in an enemy’s sign, or eclipsed by the light of the Sun, one should predict the loss of the wife. Alternatively,
if Venus is in the seventh house along with a malefic planet, or is in the fifth or ninth house, the person will have an incomplete marriage.
Or if Venus is joined with or aspected by the divisions (vargas) of Mars or Saturn, [the native] is devoted to another's wife. || 4 ||
If Mars and Saturn are in the seventh house, or Venus and the Moon are combust or without a son,
or if they are in the seventh house as eunuchs, there will be two wives.
If Jupiter and Venus occupy the Navamsha of a dual sign, that person shall have two wives.
Let them state the number of wives possessed by those who dwell in the sky, joined with those two.

If the lord of the seventh house (the dyūna) is strong and benefic, and the number of women [is determined] by the planets in the seventh house, their dignities, and the malefic planets along with the four [elements], then the wife will be virtuous and endowed with good sons;
even if he is a malefic planet, having gone to its own house, it brings auspiciousness to the wife and fulfills her desires.
Leaving the sixth, the twelfth, and the eighth houses, benefics situated in the houses of passion (the seventh) bring about happiness. || 6 ||
If the seventh house (the wife) and the second and fifth houses (wealth and desire) are aspected by malefic planets,
they are said to yield inauspicious results there, especially due to a cruel aspect;
likewise, even for the wife, there is a fault when there is intoxication or pride.
When it is aspected by benefics and joined with a benefic, the couple will be fortunate. || 7 ||

If the Moon, Venus, or Mars is in the seventh house, there will be a remarried husband or one who has no children; if malefics are in the seventh house in their signs of debilitation or inimical signs, [the native will suffer] from his wife—
The death of a man occurs in the eighth or the second house.
When the house of the wife from the ascendant is an even sign,
and the lord of that house likewise occupies it while being devoid of the Sun’s heat, and the lords of children and wife [are similarly situated].
But when it is endowed with vigor (vīrya), there is birth [of a son], along with a son and a wife. || 9 ||
If the lords of the house, wife, and expenditure are aspected by Jupiter and situated in the four corners (the trines),
there is gain of wealth and a wife from the lord of the wife's sign.
The benefics [in the seventh house] make the wife and children wealthy in happiness. || 10||
The birth of a wife occurs when the lord of the ascendant or the seventh house is situated in its own sign, a trine, or in a sign that is neither debilitated nor exalted;
and when the Moon is in its own sign within the Moon's Aṣṭavarga.
Likewise, [the birth] of the husband is called "kalatra-janma" (the birth of a wife). || 11 ||
For one situated in Kama, the Bhargava [Venus] indicates the Mrigashira asterism and the direction for his wife;
Venus is either in its own house or in the sign of its lord.
When it enters the trine, then there is marriage. || 12 ||

At the commencement of the *daśā* of whichever is stronger between Venus and the Moon— the lords of the house occupied by the wife and the house occupied by the husband—

The Eleventh Chapter:
The Birth Chart of Women (*Strījātaka*)
O beloved, whatever is capable of producing a male child, all that one should predict for women;
likewise, auspiciousness from the eighth house, sons from the ninth, physical beauty from the ascendant (lagna),
a husband from the seventh house, a fortunate state from the fourth house, association from the fifth house, and womanhood from the ninth house.
Among those, the benefic planets are givers of auspiciousness, while the malefic ones are givers of inauspiciousness; such is their lord.
If both the Sun and the Moon are situated in a mutual relationship (yugmagau) and aspected by benefics,
one possesses children, wealth, ornaments, and excellent character; however,
if they are in odd signs (ojagau) and associated with or aspected by malefics, one possesses a masculine nature.
She will be crooked-minded, uncontrollable, fierce toward her husband, and impoverished.
If the seventh house (the house of the wife) is conjoined with six signs and their respective degrees, the husband will possess splendor, fame, learning, and wealth;
if the opposite occurs, he will have a deformed body, be dull-witted, a gambler, and destitute, and there will be separation between the two.

Furthermore, if the planets of the fire element (Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn) are situated in the seventh house, she will become a widow; if they are mixed [with others], she will become a remarried woman.
When the lifespan is cruel, even if she is the slayer of her husband, the death of a virtuous woman occurs through her own [karma] regarding wealth. || 3 ||

If the Moon is situated in the fifth house from the Sun, or in Aries, Virgo, Leo, or Capricorn, there will be few children; if it is in a sign belonging to Saturn, Mars, or the Sun, or in the seventh house, there will be a wife who is unchaste.
Furthermore, if malefic planets occupy the fourth house, the native becomes a womanizer, especially if Saturn and Mars are involved.
If Venus is in the seventh house while both the Ascendant and the Moon are there, she is declared to be unchaste.

If a benefic planet is in the seventh house from the auspicious *kṣetra* (the fifth house), she possesses a beautiful gait and hips; if it is in the fourth house, she is auspicious; and even in the case of a connection with a benefic in the ascendant or the seventh house, she is a virtuous woman of excellent qualities.
If benefics are in the trines (*trikoṇa*), she is endowed with happiness, sons, wealth, and virtues.
If the planets are cruel, she will be barren or one whose children have died. || 5 ||

If the Moon is in the house of Mars, then according to the thirty-degree divisions (triṃśāṃśaka) beginning with that of Mars, the wife will respectively be: wicked, a servant, unchaste, virtuous and wealthy, deceitful, or corruptible.
If it is in the sign of Venus, she will have many defects, be the mistress of her husband, worthy of worship, and devoid of intelligence.
In the asterism of Jupiter, she is called Chhasavatī; she is neuter, virtuous, rich in qualities, and eager. || 6 ||
In the lunar mansion of Mṛgaśirā, she will be independent, a slayer of her husband, yet possessed of exceedingly great virtues; in Ārdrā, she is a skilled artisan of virtuous conduct;

in Punarvasu, she is rich in qualities and devoted to renunciation; in Puṣya, she is known for her supreme skill and is most virtuous. In Āśleṣā, she will be a slave attached to another; in Maghā, she is unchaste; and in Pūrvaphalgunī, she will be childless and destitute.
A wicked wife of low conduct, the consort of a king, who acts like a man and is attached to another.

This result is derived from the thirty-degree portions conjoined with the Moon and the Ascendant; one should thus contemplate it according to the variation in their respective strengths and weaknesses. (8)
The experts know that women born in the asterisms of Jyeṣṭhā, Ārdrā, Āśleṣā, Svāti, Śatabhiṣaj, Mūla, Kṛttikā, and Puṣya kill, respectively, their eldest brother, their mother, their father,
and their younger husband.
Whether she be barren, or a widow, or one whose sons have died, or abandoned by her beloved, or destitute; || 9 ||
If the lords of the Moon, the eighth house, and the ninth house are conjoined with benefics, situated in auspicious houses, radiant, and honored,
she will be skilled in meritorious deeds toward her kin, endowed with beauty and fortune,
pleasing to her husband, possessed of excellent sons, and virtuous in character.
She shines as highly auspicious as long as her son, the sun, remains in the eighth house, which is rich in excellence.
If the Moon is in a female sign and not in its house of exaltation, and is aspected by Mars, the menses that arise will surely yield the fruit of conception; otherwise, they are fruitless.
However, if the Moon is aspected by Jupiter while situated in its own house of exaltation, a man should perform the act of procreation.
At a time that is not to be abandoned, joined with an abundance of auspiciousness, and distinguished by the occasion of a festival or similar event. || 11 ||
Twelfth Chapter:
The Results of the Fifth House (Putrabhāva)
If the lords of the fifth house,

the ascendant, and the ninth house are well-placed, and the lord of the fifth house is in its own sign (sutarkṣa) joined with or aspected by benefics; and if the lords of the ascendant and the self (soul/ninth house) are mutually joined and aspect each other auspiciously.
If there is mutual movement in the fields, there is the accomplishment of a son. || 1 ||
When the fifth houses from the Ascendant, the Sun, and the Moon are occupied or aspected by malefic planets, or are neither occupied nor aspected by benefics;
and when the fifth houses and their lords are both malefic and benefic [in nature].
If they are situated in malefic houses, sons do not arise at all. || 2 ||

If the son [Saturn] is in its own sign and is malefic, one experiences the loss of children; if it is again with a malefic, there will be many sons. If it is in the house of a benefic and is strong, it bestows sons; however, if it is in the sign of Aries, Taurus, Virgo, Leo, or Scorpio, they know that sign as "the sign of few sons."
If that [planet] is situated in the fifth house from its own sign, one has few children; this occurs after some time. || 3 ||
When the Sun is situated in a minor sign (alpa-sutarkṣa) and Saturn is in the eighth house, Mars is in the ascendant, and Saturn, Mercury,
and Mars occupy the ascendant, the eighth, and the twelfth houses respectively; and when the Moon is in the eleventh house while the fifth house— occupied by Jupiter— is associated with a malefic.
If the ascendant is occupied by many planets, one becomes a father of sons after some time through diligent effort. || 4 ||
If the Sun is not combust and is joined with a favorable asterism while Mars or Venus is situated in the house of the Moon,
there is the attainment of a son in the second wife; or if Saturn is there,
one desires many sons, whereas if the Moon or Mercury is there, one has few children.
If Venus is in the house of the Moon, or similarly situated in the house of the lord of the fifth house, there will be many daughters.
If malefic planets occupy the tenth house from the ascendant,

and the Moon occupies the twelfth, eighth, fifth, or first houses, there is the destruction of the lineage. Furthermore, if malefic planets are situated in the fourth, seventh, fifth, and ninth houses, it results in the loss of one's position and honor.
Even when the Moon is in the fifth house and malefic planets are situated in the eighth, twelfth, and first houses. || 6 ||

If the Ascendant is a malefic sign, the lord of the Ascendant is situated in the fifth house, and the lord of the fifth house is in the tenth house while the Moon is devoid of strength, one is sonless; likewise,
if the lord of an odd-sign (masculine) asterism is in the fifth house and aspected by the Sun, [one is sonless].
If [the Moon] is in the seventh house, one will experience suffering from sons; if it is without a son, he will be childless. || 7 ||
If a planet is slow (mānda) in its own sign or in that of Mercury,
and is conjoined with or aspected by Saturn,
the native will have a son given to him; this applies when the lord of the ascendant or the lord of the seventh house is thus situated.
The lord of the fifth house is devoid of relationship and lacks strength. || 8 ||
When the lord of the fifth house is situated in a debilitated sign, an enemy's sign, or its fall, or is conjoined with the lords of the twelfth, sixth, or eighth houses,
the destruction of children is declared here by those who know the truth.
When the fifth house is aspected by benefics and the lord of the fifth house is situated in the fifth house; || 9 ||
When Mercury, Jupiter, Mars, and the Sun are situated anywhere within the male signs,
the sages declare that one will then have many sons.
[He attains] the state of being a good son through the power of the effort of the Lord of the Sūtras. || 10 ||
If the sign, degree, and lord of the ascendant are masculine, and are conjoined with or aspected by male planets, or if a male planet [is present], there is the birth of a male;
if they are feminine signs and degrees, and are conjoined with or aspected by female planets, [there is the birth of a female].
The birth of daughters occurs when the lord of the fifth house is in a female sign.
When the Sun and Venus are endowed with strength and situated in their own houses or divisions, or in signs of increase (upacaya) for men;
or when Mars and the Moon are so positioned for women, then conception occurs.
If the Navāṃśakas are moving in signs free from enemies,
or if they are likewise joined with the lord of the fifth house,
or if they occupy the fifth sign from Jupiter’s sign and so forth, [the result is] in the fifth house.
The number of sons is determined by the fruits. || 13 ||

When the sum of the true longitudes of Mercury, the Moon, and Mars occurs in an even sign and an even degree, they say there is "field-strength" (*kṣetrabala*) for women, which bestows sons; if it is mixed [i.e., an odd sign and even degree], the result comes through great effort.
When the sum of the true longitudes of the Sun, Venus, and Jupiter occurs in an odd sign and an odd degree, [the same applies].
For men, this seed-strength bestows a son; however, if it is mixed, one should declare the result to be mixed.
One should subtract the true moon, increased by five and multiplied by the *phuṭādi* [of the sun], from the true sun;

having added the lunar day (*tithi*) therein, if it is a bright fortnight, a son is obtained even without effort on that auspicious lunar day. In the dark fortnight, there is no son due to the strength of the lunar day; thus one should declare [the result] for both fortnights according to the power of the *tithi*.
On the new moon day, on a defective lunar day, and during the Viṣṭi karaṇa, a son born under a fixed (sthira) asterism would not survive. || 15 ||
If the *karaṇa* is *viṣṭi* or a fixed (*sthira*) one,
one should conquer the dark [forces] with the mantras of the *Puruṣasūkta*; on the sixth lunar day, the worship of Guha should be performed here.
One should indeed worship the Naga king on the fourth lunar day. || 16 ||
If it is the ninth lunar day, one should listen to the Rāmāyaṇa; if it is the eighth, the Śravaṇa-vrata;
and if it is the fourteenth, the worship of Rudra.
If it be the twelfth day, the gift of food is fully effective. || 17 ||
On the fifteenth day of the dark fortnight, after the tenth day, the ancestors are satisfied here with great effort;
likewise, during the three divisions of the fortnight, [one should worship] the King of Nagas.
And one should worship Skanda and Hari in due order. || 18 ||
If Putreśa (the lord of the fifth house) is situated in the sixth, the sign of debilitation, the eighth, the twelfth, or the sixth house, or likewise if it is situated in the fifth house itself,
one should declare that as the cause for the absence of a son; this is determined by the sign occupied by that planet.
One should declare the cause of offspring even by means of the aforementioned deities, trees, and animals.

A son [is not born] due to enmity between Śambhu and Suparṇa; nor from a father's curse, as in the case of Rāvaṇa; nor from the anger of a mother’s co-wife, as in the case of Indra; nor from mental defects; nor from the fault arising from a relative of one's own village, such as Vyāsa, Guha, or Hari, in the case of Kuja.
From the curse uttered by Bālaka due to the killing of a cat, and from the wrath of Śrī Viṣṇu, O Sage.

Due to her enmity toward her elders, Brahmins, and preceptors— whom the gods hold dear through tradition— and from cutting down fruit-bearing trees, as well as from cutting flowering trees when Venus was in the position of Jupiter,
and due to the fault of having committed adultery with a cowherd, she [became] desirous of Yakṣīs and other such beings.
In his anger at the destruction of the Aśvattha tree, the Lord of the Ancestors was joined by the pretas, piśācas, and other such beings. || 21 ||

If Rāhu is in the fifth house conjoined with the lord of the fifth, one should predict death due to the curse of a serpent; likewise, if Ketu is there due to the curse of a Brāhmaṇa, or Gulika is there, one should predict death from the curse of a ghost.
If Venus and the Moon are conjoined with Gulika in the fifth house, they say there will be the loss of the wife and cattle.
Or if the Jīva or Śikhī is in the fourth house from the lord of the year, there will be a son born of a Brāhmaṇa woman.
For thus do those who know [astrology] declare that at the time of his birth, there was misfortune accumulated by him through the karma of many previous lives;
[this is remedied] by the recitation of mantras, giving, and auspicious rites prescribed for each respective planet.
May he proclaim here the pacification of those faults for the sake of the success of his son. || 23 ||
Bathing at Setu, the chanting of sacred stories,
worship of Śambhu and the Lord of Śrī, virtuous vows, charity, ancestral rites, and the consecration of Karanja trees and serpents— [these are the means].
One should perform [these rites] with these [mantras]; by doing so, one shall attain peace.

If the lord of the fifth house is in its own period or sub-period during the periods or sub-periods of the lords of the ascendant, the eighth, or the fifth house; or if it aspects the fifth house or is situated in the fifth house; or if it is in the sign occupied by the lord of the fifth house, or in a *yamakaṇṭaka* or *ṛkṣa* configuration, there is the attainment of a son.
If Jupiter is in its own sign, or in its exaltation, or in its own Navamsha, there is the attainment of a son. || 25 ||
If the lord of the ascendant comes into conjunction with the lord of the fifth house by its own motion while in its exaltation or its own sign,
then there shall be the acquisition of a son through the lord of the ascendant.
Or it goes to the constellation of the son (Puṣya), or to the constellation of the lord of wisdom (Jyeṣṭhā). || 26 ||

By bringing together the periods known as *mahādaśās* through the conjunction of the lords of the ascendant, the self, and the son, the birth of a son occurs during the sub-periods (*apahāra*) of the planet situated in the fifth house, the planet aspecting it, and its lord. (27)

Or else, there is the attainment of a son during the major period (daśā) of the lord of the fifth house, or of the lords of the signs and degrees occupied by that [fifth] house, provided they possess strength; or it may occur during the sub-period (apahāra) of such a planet. || 28 ||
If Jupiter is in the third, eleventh, or ninth house from the ascendant, there will be the birth of sons for men;
furthermore, according to another treatise, [this is calculated] from the time of birth.
The wise one should discern the characteristic of the continuity of existence.
When Jupiter attains a clear conjunction with, or occupies a trine from, both the lord of the birth asterism and the lord of the asterism of prosperity, the birth of a son occurs. (30)
When the lord of the day, by the power of its motion, arrives at the third sign from the *niṣeka-lagna* (conception ascendant),
or when the Sun is in a trine from the *ādhāna-lagna* (impregnation ascendant), one should predict the birth of men.
The birth [of the child] should be predicted from the lord of the fifth house from the ascendant at conception, or from the ninth house, or by the power of merit (puṇya);
provided there is a yoga with a benefic aspect upon the ascendant at conception.
The man shall be long-lived and endowed with sovereignty. || 32 ||
At that time, in the twelfth part of the moon [from the sun], or in the same number of signs from Aries,
or in the same number of signs from that [position], the wise man should state the birth-moon.

One should declare that the fruit is equal to that of birth during the times of questioning, the son’s acceptance [of initiation], the bringing forward [of the bride], the giving away of the daughter, the onset of the first menses, and also at the time of the *ādhāna* ceremony; and this should be determined from the birth ascendant (*janmalagna*).
Thirteenth Chapter:
The House of Longevity (Āyurbhāva)
When a prince has been born, the noble ones must first consider his lifespan, and thereafter his future fruits; likewise,
when one is established in virtue, these matters should be investigated.
Indeed, the qualities are established as equal by those who know the characteristics. || 1 ||
Some [astrologers] say the time of death is determined by the ascendant at the moment of conception; others, by the rising of the head [at birth]; and still others, by the falling to the ground.
Those who know the *horā* declare the time of separation from the body to be determined by the ascendant of the mind and the womb. (2)
Until twelve years have passed since birth in a human womb,
it is impossible for either the mother or the father to determine the lifespan of one who has committed sinful deeds.
The child comes to destruction by means of the childhood-seizing spirits. || 3 ||
In the first four [years], by the sins committed by his mother; in the middle [four], by the mass of evils acquired by his father;
and in the final four years, the child [is purified].
Through one's own faults, one meets with destruction.
O Father, for the sake of pacifying that defect, perform throughout each birth a life-prolonging rite for twelve years, preceded by recitation and fire-offerings.
One should refine the fool by means of medical treatment and the like alone. || 5 ||
They say that for men, there are eight signs of untimely death (*bālāriṣṭa*) at the beginning, twenty signs of death through yoga (*yogāriṣṭa*),
and a short life up to thirty-two years, while the middle lifespan is [longer].
And their full lifespan extends to one hundred years, beginning from seventy.
The lifespan of humans is indeed one hundred years, which is divided into three parts:
short, medium, and long; this is the consensus of all. (7)

Death may occur on the day of death, or during the time of a disease, poison, or a fatal *ghaṭī*. Furthermore, in the asterism of Tiṣya (Puṣya) or Ambu (Śatabhiṣaj), one shall kill the father, mother, son, or maternal uncle according to the sequence of the quarters; likewise, in the asterism of Tvaṣṭṛ (Citrā).
In the asterism of Mūla, there is the destruction of the paternal and maternal lineages, and in its final quarter, the destruction of wealth.
If this result is scattered in the Sarpa [Dasa] and the ascendant has no auspicious connection, it is not favorable. || 8 ||
If a birth occurs at the junction of a sign aspected by malefic planets, destruction is certain immediately;

at the *gaṇḍānta*, there is the death of the child or the killing of the father and mother. If born at any of the four junctions (*sandhi*) conjoined with or aspected by malefics, death shall occur—even if he lives, he will become a king.

If the Moon is situated in the eighth house from the Ascendant (Mṛtyu-bhāva), death occurs; likewise, if it is in the eighth house from the Moon, or if the Moon is in a quadrant or the eighth house, death occurs. || 9 ||
The hero of the world, the knower of the supreme, perceived the lunar form as a painting on a wall in the world of fortune; he considered the kingdoms of the parrots to be destined for death.
The [digits] of the moon [are determined] by the number of syllables in the names of Aries and the other signs. || 10 ||
O Rudra, the cow is the portion for Dāna through the mouth;
Bhāgyā is the portion for Bhanu through the hoof; the wife is the portion for Gotra through the claw;
and the daughter is always the portion for Mṛtyu through the sequence.
Those born in those [signs] beginning with Aries have their life-span exhausted. || 11 ||
If malefic planets occupy the eighth or the angles (kendras), or if they are situated in the ascendant and the eighth house, or if the Moon is between malefics in the ascendant or the seventh house;

or if the Moon is weak and placed in the twelfth, eighth, or sixth house; or if the waning Moon is with malefics occupying the first, tenth, fourth, or fifth houses; or if malefics occupy the eighth, seventh, or second houses—[in such cases, death occurs].
Death would occur quickly in the ascendant if there are no auspicious planets [in the angles] with either conjunction or aspect. || 12 ||

If the lord of the birth ascendant or the lord of the year’s ascendant is situated in a malefic house and is weak, it causes death within as many years as there are signs from that [ascendant]; likewise, the lord of the drekkāṇa causes death within those many months; the lord of the navāṃśa within those many days. If there are many combinations of two, three, or more [such factors], [death occurs sooner].
One should not speak of misfortune for the child based on malefic planets situated in the fifth or eighth houses without having first performed the *āloca* (examination).
From the mutual positions of the Ascendant and the Moon, and also from those of their respective lords; from the mutual positions of the Lord of the Ascendant and the Lord of the Eighth House;

and also from the decans (drekkāṇa), their own navāṃśas, and their mutual dvādaśāṃśas—in this sequence, longevity is determined as long, medium, or short by means of the moving, fixed, and dual signs, respectively. Furthermore, in the case of a movable sign, it is by the degrees of the moving part; in a fixed sign, by the degrees of the fixed part.
One should predict through planets that move in pairs, those that are stationary, those that belong to both categories, those that remain fixed, and those that travel through two bodies.

Benefic planets occupying the ascendant, the tenth house, and the other houses in order produce long, medium, and short lifespans respectively; likewise, malefic planets situated in the eighth house produce the same results in reverse. Furthermore, through friendship between the lord of the birth sign and the lord of the eighth house, or between the lord of the ascendant and the lord of the eighth house, these results are modified.
If the luminous ascendant is even, it bestows long life; if odd, short life; and if neutral, middling life. || 15 ||
If the lord of the ascendant, the lord of the navāṃśa of the ascendant,
the lord of the birth [sign],
and the lord of the navāṃśa of the birth [sign] are endowed with strength along with the lords of their respective eighth houses;
They shall be long-lived; otherwise, it is the opposite.

If the lord of the eighth house is exceedingly stronger than the lord of the ascendant, situated in a quadrant (kendr), and is in the eighth, twelfth, or sixth house from the eighth house, and is conjoined with malefic planets,
his lifespan will be short; or else, it will be middling.
Through the power of exertion, daring, and overcoming adversity, one attains the supreme lifespan. || 17 ||
A man’s life perishes in the first revolution of Saturn during a short lifespan; if he possesses a medium or long lifespan, his death occurs in the second;
and in the third, his departure [from life] is determined by the true positions of Saturn, Jupiter, the Sun, and the Moon.
The wise one, having determined it with certainty, declares that even the enjoyment of a period may be fraught with suffering. || 18 ||

When the lord of the ascendant is sinful, its luster eclipsed by the Sun, situated in its sign of debilitation or an enemy's sign, and has come to occupy an inauspicious house by virtue of its transits (gocara),
or if there is such a conjunction with the Moon in the first house, they say it brings death for embodied beings.
One should also declare [the results] from the ninth-part (navāṃśa), the decan (drekkāṇa), and the moon-ascendant (śiśirakaralagna). || 19 ||
When the Moon, the lord of the sign occupied by it, and the lord of the ascendant— these three—
are endowed with superior qualities and joined with the aspect of benefic planets;
They describe that time as one characterized by an abundance of virtues.
The lord of the ascendant, being exceedingly strong, not aspected by malefic planets, situated in a quadrant, and being gazed upon by benefic planets,
bestows a long life, setting aside death.
Together with many virtues and the most exalted royal splendor.
Surpassing all others in power, with a shimmering web of rays,
the minister of the King of Gods, standing at the moment of transition, alone can pacify many most difficult evils.
Just as one offers salutation to Cakradhara through devotion and application, so too [should one offer salutation]. || 22 ||
When situated in the triplicity, trine, or kendras of the sign of the Sun, the Moon, or Jupiter, or within their respective navāṃśas, the Moon—
increasing in strength like a non-heating sun— performs auspicious deeds and destroys all defects.
He whose malefic planets are not situated in the ascendant, the trines, or the eighth house, and whose lord of the ascendant and Jupiter are both placed in the quadrants—
having performed highly meritorious deeds, he shall enjoy various pleasures.
He shall live for a hundred years, freed from disease. || 24 ||
Then, from the states proclaimed by Ścīpati, from the eightfold divisions (aṣṭavarga), from the periods of the Kālacakra, and from the various types of lunar mansions' periods—
by means of a calculation rendered perfectly clear through the application of the obtained statements—
May the wise one speak with extensive examination. || 25 ||
Chapter Fourteen: Determination of Diseases (Roganirṇaya)

One should predict even the anxiety regarding disease by means of planets situated in the house of illness, or those placed in the twelfth or eighth houses, or by the lord of the house of illness, or by those associated with them, according to the concurrence of two, three, or more such factors. || 1 ||

The Sun indicates diseases of bile, fever, heat, bodily burning, epilepsy, and ailments of the heart and chest; it also signifies pain in the eyes, fear of enemies, skin disorders, decay of the bones,
and danger from fire, weapons, poison, enemies, wife, children, and quadrupeds.
Fear has become a source of terror for thieves, kings, Dharmadeva, Śeṣanāga, and Śiva. || 2 ||

The Moon [causes] sleep, laziness, phlegm, diarrhea, pustules, and cold fever; Śṛṅgī [causes] injury from water-lilies, loss of appetite, and sluggish digestion; Abja [causes] women, pain, and jaundice; Udaka [causes] mental peace; and Bālagraha [causes] blood disorders and fear.
One should declare fear from Durgas, Kinnaras, Dharmadevas, serpents, and Yakṣas. || 3 ||
It brings about thirst, hemorrhage, fever caused by the provocation of *pitta*, loss of appetite, poisoning, weapons, consumption, leprosy, eye diseases,
abdominal tumors, epilepsy, injury to the marrow, harshness, heat, bodily fractures,
affliction from kings, enemies, and thieves, and conflict with one's own children and friends.
The son of the Earth (Mars) [removes] the fear of Rākṣasas, Gandharvas, and terrible Grahas, as well as diseases of the upper body. || 4 ||

Delusion, harsh speech, diseases of the eyes, nose, and throat, fever born of bile, phlegm, and wind, poison, skin disorders, jaundice, bad dreams, scabies, burns from fire, roughness, imprisonment, and exhaustion— [all these are destroyed].
Even when planets are situated in the Gandharva, Kṣiti, or Harmya houses, the wise one declares that they cause affliction. || 5 ||
[It cures] diseases born of *gulma*, intestinal disorders, fever, grief, delusion, and *kapha*; ailments such as earache and fainting;
afflictions arising from the displeasure of deities, sacred sites, or treasures, or from the curses of lords of the earth;
and diseases produced by *kiṃnaras*, *yakṣas*, serpents, *vidyādharas*, and others.
The soul itself indicates [the suffering] arising from excessive misconduct toward the wise and the preceptor.
The Yoginī [removes] disorders of the eyes caused by the provocation of wind, phlegm, and bile; diseases such as urinary disorders (*prameha*);
ailments of the private parts, stiffness, dysuria, and the discharge of semen; the loss of bodily luster caused by women and wives; and the disease of emaciation.
A white [planet] indicates fear from the host of Yakṣī mothers and the ruin of dear friends.
The son of the Sun (Saturn) causes disorders of wind and phlegm, lameness, falls, lethargy, fatigue, vertigo, pain in the belly, internal heat, loss of servants, pain in the sides,
misfortune to wife and children, injury to the limbs, and heartburn.
One should declare injury from trees or stones, as well as affliction by hosts of malevolent spirits such as piśācas and the like.
Svarbhānu (Rāhu) portends fever, leprosy, mental delusion, artificial poison, pain in the feet, fear of Piśācas and serpents, and calamities concerning one's wife and children;
Ketu, moreover, indicates enmity with Brāhmaṇas and Kṣatriyas, fear arising from enemies, and danger from weapons.
Fear arising from ghosts, poison, bodily ailments, and impurity resulting from [the death of] a relative—all these are [neutralized]. || 9 ||
If Mandāra is conjoined with Vyaya in the second house, there will be eye pain; if Candra and Aruṇa are seen [there], there is eye pain.
If Śaurya and Aṅgirasa are seen conjoined with Yama and Āra, there is ear pain.
If Sogra is in the fifth house conjoined with Anghri, Ari, and Nātha, there will be abdominal pain.
Likewise, when the seventh house is occupied by Mars and Venus, there is a disease of the private parts. || 10 ||

If Saturn is in the sixth or eighth house, there is fear of fever; if Mars and Ketu are present, wounds; if Venus, pain in the private parts; if Jupiter, consumption; and if Saturn, wind-related ailments.
Furthermore, if Rahu is aspected by Mars, there are boils; and if Saturn is with the Moon, there is a disorder arising from abdominal tumors (gulma).
If the Moon is waning and situated in a water sign conjoined with malefic planets, there will be water-born disease and emaciation.

Once born, one goes by whatever path toward death; I shall now declare its cause. Death occurs through diseases mentioned for the signs situated in the eighth house (the *randhra*), provided they are strong, or else by the disease stated for the eighth-sign itself, or by the fault of the sign occupied by the lord of the eighth house.
One should predict certain death by the lord of the eighth house being the lord of the Khara-triṃśāṃśa of that [ascendant]. || 12 ||

If the eighth house (nidhana) is conjoined with a planet, death occurs due to the diseases indicated by that planet; or else, if the eighth house is aspected by planets, death results from the class of defects inherent to the nature of that sign. || 13 ||
The Moon [causes death] through fire, heat, fever, bile, weapons, and exhaustion;
Mars through cholera, water-borne diseases, consumption, and the like, as well as through blood, fire, minor ailments, malevolent spells, and weapons;
Mercury through jaundice and the like, or from delusions; and Jupiter through phlegm and death without exertion.
But a poet [should describe] a disease arising from association with women as being caused by wind (vāta), or by the humors in combination (sannipāta), or by Saturn (śani).
Through leprosy, or from the consumption of artificial poisons, or from the poison of Rāhu, or from smallpox and the like;
or through the hostility of enemies, or from insects and such, the planet Ketu brings about an untimely death for men. (15)

One should declare death arising from the inherent defects of the eighth house from the ascendant, or else that produced by the defect caused by the sign occupied by the ninth-part (navāṃśa) of the lord of the eighth house. || 16 ||
In the year of the Peacock (Paittya), there is fever from heat and digestive fire;
in the Bull (Vṛṣa), it arises from the three *doṣas* and weapons; but in the Twin (Yugma) year, there is death from time, wind, heat, and colic.
In Cancer, [there is affliction] from insanity, wind-disorders, and loss of appetite. || 17 ||
In Hari, [the fever] is born of wild beasts, eruptions, or enemies;
in a woman, it is born from the secret parts due to falling;
in Tulādhara, it is born of mental distress, fever, or *saṃnipāta*.
In those afflicted by diseases of the spleen, jaundice, anemia, and malabsorption syndrome. || 18 ||
In Vṛścika, [death occurs] from trees, water, wood, or weapons;
in Mṛga, from horses, limbs, wild beasts, spears, fire, delusions, and the like;
and in Kumbha, from cough, fever, and consumption.
In the middle there is danger from water, or in the end, from a water-borne disease.
If the eighth house is joined by a malefic and also contains a malefic,
there is suffering from weapons, fire, wild beasts, or serpents; likewise,
if two malefics aspect each other while occupying the ascendant, there is similar affliction.
Or [death] may come from the wrath of a lord, or from weapons, poison, fire, and so forth. || 20 ||
If [the Moon] is in a benefic Navamsha, in a benefic house, or in a sign related to benefics, or if the lord of the eighth house is in a sign of loss (Kshaya-bha),
the death of men occurs without suffering.
When they are thus separated, they say there will be a cruel death. || 21 ||
If the lord of the twelfth house is in its own exaltation, in its own sign, or in a benefic varga, and is situated in an upward motion (ūrdhvagati) with a benefic, [the native attains prosperity];
in the opposite case, some say there is only a downward motion (adhogati).
[This is] due to the division of the zodiacal signs arising from the upward-facing head. || 22 ||
The Sun and Moon lead to Mount Kailāsa; Venus to heaven; Mars to the earth; Mercury to Vaikuṇṭha; Saturn to the city of Yama; Jupiter to the eternal world of Brahmā;
Rāhu to the islands; and Ketu leads living beings to hell.
One should relate the relationship of the lord of the ascendant there, according to the degrees of the final sign. || 23 ||
Indeed, the events of the previous birth are indicated by Dharmeśvara (the lord of the ninth house),
and the future birth by Suteśa (the lord of the fifth house); likewise, the caste of that [birth] and the constellation presiding over it [are determined from these].
For in that very place is the direction, specifically the region of its lord. || 24 ||

If [the planet] is in its exaltation or its own lord's sign, there is birth in a divine land; if it is in its fall, an enemy's sign, or a neuter sign, it is another continent; if it is situated in its own house, a friend's house, or a neutral house, [it is likewise].
One would surely attain the land of Bhārata-varṣa itself. || 25 ||
Āryāvarta is the sacred abode of Bṛhaspati; the Śutudrī river is that of Kavi and Indu; the region of Jña is a holy place;
the land of the Mlecchas is that of the Sun, the burner with sharp rays; and the Paṅgunī river is that of the Moon.
Saulāraṇya and Kīkaṭa belong to Bhūmija. || 26 ||
If a malefic planet is situated in a fixed sign, occupying a fixed portion, in a sign that rises from the back (a posterior-ascendant), and is located in a downward-facing sign,
the birth will be from trees, creepers, and the like; so too if its lord is so situated.
There might be a living being endowed with a body in a different way. || 27 ||
The lord of the Lagna goes to the exaltation, friend's sign, or own house of the lord of the [ascendant] for human birth;
in an even sign, there would be quadrupeds, and in the other, birds.
It should also be considered by means of the forms of the *drekkāṇas*. || 28 ||
If two planets are born in the same sign in one's own country, and they are of equal strength and the same species,
then the color and quality of that planet are identical.
One should express everything using only those things designated by names.
Fifteenth Chapter:
Contemplation of Dispositions (Bhāvacintā)
All houses, when joined with or aspected by the lords of auspicious houses,
grant the full fruits of those respective houses, provided they are free from the aspect or conjunction of malefics;
likewise, all malefics are said to be the lords of their own houses in this system.
All planets, when devoid of being in their fall, combust, or inimical positions, yield auspicious results here. || 1 ||

When each respective house is in its own trine, its own sign of happiness, or its own sign of passion, and is conjoined with benefics, devoid of the aspect of malefics, occupied by the lord of that house, and not joined by malefic planets, they say there is prosperity for those houses; this brings about all auspicious results, whereas otherwise, there is destruction.
Likewise, the entire [chart] consisting of the houses of the signs and so forth is mixed with the lords of the planets. II.2.

If the lord of the house has gone to its place of destruction (the eighth house), or is eclipsed by the rays of the Sun, or has entered the sign of its debilitation or an enemy, and is neither conjoined with nor aspected by benefics,
it brings about the destruction of that house; such is the case unless there is another [beneficial factor] present.
Even its presence does not bestow fruit if it is not auspicious, for a fierce planet brings about destruction. || 3 ||

If malefic planets are situated in the sixth, eighth, or twelfth houses from the ascendant or any other house, they cause the destruction of that house and so forth; however, benefic planets do not bestow such extreme results. Thus they have declared the results of the houses and so on. ||4||

Experts declare that if the lord of a house, or its enemy, or a planet in the eighth or twelfth house from it, or the lord of an afflicted house occupies that house, there will be the destruction of that house; however, if it is aspected by a benefic, there is happiness for that house. || 5 ||

When the lord of the house is situated in that house but is devoid of strength, and the planet known as the *kāraka* (the significator) is placed between malefics, aspected by malefics and enemies but not by other planets,
and when malefics occupy its fifth, eighth, or twelfth houses, or its trines— [In such a case, the native will suffer from the afflictions of that house.]
It must be stated that the loss of its true nature here becomes evident due to the absence of corroboration by two or three [independent sources]. || 6 ||

Planets that are lords of the respective houses, their sub-periods (*parabhava*), the lord of the *īśvara* *dreṣkāṇa*, or the lord of the *kharadraṣkāṇa*, and those that are weak or situated in the eighth or seventh house from a house, cause the destruction of that house during their own periods. Malefic planets situated in the third, sixth, or eleventh house from a house are auspicious when located in a quadrant or a trine from that house.
Indeed, those who are rich in vigor and are friends of the Lord of Meditation bestow the accomplishment of one's being. || 7 ||
If the lord of the *dhṛti* (the eighth house) from either the birth sign (*rāśi*) or the ascendant (*lagna*), its occupant, or its aspector;

Saturn; the lord of the *krūra-dṛg-aṇa*; the lord of the *gulika-pada*; the lords of the signs and degrees occupied by these [planets]; and Rāhu are all situated in houses other than the desired ones at birth, that person is extremely weak.
When conjoined with malefic aspects during its own period, it brings about the destruction of one's thoughts.
If the lord of a house remains conjoined with a benefic planet while occupying that house, he shall yield the results arising from that house;
however, if the lord of the house is weak and situated in an unfavorable house, the opposite of this is declared.
The Dosha would become exceedingly strong; therefore, the smallness of the Dosha has been described [only] in relation to its strength. || 9 ||
If the lord of the sixth house is the ruler of the house in question, he bestows the increase of that house even if it is inauspicious,
provided that there is no strength in another [planet] occupying the ascendant.
An example of this is when Mars is situated in Leo in the fifth house, or when Venus is so placed.
The best authorities state that when there is a benefic aspect, one obtains a son; they declare that such attainment occurs swiftly.
If there is lordship over two places, the primary [strength] arises from the trine-sign;

half of that [strength] is in its own house. One should state the former of the two [halves] at the beginning of the period (dṛṣādi), and the latter half of the bhāva here at the time of the subsequent [period]. In the case of a dual sign, the strength arising from the dual sign [is determined] in the dual house.
And when [the Moon] is situated in Taurus, some people declare that it produces the results of the state of possessing vigor. || 11 ||

Whichever planet is the lord of the house of destruction (the eighth), or whichever planet is an enemy by aspect, or whichever planet is joined with zero points or empty signs— in its respective period, [it causes affliction] to the house of the body (the first) and so forth.
One who knows the truth should not speak of destruction to a physician. || 12 ||
Even if a lord of planets is situated in its own exaltation or the sign of a friend and is endowed with the six primary strengths,
it will yield no fruit if it is situated in a *sandhi* (a junction between signs).
Having reflected thus, one should speak here regarding the ripening of karma.
In the houses, the portion equal to the degrees clearly occupied by a planet produces the full result arising from that house;
at the junction (sandhi), there is no result, nor is there any in the interval between them.
Indeed, the movement of those who travel through the sky is inconceivable. || 14 ||
One should contemplate the Sun as the source of one's own paternal splendor and power,
and the Moon as the progenitor of prosperity, generating favor from the mind, intellect, and the king;
through the Son of the Earth (Mars), one attains courage, the qualities of health, and the destruction of enemies and kinsmen.
He is the kinsman of knowledge, the discernment that acts as a maternal uncle, the friend who performs deeds through speech, and the awakener. || 15 ||
From Vāgīśvara (Jupiter), one should state wisdom, wealth, physical nourishment, sons, and knowledge;
from Bhṛgu (Venus), a wife, vehicles, ornaments, and the pleasures of amorous activity;
and from Mandu (Saturn), longevity, the causes of death, calamities, and servants.
One should meditate upon the Grandfather (Brahmā) as a serpent, and the Maternal Grandfather (Śiva) as a peacock.
The Sun, Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Saturn, Venus, Rahu,
the Sun, Jupiter, the Moon, and Saturn.
Jupiter and the Sun are the karakas from the ascendant. 17.

The results for planets situated in friendly, inimical, or neutral signs, or in their own signs, exaltations, and so forth, should be considered through the houses beginning with the ascendant as the body; likewise,
prosperity and adversity arise from the presence of benefics and malefics respectively.
It speaks falsely regarding the twelfth, sixth, and eighth houses. || 18 ||
Malefic planets situated in the sixth, eighth,
or twelfth houses cause the increase of those houses through their defects; however, benefic planets indeed cause the destruction of those houses.
Therefore, there is the destruction of the sprout of existence, beginning with the umbrella and so forth. || 19 ||
Having reflected upon the fruit of whichever house and having designated that house as the ascendant (lagna),
one should then declare the results arising from the twelve houses based on that.
The fruits are such things as wealth corresponding to that [form]. || 20 ||
For thus it should be considered by the one who performs the act:
with respect to the father, the mother, the uterine brother,
as well as the maternal uncle, the son, and the husband.
[The calculation] for the servant is from the asterism in which the Sun and other planets are situated. || 21 ||
From the asterism occupied by the Sun, one determines the nature of the progenitor; from the second, his prosperity and his manifestation;
and from the third, his brother and his qualities.
And from the fourth [day] onwards, one may also happily visit his mother. || 22 ||
From the sixth [house], one obtains intelligence, favor, and sons; from the seventh, suffering for the father, harm from enemies, disease, lust, and pride.
They experienced suffering and death within the house of death; thus they passed their time. || 23 ||
Merit is auspicious; it indeed causes its father to flourish through that very auspicious activity because of its nature as karma.
For from the penultimate [moment] comes gain, and from the final [moment] comes destruction.
Thus they have declared the results for the moon and the other [planets] according to their presence. || 24 ||
In this manner, one should infer each respective mother, brother, father, son, and so forth, from their corresponding state and agent;
when that state and agent are present, [one considers] the lord of that bhāva.
For one endowed with vigor, there is happiness regarding that state. || 25 ||
The Sun is in the house of Dharma, the Moon in the house of Bandhu, Mars in the house of Śaurya, Jupiter in the fifth house,
Venus in the house of Kāma, and Saturn in the eighth house.
Others say that one should cause him distress. || 26 ||
The lord of the ascendant, joined with the lord of whichever house and situated in that house, bestows the fruit of that house;
provided that the lord of that house possesses strength.
Through the [influence of] Bhāva there is happiness; through Balona there is calamity. || 27 ||

If the lord of the ascendant is joined with the powerful lord of a particular house and occupies a primary division (mukhyāṅga), it brings about the experience of that house; likewise for [the lord of] whichever house [it occupies].
However, if it is joined with the weak lord of a house that occupies a censurable division (nindyāṅga), it yields the results of those [censured houses].
One should act in the opposite manner; thus it has been declared regarding all states of being as well. || 28 ||
If a planet situated in an unfavorable house is located in its own sign or its own house, it produces only the results of its own sign and house; otherwise, it is weak.
If Saturn is in Capricorn in the fifth house, there is success regarding children.
And here, there is no result of faults caused by the presiding lord of the sixth house. || 29 ||
Mutual conjunction in a single sign, aspecting from angles (kendras), or being situated in a trine—this fivefold method is declared to be "bondage" (bandha). || 30 ||
Chapter Sixteen:
The Results of the Twelve Houses (Dvādaśabhāvaphala)

The body [of the native] shall correspond to the sign and sub-division (navāṃśa) of the ascendant, or to the sign occupied by the most powerful planet; its complexion shall be that of the sub-division occupied by the Moon, and its limbs shall be distributed according to the signs beginning with Aries starting from the ascendant. || 1 ||
If the lord of the ascendant is situated in a quadrant or a trine, possessing a full orb, or in its exaltation sign or its own sign—
even if located elsewhere than in a quadrant— and if the lord of the eighth house is conjoined with a benefic at the time of the ascendant,
the native will be long-lived, wealthy, endowed with honored virtues, and esteemed by kings.
If the lord of the body is joined with a benefic planet, one becomes prosperous, handsome-limbed, firm-bodied, fearless, righteous,
and possessed of a virtuous family. Alternatively,
if it is conjoined with a powerful planet, there is residence in a good village or association with the virtuous, or patronage by a renowned king.

If [a planet] is in its exaltation, one becomes a king oneself; if it is in its own house, there is residence in its native land. If it is in a movable sign, there is travel; if in a fixed sign, there is stability. In a dual sign, the result is of two kinds. || 3 ||
When the lord of the body (the Sun) is situated in its own sign, it is renowned and radiant; when well-placed, it brings happiness and prosperity;
when ill-placed, it causes suffering; and when in a house of an enemy or a debilitated sign, it dwells in a lowly place.
When healthy and powerful in a rising sign of its exaltation, it lives in comfort, increasing in strength and vigor.
Lacking confidence, he is struck down by calamities; repeatedly distressed, he becomes afflicted. || 4 ||

When the lord of wealth (Jupiter) attains its primary dignity in the second house, a man endowed with the excellence of all virtues, possessing family prosperity, wealth, and a pleasant countenance, shall be far-sighted; likewise,
when the Sun is in conjunction with the second lord, he will be capable of removing obstacles.
One may obtain knowledge and wealth; however, under Saturn, one is devoted to trivial and insignificant learning. || 5 ||

If Jupiter is situated there, one becomes proficient in the Vedic scriptures and Dharmaśāstras; if Mercury, one is skilled in the science of statecraft (Arthaśāstra); if Venus, one is adept in erotic expression; and if the Moon, one may possess some proficiency in the arts. If Mars is situated there, one is skilled in cruel arts and is a slanderer; and if Rāhu is situated there, one is stubborn and dull-witted.
In Ketu, one's wealth is lost through false speech; with malefic planets, one is deluded and destitute. || 6 ||
If there should be a conjunction between the lord of the ascendant and the lord of the third house, situated in each other's signs and endowed with strength, it bestows courage,
heroism, and favorability toward siblings.
He incurs the state of being a perpetrator of a rash act. || 7 ||

If the lord of the third house is strong, conjoined with a benefic planet, and the Karaka (the significator) has also attained a benefic state, there is an increase of brothers; however, if it is devoid of strength and situated in an unfavorable house, the destruction of siblings occurs. || 8 ||
If the lord of the significator in an odd sign is aspected by Jupiter, the Sun, and Mars,
it shall be an odd house known as Vikrama.
The brothers shall become [heirs] by virtue of their respective shares. || 9 ||
Even if the Moon is in a benefic house but situated in an inauspicious *duḥsthāna*, devoid of the yoga or aspect of the virtuous planets,
and joined with or aspected by malefic planets while remaining within the domain of the sinners (*pāpa*), death from the mother occurs.
If both of these [the Sun and the Moon] are endowed with strength, joined with benefics, and aspected by benefics while situated in the house of siblings (*bandhu*), [the mother survives].
One should declare that happiness for the mother and the Moon arises from benefics situated in the houses of happiness (the fourth house). || 10 ||
If the lord of the ascendant is in the fourth house, or the lord of the fourth house is in the ascendant, or there is a mutual aspect between these two, or likewise from the Moon;
or if these two are in each other's sign of enemies, or in their signs of debilitation, or in the sixth or eighth houses from each other, [then it indicates the death of the mother].
If it does not benefit the mother, nor does it prevent their destruction, or if there is no bond between them; || 11 ||
The same as described for the mother's state should be declared for the father, brothers, sons, and so forth;
one should speak [of their conditions] by means of the significator of the state, the lord of that house, the lord of the ascendant, and the lord of the ascendant itself.
When Venus and Jupiter are strong and situated in the fourth or third houses,
they bestow the status of a lord of the people and a palanquin;
one obtains golden rivers, priceless jewel ornaments, and silken beds.
And for the enjoyment of desires, [he gave] cows, elephants, and horses.
If the lord of the fourth house is situated in an inauspicious house and conjoined with Mars and the Sun, or if the fourth house itself is so afflicted, the birth-house is burnt;
it is likewise ruined if it is joined by Rāhu or Saturn and associated with an enemy planet.
Cattle, land, vehicles, and so forth taken away by others.
If Mercury is in its own sign or division, conjoined with Mercury, or in the fifth house from it or its lord's sign,
and is in its specific division (vaiśeṣikāṃśa) and in its state of excellence (sadbhāva), the person will be intelligent and free from deceit.
If the lord of the ascendant is situated in an inimical house, conjoined with or aspected by malefic planets, or joined with the lord of the sixth house;
or if the lord of the sixth house is in a quadrant (kendram) and conjoined with or aspected by malefic planets.
It swiftly and intensely spreads an unavoidable affliction among enemies. || 16 ||
If the lord of the ascendant is exceedingly powerful than the lord of the sixth house,
