is endowed with the portions of benefic planets, and is joined with the aspect of benefics; and if the lord of the house of happiness (the fourth house) is also strong and situated in a quadrant or a trine—
Endowed with health and good fortune, he possesses firm limbs. || 17 ||

If the lord of the sixth house is in an unfavorable house (duḥsthāna) and conjoined with its debilitation, its retrograde state, or an enemy planet, then, provided the lord of the ascendant is stronger than that and the Sun is auspicious, there is the destruction of enemies.

If the lord of the sixth house is conjoined with the lord of a certain house and occupies that house, or if the lord of that house is situated in the sixth house, those houses become enemies. || 19 ||
When the seventh lunar mansion is conjoined with the six auspicious relations and its lord is endowed with strength,
the wife will possess a husband and children, be devoted to her six duties, and be possessed of all excellent qualities.

If the lord of the eighth house is other than the tenth house and is weak from the lord of the ascendant, there will be no mental distress, no obstacles, and no suffering for men; their lifespan shall be long. (21)
If Mars or the Sun is in an unfavorable house (duḥstha), or if its ruler is so situated,
or if they are even situated between malefic planets, one should predict the death of the father.

If the lord of the ninth house (Dharmeśa) is strong during the day when the Sun is present, or at night when the Moon is present, and is aspected by benefics, the father of that [native] lives for a long time. || 23 ||
If both Mandāra and Śītaruci (the Moon) are in a trine from the Sun, the son will be abandoned by his mother and father;
however, if he is aspected by Śakrapurohita (Jupiter), the son shall be happy and long-lived.
If Saturn is the lord of the ninth house (bhagya) and is situated in a movable sign (chara rasi) without being aspected by benefics,
then even if the Sun is in an unfavorable position, the native indeed lives off another father.

If the lord of the ninth house, or its ruler, is weakly conjoined or aspected, or if it is combust, the child born will surely be given away; however, if the lord of the twelfth house is strong, he will remain with his parents.
When a benefic planet is in the tenth house, or its lord is strong in a quadrant or a trine, situated in its own sign, its exaltation, or in the tenth or the first house,
one becomes possessed of honored and great fame and is devoted to righteous deeds.
He shall possess fortune equal to that of a king and enjoy a long life. || 27 ||

If the Sun or Mars is in the tenth house in the Janavallabha yoga, one accomplishes a great undertaking characterized by great prowess, provided that the Lord of the Tenth (Sūrya) is well-placed; furthermore,
if Mercury is there, he carries out activities involving deceit and learning.
When Saturn, Mars, and Ketu are situated in the tenth house, a man becomes a doer of evil deeds. || 28 ||
If the lord of the eleventh house is joined with the lord of a particular house, or even situated in that house, there will be the acquisition of an object corresponding to that house;
the same applies if [the lord of the eleventh] is in the houses of others.

Whichever lord of a house is situated in the twelfth house, and whichever lord of the twelfth house is situated in that [first] house, one should predict the destruction of the corresponding object of that house.
If the lord of a house occupies the sign, degree, or trine of the lord of the ascendant,

or if the lord of the ascendant occupies the sign, degree, or trine of the lord of that house, or if he reaches the ascendant itself— then, through either their conjunction or their aspect, there is the accomplishment of that house.
One should declare [the results] based on the conjunction with the karakas, from the lord of the ascendant, and also from the Moon.
When Jupiter transits the sign, degree, or trine occupied by the lord of a house,
one should predict the attainment of the results of that house.

But when there is a conjunction with the lord of the sixth house, and that enemy planet is weak compared to the lord of the ascendant, then the native is under its control; otherwise, it is the reverse. (33)
If the lord of the ascendant is an enemy by nature, or is situated in the sixth house due to the influence of a temporary enemy, or is placed in the eighth house,
then let him speak of rivalry; however, this is not the case when he is situated in its own sign (gocara).
Likewise, friendship also arises from association and from affection. || 34 ||
When there is a conjunction between the lord of the ascendant and the lord of a particular house,
that is the time for the attainment of its results; if the lord of the house possesses strength, it is auspicious, otherwise the opposite.
This should also be considered from the ascendant and from the moon. || 35 ||
Chapter Seventeen:
The Section on the Great Departure (Niryāṇa)

If Saturn is situated in the degrees occupied by the lord of the eighth house from each respective house, or in its trine, or in the sign and degrees occupied by the lord of the twelfth house, there is the destruction of that house. || 1 ||

If Gulika, Saturn, or the lord of the eighth house, or even the ruler of its Khara Drekkāṇa, occupies a sign, its Navāṃśa, or its Trikoṇa, and Rāhu (the son of the Sun) is also there, one dies. || 2 ||

Likewise, death occurs when Jupiter is in the ninth-part (navāṃśa), a trine, or a quadrant from the lord of the rising sign, the lord of the eighth house, or the lord of the eighth-decanate (drekkāṇa). || 3 ||

Death occurs when [the Moon] is in its own exact twelfth-part (dvādaśāṃśa), or in the navāṃśa occupied by the lord of the eighth house, or in the navāṃśa occupied by the lord of the ascendant, or even in a trine thereof. || 4 ||
When the Moon has gone to the ninth, eighth, seventh, or fourth house from the Sun, one should predict death; all of this should be considered from both the ascendant and the Moon.

When Jupiter reaches the sign, degree, or trine occupied by the lord of the ascendant devoid of Saturn, or reaches the sign or degree of the Moon devoid of Saturn, then his own death occurs; or when [Jupiter] is devoid of Rāhu—
If Jupiter is in the ninth, fifth, or eleventh house, there is the destruction of siblings.
If Jupiter is in the sign of the Sun (Leo) devoid of malefics, or in its domicile or trine, the father perishes; likewise if Saturn is in the sign of Mars or in its own Navāṃśa or trine.
If Jupiter is in the sign of the Moon or in its own Navāṃśa or trine, [the mother perishes]; and if Rāhu is in the sign of the Moon or in its own Navāṃśa or trine...
If Saturn is in the eighth house from the ascendant, or in its own division, or situated in a trine house, there is death of the mother.
One should declare *yamakaṇṭaka* from the opposing asterism and its lord;
if Jupiter is situated in a corner of that house, there is the destruction of sons.

Whichever house is occupied by the lord of the sign resulting from the sum of the ascendant and the corrected mandi-sun, the native meets his death when Jupiter is situated in that same sign or in its trine (koṇa). || 9 ||
When the Sun is subtracted from the Māndi-sphuṭa, if the resulting sign, degree, and minute [fall within the range] of Saturn, one shall die;
[this applies to] the sign of the conjunction of the five planets beginning with Venus (Dhūma).
And when the Sun has entered the Drekkāṇa [of the Moon], death occurs. || 10 ||
The experts declare that the degree of the sum of the ascendant and the mandi-sphuta is the month of niryaṇa;
the conjunction of the niryaṇa-moon and Gulika is [the indicator].
The conjunction of the Ascendant, Saturn, the Sun, and the Moon is called Vilagna. || 11 ||
When the son of the Lord of Day (Saturn) is situated in a Navāṃśa that has arisen clearly in the sign of an immortal (Gemini), conjoined with its own Dvādaśāṃśa,
and when the Sun is in a Drekkāṇa or a Kōṇa house, death [occurs].
If the rising sign is joined by the Moon and the Moon's slow-motion point (māndi), it will be occupied by the lord of that sign at its time of rising. || 12 ||
Having multiplied Gulika and the son of the Sun (Saturn) by the number nine, death occurs when Saturn is situated in the sign or degree of the sum of both [planets]. || 13 ||
When Jupiter is situated in the ninth part of that sign from which the *yamakaṇṭaka* of the lord of the ascendant has been subtracted [and the result is] clear, there is death without a doubt. (14)
When Saturn has gone to the sign formed by the sum of the longitudes of the lord of the sixth house and the lord of the twelfth house, or has reached its trine, there is danger of death for men. (15)
If the Sun has gone to the sign occupied by the lord of the rising decanate,
or its trine, or if Saturn is in the house of the lord of the third part of the eighth house, then destruction occurs.
Or, they say that death occurs when the trine is reached by this [planet]. || 16 ||
Of the lords of the ascendant and the eighth house from birth, of the lords of their respective Khara-triṃśāṃśas,
and also of the Moon and its Mānda [the Moon's apogee], [one should consider] the weak degrees.
If Saturn is situated in a trine, death shall occur. || 17 ||
When the lord of the ninth-part (navāṃśa) occupied by the lord of the ascendant is equal to the house of the lord of the eighth house, and the lord of the pot (the Moon) has entered that [house],
one should declare a yoga of death according to many scriptures.
That was proclaimed by those whose minds were crushed and distressed. || 18 ||
If the house of the lord of the third decanate (dṛgāṇa) associated with the Moon is situated in the first [house], or has gone to the house of the lord of the third decanate,
or is in a trine, death occurs for embodied beings.
Then, if the Moon should be in the second, eighth, or twelfth house, [the following occurs].
If the Sun is in the sign occupied by the lord of the eighth house, or the Moon is in the sign occupied by the Sun,
and this occurs under a lunar mansion conjoined with the lord of the eighth house, one should predict death.
If Saturn is situated in a trine from that sign which is endowed with Gulika, death occurs for those born at night; for those born during the day, it occurs when [Saturn] is in its fall.
When Jupiter reaches the sign of the conjunction of the true positions of Jupiter and Rāhu, or when it is situated in its trine (trikoṇa), one should know that death occurs. || 22 ||
If Saturn is situated in the eighth house, occupying one-third of it, or if it has entered the ninth sign from that [eighth] house, death shall occur. (23)

If at the time of birth, Saturn is situated in a trine from the lord of the birth sign, or from the lord of the eighth house, or from the sign or degree occupied by the lord of the eighth house, the person dies. (24)

If birth occurs at night in a sign of the Moon, death occurs in a sign of Saturn; if it occurs during the day in a sign of the Sun, death occurs when Saturn is in that same sign, its seventh house, or its trine. || 25 ||
"From the sign occupied by the lord of the eighth house, count as many signs as there are from the sign occupied by Mandi;
if Saturn is located in that [counted] sign, one should predict death—so it was spoken by the True Guru. (26)

If the Sun is in the twelfth house from the Janma-kālīna-Ṛju-jātaka-kāma-śatru [the tenth house from the natal ascendant], one should declare death as certain; thus it was spoken by the true Guru. (27)
When the lords of the eighth, twelfth, and sixth houses, the lord of the third part of the eighth house,
and Saturn occupy their respective houses, and the Sun, Mars, and Moon likewise move through those same houses by virtue of their motion,
then death shall indeed come for men.
One should declare death for them due to the influence of their respective rays, or even in their respective trines.
Chapter Eighteen:
The Yoga of Two Planets (Dvigr̥hayoga)
The Sun, joined by Venus, produces a man who is a maker of stone implements; with Mars, he is sinful; with Mercury, he is skillful and endowed with wisdom, fame, and happiness;
with Jupiter, he is cruel; and with Venus, he is devoted to other undertakings and skilled in the arts of performance and weaponry.
One born when Saturn is in the ninth house will have acquired wealth through archery or various types of trade.
If the Moon is with Saturn, the woman will be deceitful, addicted to liquor, and of inauspicious character;
if with Mercury, she will be eloquent, skilled in worldly affairs, endowed with good fortune and fame;
if with Jupiter, she will be valiant, the foremost of her family, yet of unstable mind, and a mistress of her own heart.
The Moon with Venus brings skill in crafts and the like, while the Sun likewise bestows the son of a remarried woman. || 2 ||
If Venus is with Mercury, one becomes a merchant or a wrestler who carries loads of oil and the like;
if with Jupiter, he becomes a city magistrate or a king, or a Brahmin who has acquired wealth.
If with Saturn, he is a cowherd, a wrestler, or a clever man devoted to the wives of others and a gambler.
Afflicted by suffering, untruthful, and censured when Mars is in the son of the Sun (Saturn). || 3 ||

If Jupiter is in the fourth house conjoined with Mercury, one is a performer on stage; if conjoined with Venus, one is fond of song, skilled in dance, eloquent, and a leader among the multitude of people;
if conjoined with Saturn, one is gentle, clever in illusion, and lecherous;
and if Jupiter is said to be conjoined with Venus, one is learned, possesses wealth and a wife, and is endowed with many virtues.
One born under Asita is to be known as a maker of beards; one born under Ghaṭa is also a maker of food.
When Asita and Sita meet, one who has little vision becomes wealthy through the accumulation of trust from young women,
and becomes a knower of writing, books, and painting.
They are to be conceptualized subsequently by means of the fruits already described. || 5 ||
If the Moon is in Aries, the native becomes a king, a learned man, a sovereign, or equal to a king; however, he may also be a thief or impoverished.
If it is at night, he is a thief; if by day, he is honored by the world and a lord of the earth.
One who is seen by Mars and the other [malefics] becomes wealthy yet also a servant. || 6 ||
If the Moon is in a dual sign and aspected by Mars, Jupiter, the Sun, Mercury, or Venus, the native will be a weaver and poor; however,
if it is in its own sign and aspected by Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, or Saturn, he will be a warrior, a wise man, a teacher, or a king.
One who subsists by working with iron and one suffering from eye disease [are born] in due order. || 7 ||
When the Moon is in Leo, one becomes a king, a master of astrology, or wealthy; a lord of men, a barber, or a sovereign ruler.
When it is in Virgo, one becomes a clever king or a commander of the army.
The lord of the earth, the king, should be thoroughly proficient [in these].
In Taurus, the ruler is deceitful; in Libra, a goldsmith; in Scorpio, a merchant who is slanderous and wicked;
and in Gemini, a king who is the father of twins and a sovereign of the earth.
He may be a cloth merchant, possessing wealth through his deformed limbs. || 9 ||
The rogue, the one with horse-limbs, the kinsman, the lord of men,
the multitude of men— relying upon these, the deceitful, treacherous king, the ruler of men, the sovereign of the earth, the wise man.
When the moon is in Capricorn, one who was wealthy becomes poor.
If the Moon is in Kumbha (Aquarius), the king is devoted to the wives of others;
if it is in Mīna (Pisces), he is a lord of men who is a master of courtesans and devoted to royalty, yet is honored by men.
In the final sign (Pisces), he is a doer of evil, yet possesses keen intellect, is a sovereign, and is learned.
It is difficult to overcome for one who perceives only faults when aspected by Mars and other [malefics]. || 11 ||
The results of the Moon being in its various Navāṃśas and the aspects of various planets upon it:
[If the Moon is in the Navāṃśa of Mars,] one is fond of killing guards and is skilled in battle.
If Mars is situated in the portion of the Earth (the second house), the king becomes wealthy but quarrelsome; if Venus is there, he is foolish, devoted to another's wife, and fond of pleasure;
and if Mercury is there, he is a composer of fine poetry, intent on happiness, and attached to another woman.
For when Baudha is situated in the portion of Śahini, one becomes skilled in acting on stage, in the arts of the Corakas, in counsel, in singing, and in crafts;
whereas when it is in its own portion, one becomes a chief among ascetics who are greedy for small bodies and wealth.
And while being watched, he was intent on the tasks of serving women. || 13 ||
In the portion of Leo, he is a lord of treasures, esteemed by kings, wrathful, and a son who is exceedingly cruel in his actions;
in the portion of Sagittarius, he is one of celebrated strength and an instructor in warfare.
He understands humor and possesses the mature character of an experienced counselor. || 14 ||
In the portion of Saturn, one has few children, is miserable, lacks respect for one's own kin, is devoted to one's own work,
is fond of wicked women, and is prone to anger.
Likewise, when the Moon or the Sun is aspected by the Moon and so forth. || 15 ||

The results for the degrees (aṃśa) from the Sun onwards prescribed here are to be understood as the very same results for the ninth-parts (navāṃśa). Whatever result was stated for the Moon in the examination of the signs (rāśīkṣaṇa)—
Indeed, the result of that twelfth part must be stated.

Whatever was stated as auspicious regarding [planets] situated in their own or exaltation *vargottama* divisions becomes, respectively, full, middling, or slight; whereas inauspiciousness follows the reverse order.
A planet endowed with strength first obstructs the effects of its own divisional lord.
The result of the moment of the zodiacal sign yields the result of the degrees. || 17 ||
Chapter Nineteen: The Results of Planetary Periods (Daśāphala)

Having compiled from the *Horā-āgama* that which was proclaimed by the renowned Parāśara— who, having long propitiated the nine planets with various kinds of devotion, received their favor and was granted a definitive conclusion for the sake of awakening through the fruits [of one's actions]— [this work is composed].
Having extensively examined the essence [of the various systems], I shall describe the great period known as Mahādaśā, which yields abundant results. || 1 ||
Agni, Āditya, Tāra-pati (Brahmā), Ravi, Candra, Bhauma,
Sarpamarenya, Śani, Candraja, Ketu, and Śukra; by him, the actor Sanijaya, together with Caṭudhānya-saumya—
It is appropriate that the nails of those [teeth] are said to be like autumn [lotuses]. || 2 ||
The *ghaṭikās* traversed by Tṛkṣa, multiplied by ten years and divided by the [ascensional] difference (*nata*), yield the number of his own years;
one should multiply that by seven and divide by the *nata*.
The months and days have been taken away in succession. || 3 ||
If the Sun, at its birth [of the year], were of such a nature as it was when that [previous] true Sun occurred,
then there are returns of the ten-year periods.
The corresponding signs should be determined according to the sequence of the divisions. || 4 ||
The Sun produces the results of the period (daśā) as follows: it causes quarrels, the wrath of kings, sudden calamities, and wandering due to disease among one's own kin.
Mutual enmity, unbearable mental agitation, and the suffering of one's wife, children, wealth, and grain due to the need for concealment; || 5 ||
The Sun, being well-placed, brings about the acquisition of wealth through cruelty, travel, kings, and quarrels; it causes wandering in forests and mountains, great renown, and victory.
Sharpness, constant delight in exertion, and happiness. || 6 ||
The Moon brings clarity of mind,
the accomplishment of all goals, and the enjoyment of happiness; it grants success in matters of women, sons, ornaments, garments, and jewels.
The attainment of the cow-land and the honoring of the twice-born. || 7 ||
Everything concerning the Moon should be declared by its strength;
in the first ten-day period, the result here is middling,
while in the middle ten-day period, it possesses full potency.
In the third part, the fruit is small, in due order.

The results of Mars's own period (daśā) are as follows: wealth is acquired through fire, kings, battles, and the like; the arrival of riches occurs through medicine, falsehoods, and various acts of cruelty.
One is constantly afflicted by bile, blood disorders, and fever, and indulges in the company of low-born women.
There is enmity with children, wife, kinsmen, and teachers; one is afflicted and finds pleasure in the fortunes of others. || 9 ||
Saumya brings about the arrival of friends, personal happiness, fame praised by the learned, the favor of one's teacher,
eloquence even in matters of bold speech, and service to others.
The welfare and greatness of one's wife, children, and other friends. || 10 ||
The preceptor of the lord of the gods bestows the attainment of righteous deeds,
the accomplishment of progeny, and honor from kings;
he also grants renown among exalted people and [the possession of] elephants, horses, and vehicles.
[One obtains] the acquisition [of wealth], splendor through a bride, son, and friends, and the fulfillment of desired goals. || 11 ||
In the sub-period of Venus, one attains articles for the pleasure of play, excellent vehicles,
cattle, ornaments, treasures, and delight with women; as well as knowledge, ritual action, and travel by water.
From the Lord of Milā, who holds great esteem for virtuous deeds. || 12 ||
In the Pāka [period] of Saturn, there arise diseases caused by one's own wife and children,
disorders of wind (vāta), destruction of agriculture, senseless chatter,
attachment to a wicked woman, separation from one's attendants, and living abroad.
Do not cause the sudden destruction of the happiness and goals pertaining to one's own kin and land. || 13 ||
It causes fear of kings, enemies, poison, fire, and weapons; suffering for children, mental agitation, loss of kin,
humiliation from low-born persons, and defamation due to transgression.
He suffers displacement from his position, loss of rank, and the failure of his undertakings. || 14 ||
When Rāhu (Vidhuntuda) is endowed with auspicious [planets] and conjoined with commendable houses,
its period (daśā) then bestows auspiciousness and grants prosperity equal to that of a sovereign;
there shall be the accomplishment of desired undertakings and a state of happiness within the home.
Those who accumulated wealth through their generosity became renowned for their fame upon the earth. || 15 ||
During the ripening of the planetary period (*daśā*) of Rāhu when it is situated in the sign of Scorpio, there is honored happiness,
the acquisition of a kingdom, and the attainment of a vehicle drawn by men.
At the end of the ten-fold cycle, there is the destruction of everything.
During the period of Ketu, there is suffering from enemies, thieves, and kings, as well as wounds from weapons and diseases caused by heat;
furthermore, one suffers false accusations and the disgrace of one's family.
There is danger from fire and expulsion from one's own country. || 17 ||
Now, during the period of Saturn (Taraṇi), there is conflict with cruel kings, suffering from fire and quadrupeds, distress to the eyes,
diseases of the stomach and teeth, and great affliction for children and wife.
There will be separation from one's elders, loss of servants, and loss of wealth. || 18 ||
During the period (daśā) of the Moon, there is the attainment of prosperity through mantras, deities, Brahmins, and kings;
success regarding women, wealth, and land;
and the acquisition of flowers, garments, ornaments, perfumes, and various flavors.
Indeed, there will be conflict with one's own kin or a wind-related disease. || 19 ||
During the period (daśā) of the son of the Earth (Mars), there will be prosperity arising from fields, enmity with kings, and the acquisition of cattle and land; however,
there will be enmity with siblings and sons, and attachment to wicked women.
There will be eye disease, blood disorders, bile-related ailments, and loss of wealth. || 20 ||
During the period of the best of Asuras (Rāhu), there may be a wicked nature,
or intense suffering from diseases, the destruction of children and wife,
fear of poison, affliction by enemies, and diseases of the eyes and the upper parts of the body.
There will be opposition from friends for the king, and he will incur the enmity of others. || 21 ||
During the major period (daśā) of Jupiter, there is the attainment of wealth such as clothing and other articles,
an increase in attendants and retinue, excessive honor, the acquisition of children, wealth, and friends, and the receipt of praise and worship from virtuous people.
There occurs separation from one's teacher, ear disease, and affliction by phlegm. || 22 ||
During the period (daśā) of Saturn, there is wealth acquired through the suffering and blows inflicted upon the nation;
the acquisition of servants, elderly women, and cattle such as buffaloes and bulls; yet, there is also great affliction for one's children and wife.
There is pain in the anus due to wind and phlegm, and a burning sensation in the feet, hands, and limbs. || 23 ||
During the period of Mercury, there is constant success through teachers, the acquisition of wealth produced by Brahmins, the gain of fields, cattle, and horses,
honor from men, heroes, and gods, and the accomplishment of accumulated riches.
There prevails the affliction of diseases caused by wind, heat, and phlegm. || 24 ||
In the state caused by Śikhin (the planet Ketu), there is grief and delusion for women, suffering at the hands of powerful men, loss of wealth, and offenses;
these prevail for embodied beings in their own country.
The disease of the feet is caused by seeing [impure things], and the affliction of phlegm is caused by heat. || 25 ||

During the period (daśā) of the son of Bhṛgu (Venus), there is the acquisition of women, jewels, garments, gold, wealth, ornaments, horses, beds, and seats; or else, the arrival of wealth obtained through trade, agriculture, and water-borne transport.
There occurs separation from one's teacher and excessive mental anguish regarding kinsmen.
Chapter Twenty:
The Results of Sub-periods (Antardaśāphala)
Whatever fruit is to be experienced by whichever [planet] as the powerful lord of the house, or by whichever one of weak strength—
[the author] shall now indicate that correctly and concisely.

When the ascendant is strong, this person born therein attains sovereignty in the world, a state of happiness, physical vigor, and great luster; he achieves ever-increasing prosperity, like the waxing young moon. (2)
When the Sun is in the ninth house (Pāka), one attains the fulfillment of family life,
the acquisition of virtuous daughters, and the enjoyment of happiness; furthermore, one obtains wealth through a livelihood based on speech.
The speaker [utters] a well-spoken word that is praised in the assembly. || 3 ||
In the presence of valor and prowess, natural favorability and the hearing of the wind of contentment constitute valor;
one attains the status of a general and self-confidence.
A refuge for people is the state of being a vessel for excellent qualities. || 4 ||
In the sub-period (dāya) of the lord of the fourth house, one obtains assistance from kinsmen, success in agricultural work, association with groups of women, and the acquisition of vehicles;
furthermore, there is a new field, a house, the attainment of wealth, and a praiseworthy residence. || 5 ||

During the period of Mercury, one obtains a son, enjoys the company of kinsmen, attains the position of a minister for kings, or receives great honor; and here on earth, one eats and gives away abundant, delicious, and refined foods.
He should perform that which is conducive to the highest good and praised by the virtuous.
In the year of the Lord of Enemies (Rudra), one slays enemies through acts of daring and attains freedom from disease, magnanimity, invincibility, and extraordinary prosperity.
Having prepared garments and ornaments for his bed,
the exceedingly powerful one, being delighted, enjoys himself with his beloved and performs auspicious great festivals and other rites.
And there is a journey for contentment during the sub-period of Mars within the major period. || 8 ||
He attains liberation from debt, elevation of self, and the cessation of quarrelsome activities;
he also gains buffaloes, cattle, goats, servants, and people.
In the age of the powerful Lord of the Aperture (the Sun). || 9 ||
Together with his wife, sons, grandsons, and circle of kinsmen,
he constantly experiences good fortune and prosperity;
[he attains] auspicious deeds and honor from the lords of the earth.
In the period of the lord of the ninth house, there is devotion to the victors and the gods. || 10 ||
Whatever task has been undertaken, by means of this [practice], one attains its very accomplishment, a happy life,
fame, stability, and the engagement in wholesome conduct.
[There is] the heightening of pride during the period of the lord of karma. || 11 ||
Unimpeded sovereignty, reunion with beloved kinsmen, servants and slaves,
and the great rise of worldly fortune— these are the blessings of saṃsāra.
One shall obtain [gain] during the period (daśā) of the lord of gains. || 12 ||
The lord of the twelfth house causes excessive expenditure toward virtuous people, the destruction of a multitude of sins, auspicious deeds, and honor from the king. (13)

The results of the *daśā* of a planet situated in its own sign, exaltation, or the house of a friend are thus; [the results] of one in an enemy's sign, a debilitation sign, *mūḍha* (retrograde), the sixth, or the twelfth house are as follows:
But I shall also describe the results for one who has a perforated belly.
When the lord of the ascendant is in an unfavorable position, one encounters confinement, living in concealment, fear, dependence on others due to disease, loss of status, and calamity;
as well as dullness in assemblies, instability in speech and family, ill-repute, and eye disease.
When the lord of the second house is in the sixth house, there is verbal fault, loss of wealth, and fear of the king.

If the lord of the third house is in *duścikya*, one should predict the death of a sibling, ill-considered actions in one's affairs, the oppression of internal enemies, humiliation, and the crushing of their pride;
as well as distress to the mother, misfortune, harm to beloved friends, and calamities regarding fields and houses.
When the lord of the netherworld (Pātālanātha) is weak, there is the destruction of cattle, horses, and other livestock, as well as danger from water.
During the sub-period of Vīryonnaprati-bhāpati, there is the death of a son, confusion of the intellect, travel on the five paths,
abdominal disease, the wrath of the king,
the loss of one's own power, fear of thieves, misfortune, punishment, many diseases, and wicked deeds.
In the sub-period of the sixth lord, one attains servitude, humiliation, infamy, and physical wounds. || 17 ||

If the lord of the eighth house (the *randhreśa*) is weak, there will be calamity for the son-in-law, separation from one's wife, the arrival of misfortune caused by women, addiction to gambling, secret diseases,
and wandering about; furthermore, during its period (*dasa*), there will be an increase in grief, delusion, intoxication, envy, and fainting.
One should declare poverty, wandering, ill repute, diseases, contempt, and death. (18)

Inauspiciousness equal to the wrath of a deity worshipped in the past, calamities concerning wife and children, the death of one's own preceptor and father, and wretchedness when auspiciousness is weak—
whatever action one performs will be fruitless, and there shall be a shattering of honor. The sky...
[He perceived] the presence of evil qualities, exile, misfortune, and the occurrence of wicked conduct. || 19 ||
In one's old age, there is hearing unpleasant speech, suffering for siblings,
grief for children, wretchedness, deception, ear disease, many ailments, humiliation, imprisonment, and the loss of all prosperity.
During the period of the lord of the twelfth house, one undergoes decline like the waning moon.

Whatever has been stated in the verses on the rules for the *kārakas* regarding the signification of the accusative case, whatever result is described in the determination of livelihoods, whatever fruit arises from the conjunction of the lord of the ascendant (*lagna*) with a planet in the rules for longevity and disease,
and whatever result arises from the conjunction with the lord of the house (*bhāveśa*).
In this [system], the results of both the lords of the houses and the planets occupying those houses should be declared during their respective periods. || 21 ||

The Dasha of a planet situated in a Vargottama Navamsa bestows auspicious results; however, that same Dasha becomes mixed when the planet is set or in its sign of debilitation, as is the case with the Dashas of the lords of the eighth, twelfth, and sixth houses, or during their periods of loss.
Even for one remaining there, the fruit will be inauspicious. || 22 ||
During the removal of the period of a malefic planet, during the fruition of the lord of the third, fifth, or seventh asterism,
and likewise during the enjoyment of the lord of the eighth house from birth;
He suffers the affliction of thieves and enemies, as well as extreme misery. || 23 ||
If the fourth of Saturn, the sixth of Jupiter,
or the fifth of Mars occurs at the end of a sign,
it will be painful.
Likewise for one who remains [in that state], though he is a lord of a difficult position. || 24 ||
Indeed, the period of one born on the earth situated in a lofty palace with its face turned upward, having reached the point of karmic fruition, bestows sovereignty; for,
having conquered enemies, he is endowed with vast mounts and armies.
The gift of food greatly expands the glory of sovereignty. || 25 ||
If Venus is situated in its exaltation, or placed in the twelfth,
tenth, or eleventh house, and is not eclipsed by the Sun nor conjoined with malefic planets, then at the time of its annual fruition, that person will be filled with many jewels.
Victorious is the wise one, of vast splendor and highly praised. || 26 ||
For all auspicious planets situated in the eighth, sixth, or twelfth houses bestow inauspicious results; however,
malefic planets occupying these same houses bestow [the opposite].
Their miseries at the ten stages are ultimately unfailing. || 27 ||
If the lord of the tenth house occupies the sixth or eighth house, or if the lord of the ascendant occupies the sixth house during its period,
there will be fear of enemies and the loss of one's position for that person.
Even one who is affectionate surely becomes an enemy. || 28 ||
The lord of the house of ripening (the Sun) produces results corresponding to the house it occupies from the lord of the tenth house; however,
this does not apply if it is situated in the sixth, twelfth, or eighth house.
It would produce suffering in one case and happiness in the other. || 29 ||
In its own sign, exaltation, trine, friend's sign, enemy's sign, and fall, [the strength] is full, three-quarters,
half, one-quarter, small,
and zero respectively; if it is auspicious, this is so in direct order, but if inauspicious, it is the reverse.
In a retrograde planet, the result shall be equal to that of one in its sign of debilitation. || 30 ||
The planets that are the lords of the 8th,
12th, 6th, and 3rd houses, as well as those who are the lords of their respective navāṃśas— if these possess weak periods (daśās), they bestow death.
When the son of the Sun (Saturn) moves in a painful sign. || 31 ||
At the commencement of the *daśā* of whichever is stronger between the lord of the *bhāva* occupied by the lord of the eighth house and the lord of the *kha-ra-tri-bhāga*,
[the death occurs] in the *aṃśaka* associated with the eighth house.
When Jupiter is situated in a trine, there is emaciation of the body. || 32 ||
The lords of the fourth, the natal ascendant,
and the ascendant [at the time of query] bestow happiness during middle age; they do so respectively when situated in the back, both sides, or the head of the horoscope.
Situated in the last, middle, or first [houses], it brings about its fruition. || 33 ||
If the lord of the Dasa, by its position in the zodiac from the ascendant, is situated in its own sign, its exaltation, or the house of a friend,
it brings about the strengthening of that particular house at that time.
If he is endowed with strength even at birth, [he will become a great man]. || 34 ||
If the lord of the ninth house at birth is combust,
in its state of debilitation, in an enemy's sign, or in its fall, and moves by direct motion toward whichever house it occupies [at that time], [it causes misfortune].
At that moment, it brings about the destruction of that [state]. || 35 ||

When the Moon, by its course of motion, arrives at the exaltation of the lord of the period, or in a friendly sign, or in the third, sixth, tenth, eleventh, trine, or seventh house from the lord of the period;
If one arranges [the ritual] otherwise, misfortune will occur. || 36 ||
When the Sun, from its position in its domain,
reaches its own sign of debilitation or its enemy's sign, it brings about suffering; however, when it is in its own house or its exaltation, it bestows auspicious results.
When it has gone retrograde, it then yields the fruit of happiness. || 37 ||

When the Sun enters the exalted house of a planet that bestows auspicious results, one attains the fulfillment of those results; the Guru (Jupiter) should likewise consider the result in this manner. However, when it enters the sign of debilitation or the enemy's place for a lord of a period that yields difficult results, [the outcome is adverse].
When the sun has entered its range of vision, one reaps the painful fruit of that very act. || 38 ||
Accompanied by whichever planet it may be, that lord of the serpents (Rāhu) shall produce the fruits of the virtues and defects arising from that planet;
for even if that celestial body is endowed with serpents and is auspicious, it brings hardship.
It produces suffering especially at the time of the final ten [degrees]. || 39 ||
Two [planets] desiring wealth and pleasure here are called "demons" (māraka);
their lord, having gone there, being full of strength,
destroys [them] at its own fruition, like a lord of death.
Or if the lord of the twelfth house is also exceedingly weak. || 40 ||

The lords of the tenth and ninth houses, whether situated in their own signs or not, shall bring auspicious or inauspicious results during their periods; all lords of the trines (5th and 9th) bestow auspiciousness, even if they are givers of misfortune as lords of the third, sixth, and eleventh houses.
Furthermore, the lord of the eighth house, if he is also the lord of the ascendant, shall produce auspicious results, as will the Sun or the Moon.
If it is thus auspicious, then according to the opinion of Parāśara, the result occurs during that respective period (daśā). || 41 ||
If the lord of a trine is situated in a quadrant, or the lord of a quadrant is situated in a trine, both grant a yoga;
both of these [grant it] during the period of enjoyment.
Those two, bestowing yoga upon one another, were mutually beneficial.

All the planets do not bestow auspicious or inauspicious results upon people during their own periods or their own sub-periods according to their own nature; rather, they do so in accordance with the individual's own disposition. 43.
Those who are connected to oneself and those who are one's own companions bestow the fruit of their own condition only within the hearts of others.
The lords of the Kendras and Trikonas, even if they themselves are afflicted by defects, become strong and causeers of auspicious Yogas merely through their association [with other planets]. // 45 //
If there is a relationship between the lords of the trines by any means whatsoever,
and it occurs with the strong lord of a quadrant, that constitutes a yoga-maker.
If there is a conjunction between the lords of the ascendant and the trine, those two act as the cause of a yoga;
how much more so if there is a connection with the lord of another trine? (47)
Due to their connection with the performers of yoga, even malefic planets naturally bestow yogic results according to their respective periods of transit. (48)
If the lord of the trine is in its own period (dasa) while the lord of the quadrant is in the pearl (śukti), he bestows auspiciousness;
if it is not so, even in the absence of such a relationship, he causes evil.
However, the defect of central lordship is powerful for Jupiter and Venus;
even though they are malefics, their placement in a malefic house [neutralizes that defect]. (50)
Following that, Mercury and the Moon would also be of that same nature;
if the malefics are the lords of the angles (kendras), they become increasingly auspicious.
If two malefic planets should reside in a quadrant or a trine,
they become makers of a yoga through their connection with the lord of either one of them.
If the two nodes (Rāhu and Ketu) are situated in auspicious houses and are unconnected with anything else, they become yoga-producers according to their respective sub-periods (antardaśās). || 53 ||
The commencement of Rājayoga occurs during the periods of malefic planets;
starting from that point, the periods of the malefics gradually expand it. (54)
The lord of the eighth house,

the lord of the sub-period (dasa) of the eighth house, the lord of the ninth part of the eighth house, and the lord of the sign occupied by the lord of the eighth house— these bestow suffering, especially whichever among them is weak.
It causes destruction when its own period is eclipsed. || 55 ||
For a planet that has fallen from its exaltation, the state known as "descending" (avarohi) occurs when it is in a friendly sign or its exaltation degree;
for one that has fallen from its depression, it is "ascending" (ārohiṇī).
If it is in the degrees of its debilitation, enemy, or fall, it becomes base. || 56 ||
If a planet is in its exaltation house, in its exaltation degree, or even if it is in its sign of debilitation, an enemy sign, or situated in its setting,
its period (daśā) should be known as yielding mixed results, with the results being manifested in the latter half of the period.
During the period of a planet that has lost its respective state, whose own state has perished, and which is devoid of strength, one shall meet with death. || 58 ||
If the lord of the *daśā* should be situated in the ascendant from the ascendant, or in the third, sixth, tenth, or eleventh house from the ascendant,
or likewise in its own *saptavarga*, or if it is its friend;
If a benefic is in the ascendant, its period will be auspicious. || 59 ||
The number of years [indicated by the letters] shall constitute the period (daśā), and the lord of that period is the planet situated there according to the sequence of the zodiacal signs;
from whichever sign the Moon is positioned, that is its house.
For the fruit, whether existent or non-existent, must indeed be conceived based on its persistence.
If [the planet] is situated in a friend’s house from the lord of the period (daśādhinātha),
or is in its exaltation from the lord of the period, or is situated in the fifth, ninth, or eleventh house from the lord of the period;
Indeed, the moon bestows excellent fruits. || 61 ||
Among the signs mentioned, whichever sign the Moon has entered shall be the house of the body, wealth, and so forth, as they existed at the time of birth;
it is declared that this [sign] brings about the increase of those respective [matters] for men.
If situated in another sign than that, it causes the destruction of its existence.
Having examined the Sārāvalī, the Muhūrtadaśā, and Varāha’s Horā, one should declare the results of birth for men;
or else, by means of the planets at the time of a query or their own birth [horoscope].
One may speak by means of the zodiac signs and so forth; there is no distinction between these two. || 63 ||
Chapter Twenty-One:
The Results of the Sub-Sub-Periods (Pratyantardaśā)
I shall now clearly explain, in due order, the characteristics of the divisions of the planetary periods;
whatever is stated here should be declared at the beginning of each respective sub-period (antaradaśā) and so forth.
The years [of the period] multiplied by the years of the ripening [period] and divided by the years of the lord of the [current] period;
the remainder, multiplied by six and divided by twenty-seven, gives the months; and the remainder, divided by seven, gives the days.
One should calculate in this same manner for the other periods as well, according to the sequence of their ripening, if there is a period.
Furthermore, the lords of the intermediate periods (antarāntaradaśās) beginning with Nātha follow the sequence of the lords of their respective maturations (pāka). || 2 ||
From Sūrya Mahīśvara, one obtains greater fame,
a dwelling in forests, mountains, or on level ground, and the arrival of wealth.
The fever, the heat, the pain, the separation from loved ones, and the fear—
all these enter into the very rays of one's own glance.
The destruction of enemies, the pacification of calamities, the arrival of wealth,
success in agricultural activities, the building of a house, association with friends, the warding off of the fire of decay, and freedom from debt; these are the results.
When the Moon removes diseases born of water. || 4 ||
The onset of illness, separation from one's position, harassment by enemies, the emergence of blemishes on one's complexion, opposition from those born of one's own family,
fear for the monarch, and the loss of wealth shall occur.
When Mars is in the year, he takes away that solar year. || 5 ||
The rising of enemies, the loss of wealth, the emergence of calamities,
fear of poison, and further delusion regarding sense objects— these bring about excessive pain for embodied beings in their heads and eyes.
Ahau would be the interior of the shark-mouth. || 6 ||
The destruction of enemies, the daily acquisition of various riches,
the worship of the gods, and the honoring of Brahmins, gurus, and kinsmen;
yet there is also exhaustion of the ears and the affliction of consumption.
O Surācintā, when one enters the state of the Lord of Cows (Kṛṣṇa), one attains the condition of a cowherd.
There is loss of wealth, separation from children, illness for a woman, sudden heavy expenditure, the loss of one's belongings,
extreme filthiness, and an affliction of phlegm.
When Saturn has entered the period of the Sun. || 8 ||
Scabies, boils, leprosy, jaundice, flatulence, and pain in the stomach and waist will occur; there will be the destruction of the earth and fear of the three types of diseases at that time.
The son of the Moon (Mercury) moves for one year in the sign of the Sun (Leo). || 9 ||
There is conflict with friends, kinsmen, and family;
fear of an enemy, loss of wealth, and dismissal from one's position; as well as severe illness from the preceptor and intense pain in the feet and head.
When the crested one enters the state of the sun. || 10 ||
For embodied beings, there will be headaches, intense pain in the stomach and anus, agricultural failure, loss of home, wealth, and grain, and extreme unhappiness regarding children and wives.
Then, for one year, it moves in the son of Bhṛgu (Venus) from the Sun. || 11 ||
Under the influence of the Moon,
there will be the acquisition of a wife, the obtaining of spotless garments, and association with the most excellent of Brahmins.
The mother’s desired fruit and the happiness of women enter their own period when the moon is in its [favorable] state. || 12 ||
When Mars is present, there will be ailments arising from bile, fire, and blood;
affliction by distress, suffering, enemies, and thieves;
and the loss of wealth and honor.
When the moon had reached another state [of its phases]. || 13 ||

In the year of Saravihāraka, there will arise a great danger from the increase of enemies with intense malice and from kinsmen; there will be fear of wind and thunderbolts, and the onset of fevers produced by [improper] food and drink, just like the waxing and waning of the moon.

When Jupiter is in its period of youth, there arises a delight in the dharma of giving, the emergence of happiness, the acquisition of clothing and ornaments, meeting with friends, and receiving great honor from kings. (15)
There may arise the affliction of many diseases, great calamity resulting from the illness of friends, children, or wife,
or even the loss of life, when the Moon is in the ascendant.
The interval between the ages of Māra’s kinsmen has passed. || 16 ||
The acquisition of wealth, elephants, horses, and herds of cattle, as well as the abundance of ornaments and happiness,
arises at all times when the moon is in the *cittabodha* [dasa].
Upon the awakening of life,
there is the loss of the mind along with one's status, the loss of kinsmen, and fear arising from the waters. || 17 ||
For embodied beings, there is the slaughter of slaves and servants;
and when Ketu is in [the sign], it carries away a lunar year.
When Venus is intent on taking the inheritance, there occur the sale or purchase of water-vehicles, ornaments, and women, as well as activities such as agriculture,
and the acquisition of sons, friends, cattle, and grain.

When the wind-bile disease (pittavātaroga) has passed, there will then be great royal honor, heroism, the pacification of diseases, and the downfall of the enemy faction, until the end of the year known as Śaśāṅka.
During the major period (mahādaśā) of Mars, the results of the various sub-periods (antardaśās) are as follows:
there is danger from bilious diseases, heat-related ailments, and wounds; separation from siblings;
and the attainment of wealth and prosperity arising from disputes over land.
If the son of Dhātrī (Mars) occupies his own house during the autumn season, there will be conflict with kinsmen, fire, enemies, kings, thieves, and people. || 21 ||
There will be fear of weapons, fire, thieves, enemies, and kings; danger from poison, emaciation, eye disease, and headache; loss of one's teacher or kinsmen;
loss of life, or else great calamities.
When the lord of serpents has entered the interval between the crooked [planets]. || 22 ||
There will be worship of the twice-born and the gods, constant service to holy places and merit,
perpetual honor shown to guests, and prosperity for sons, friends, and others;
or else there may be merely an affliction of the ears or the onset of phlegmatic diseases.
When the lord of speech (Bṛhaspati) is conjoined with Mars, there occurs the end of the period of Mars. || 23 ||
Successive destructions of one's own self, children, wife, and teachers; internal suffering from uncounted calamities; loss of wealth;
seizure of property by enemies; and fear of hot winds and fire—[these are the consequences].
This occurs when Saturn has entered the period of Mars. || 24 ||
There will be fear of enemies, great danger from thieves, loss of wealth, calamity for cattle, elephants, and horses, association with foes,
oppression caused by the king, or the arising of enmity with Śūdras.
The lifespan of the son of Viṣvadhātṛ enters into the son of the Moon (Budha). || 25 ||
There may be the fear of lightning, sudden affliction by fire or weapons, departure from the body, or the loss of wealth;
or else there may be the departure of the vital breaths or the destruction of one's wife.
If Ketu enters [the asterism], there will be the end of cruel eyes and life. || 26 ||

For human beings, there arises in battle the loss of honor, exile from one's own country, the seizure of wealth by thieves, the obstruction of the eyes by vomit, and the abandonment by one's attendants.
When Venus, the lord of the Bhārgava planet, occupies the eighth house, he steals away the lifespan born of the earth. || 27 ||
Having received honors from the king, possessing power gained through his own strength, surrounded by attendants, wealth, grain, and a splendid harem,
he was utterly consumed by his own excesses after attaining fortune through reckless daring.
It is the destroyer of the lifespan of Mars, which cleaves through the darkness [of ignorance]. || 28 ||
There is the attainment and loss of various kinds of wealth and sons, conflict with groups of enemies, the production of garments, beds, ornaments, and an abundance of gems,
as well as excessive devotion to elders and suffering from abdominal tumors and bile disorders.
When the cool-rayed moon has entered the rain of Dharaṇitanaya (the constellation Śatabhiṣaj). || 29 ||

During the major period (mahādaśā) of Rāhu, the results of the various sub-periods (antardaśās) are as follows: the sight of poison, water, disease, and wicked serpents; union with another's wife; and the loss of desired objects.
There will be misfortune, evil speech, and affliction from wicked people during one's own year when it is eclipsed by Rāhu.

The attainment of happiness, the honoring of gods and Brahmins, freedom from disease, union with beautiful-eyed women, and the arising of reflection upon the meaning of the most meritorious scriptures.
When Jupiter is situated in the eleventh house from the Sun. || 31 ||
There will be affliction of the body by wind and bile, conflict with one's sons, wife,
and kinsmen, the loss of one's servants, and a fall from one's position.
Then, when Saturn is present, the life-force enters into the earth. || 32 ||
The attainment of sons and wealth, meeting with friends,
and an extreme state of being censured by the mind arise;
as do proficiency in action, skill in ornamentation, and so forth.
O Moon-like One, who brings an end to the serpent-year! || 33 ||

Fear of fever, fire, weapons, and enemies; headache, trembling of the body, and distress caused by one's own friends or teachers; affliction from poison and wounds, and quarrels with kinsmen—[these are the results].
When the fire-bearer has entered within the interval between the two arms of Indra. || 34 ||
Acquisition of a wife, the enjoyment of beds and comforts, the acquisition of horses, elephants, and land,
an increase in phlegm and wind, and conflict with one's own kinsmen.
If there is the removal of the [malefic] aspect of Venus, it would result in the lifespan of a serpent. || 35 ||
There will be no distress from enemies, yet there will be excessive affliction of the eyes, injury by poison, fire, or weapons, the onset of calamities,
and great fear from the king due to the death of a daughter-in-law or a son.
When the year of the serpent had been taken away by the enemy of darkness (the sun). || 36 ||
There will be the loss of a wife, quarrels, mental anguish, the destruction of wealth from agriculture or trade, the loss of cattle and progeny,
the misfortune of friends, and danger from water.
Divided by ten in two ways, it is of two kinds for the gods and the asuras. || 37 ||
For embodied beings, there is fear of kings, fire, thieves, and weapons;
or the destruction of the body, or great diseases; as well as stumbling on the path and affliction of the heart and eyes.
When Mars moves through this Sarpa-yoga, [the following occurs]. || 38 ||
During the major period (mahādaśā) of Bṛhaspati, the results of various sub-periods (antardaśās) are as follows: there shall be the arising of good fortune, luster, great honor, and virtues;
the attainment of virtuous sons; and honor from the king.
When Jupiter is in its own sign, it brings about association with teachers and virtuous people, the accomplishment of desired goals, and takes away one's own year [of life].
There will be association with the faults of liquor that causes madness, like that of a courtesan;
there will be suffering for one's family and cattle despite excellence and happiness; and there will be loss of wealth, eye disease, and great distress for one's children.
The sun enters a state of life-giving vitality for men. || 40 ||
Some say that the great vices of women, gambling, and liquor arise from the three humors (doṣas),
while others say they result solely from the attainment of auspiciousness;
[these vices are countered] by the practice of honoring gods and brahmins, and by the pursuit of sons, wealth, and happiness.
The Moon's son (Mercury) removes the period that is honored by the color of a peacock. || 41 ||
There will be wounds from weapons, conflict with servants, mental anguish, and trouble caused by children and wife;
there will be loss of livelihood and separation from teachers and friends.
Having taken away the sour taste and vitality, Ketu bestows it [back]. || 42 ||
The attainment of various objects, cattle, grain, household goods, women, sons, food, drink, beds, garments, and ornaments;
and the worship of gods and brahmins, as well as being intent upon spiritual service— these are the results.
When the son of Māyū took away the life-force of Jaiva, he was then worshipped by the Asuras.
There shall be victory over the enemy, the acquisition of honor and fame for the king, ferocity, the obtaining of men and horses as mounts,
and all the riches of guilds, agrahāras, cities, and kingdoms.
When the Sun has been removed by the Sahajāyu [planet] from its high declination, [the result is as follows]. || 44 ||
For men, there will be an abundance of women, the destruction of enemies, the acquisition of wealth, success in agriculture and trade, the attainment of supreme fame,
and an extreme devotion to the worship of gods and brahmins.
When the Moon is in its period, there arises the seizure by a heavy [demon]. || 45 ||
There will be the pleasing of kinsmen, the acquisition of wealth from a group of enemies, and the honoring of a fertile field; furthermore,
there will be a slight injury from one's elders or perhaps a minor wound to the eye.
When Mars is in the sign of Aries, it carries away the noble-born for a year.
There will be distress from kinsmen, severe mental anguish, suffering from disease, fear of thieves, a serious illness arising from the stomach,
oppression by a great king, calamity from enemies, or one's own destruction.
The wise man attains and brings about the state of the enemy of the gods (Śiva).

The results of various sub-periods (antardaśās) within the major period (mahādaśā) of Saturn are as follows: prosperity from agriculture, old servants, and buffaloes; affliction from wind-related diseases; and wealth from the Śūdra caste.
When the son of the Sun (Saturn) enters another sign within his own year, there is the acquisition of an elderly woman and a lack of vigor, yet no downfall.
There is good fortune, happiness from women, royal favor, victory, association with friends,
and the arising of illness from the three humors as well as suffering for siblings and children.
O son of the Moon, who takes away the inheritance of Saturn! || 49 ||
Affliction from Maruts and Agni, calamity from enemies, constant distress regarding children and wife,
inauspicious sights, and fear of great lords.
When Ketu is the lord [of the year], it takes away a mild year.
Endowed with the happiness of friends, women, and sons,
and possessing an accumulation of wealth produced by agriculture, water, and vehicles,
auspicious fame arises for embodied beings.
O son of Bhṛgu, who takes away the inheritance of Yama! || 51 ||
Furthermore, death, constant fear of enemies, illness among one's elders, ailments of the stomach and eyes,
and the loss of wealth and grain may occur here.
The lifespan of one born under the Sun enters into the intense rays [of that planet]. || 52 ||
For men, the assault of women is death itself; likewise, the misfortune of friends or the fear of disease,
as well as the fear arising from water and wind, shall become exceedingly great.
The life-force of the son of the Sun enters the Moon. || 53 ||
Falling from one's own position, conflict with one's kinsmen, illness, fever, fire, weapons, poison, or chariots;
or the increase of enemies, internal disease, and fear for one's eyes.
The life-span of one born under the Sun enters that of Mars. || 54 ||

Furthermore, there will be loss through wandering, separation from one's wife, or the fear of urinary disorders, abdominal tumors, and severe fever; men shall suffer from these afflictions constantly.
The Lord of Serpents enters the interior of the smoke. || 55 ||

There will be a delight in worshipping the immortals and in the company of groups of twice-born brahmins; yet there may be distress regarding one's home, children, and wife, while for men there will indeed be a great increase in wealth and grain.
Then, when Jupiter had reached the age of the Sun (twelve years). || 56 ||

During the major period (mahādaśā) of Mercury, the results of the various sub-periods (antardaśās) are as follows: devotion to the path of righteousness, association with wise men, and abundant wealth from Brahmins through pure intellect.
Through knowledge, one who has many honors and constant happiness under Mercury passes his own year. || 57 ||
When there is a state of being agitated by suffering, grief, and strife, trembling of the limbs, association with enemies,
and wandering through foreign lands;
The peacock, having reached the autumn that is the son of Soma, has gone [to its end]. || 58 ||

When the bright [period] of Bodhana arrives, there will be the performance of worship for gods, brahmins, and gurus, devotion to the dharma of giving, and the acquisition of clothing, ornaments, and the company of friends. (59)

When one year has passed from the time Mercury entered the constellation Bhānumālin (Pūrvaphalgunī), there will be houses covered with gold, coral, horses, and elephants, provided with food and drink, and even the honoring of kings shall take place.
When the cool-rayed moon [enters] Jyēṣṭhā, there shall be affliction of the head, pain in the eyes, leprosy, ringworm, and many throat ailments for men, along with the risk of loss of life. (61)

Fear of fire, pain arising from the eyes, extreme distress caused by fear of thieves, loss of one's position, or affliction by wind-related diseases—these take away the lifespan when the son of the Earth (Mars) is involved. (62)

When the Asura enters the period of the Moon, there occurs loss of honor or displacement from one’s position, personal ruin, danger arising from fire, poison, or water, and afflictions of the head, eyes, and stomach. (63)
There will be fear of disease, enemies, and downfall; yet there may be the attainment of Brahman, honor from the lords of the earth,
and a great surge of dharma, spiritual accomplishments, and ascetic merit.
When the minister of the gods has reached his final state. || 64 ||
When a disease born of phlegm and wind arises, there is a great loss of wealth and merit, and all the undertakings of living beings become fruitless.
When the dark fortnight has arrived at the end of one's lifespan. || 65 ||
During the major period (mahādaśā) of Ketu, the results of various sub-periods (antardaśās) include quarrels with enemies, opposition from friends,
hearing inauspicious words, fever, and burning sensations in the limbs.
When the Sun has entered its own period, one may experience the loss of wealth while traveling to another's abode. (66)
Quarreling with the best of the twice-born, conflict with one's wife,
even with those born of one's own family, the birth of a daughter, causing humiliation, and the tormenting of others— [these are the results].
It occurs during the interval between the Śikhin and Sita years. || 67 ||
The death of elders, fever, conflict with one's own kin, travel to a foreign land,
and quarrels caused by the king [occur]; [there is an excess of] phlegm and wind.
The interval between the Śikhin year and the Sun [year] enters [the calculation]. 68.
Likewise, there is the easy acquisition of much wealth, as well as loss;
birth accompanied by the separation from children and the experience of much suffering;
and the attainment of attendants, young women, and progeny.
When the moon has entered the constellation Śikhidāya (Jyeṣṭhā). || 69 ||
They say there will be internal strife within one's own family, the loss of one's kinsmen, fear arising from serpents, danger from thieves,
and affliction by fire and enemies.
If it moves in the sign of Mars, the life span of the planet named Dhvaja is [six years]. || 70 ||
Experts declare that quarrels caused by enemies, danger from kings, fire, thieves, or even serpents,
as well as the words of wicked people and ill-omened actions [are all portended].
When the *samā* has passed, they say the inheritance belongs to the eldest brother. || 71 ||
The birth of excellent sons, worship by the lords of the gods, the acquisition of land and wealth, the attainment of desired objects through offerings,
the accumulation of riches, and honor from the sovereign;
When the Guru has departed for the abode of the Lord of Peacocks (Śiva), [this occurs]. || 72 ||

The noble ones have likewise described the harassment of one's attendants, the tormenting of others, conflict with hostile persons, the breaking of one's limbs, and the loss of wealth, status, and splendor.
When the son of the Sun had departed, Śikhādharā’s life [ended]. || 73 ||
For men, there will be the loss of wealth, praise from the lord, the acquisition of land and riches, affliction by enemies and rulers, and the failure of livestock and agriculture.
The wise one enters the interval between the years [of the cycle] like a peacock. || 74 ||
During the major period (mahādaśā) of Venus, the results of various sub-periods (antardaśās) include the enjoyment of garments, ornaments, vehicles, sandalwood paste, and other luxuries,
as well as the happiness and prosperity derived from women.
Splendor, splendor, kingship, and the acquisition of wealth [occur] when the son of Bhṛgu enters his own period. (75)
For embodied beings, there is danger from the mountains arising from diseases of the eyes, the belly, and the cheeks;
and there is affliction caused by the preceptor’s family and kinsmen.
While Bhānumat, the son of Bhṛgu, remained alive. || 76 ||
It causes injury to the nails, head, and teeth; it destroys wind, bile, diseases, and poverty; and it afflicts those suffering from malabsorption syndrome, abdominal tumors, and consumption.
In that place, where the white [snow] removes the heat, there is the Himālaya poison.
It is the primary locus for diseases of blood and bile, a receptacle for gold, copper, and iron,
a source of great reproach, and a fall from one's exertion.
When Mars is in the year [known as] Vṛṣabhavallabha, || 78 ||
The acquisition of treasures, the birth of a son, the fulfillment of desired speech,
the honoring of one's own kin, and even the imprisonment of enemies; yet there is also suffering arising from fire, thieves, and poison.
When the year of Tulādhareśvara has passed, O Asura.
There shall be homage paid by the lords of various deities, the arrival of the scriptures of the self-born and the left-handed path,
and manifold royal pleasures for embodied beings.
The poet has brought [this] into the presence of the Lord of the Bow. || 80 ||
There will be honor bestowed by the king born in the city of Nagara,
the acquisition of excellent women, or else the possession of various riches and attendants.
When Saturn has gone to the house of Diti-pūjita (Vṛhaspati). || 81 ||
Happiness from sons, the attainment of the wealth of the scriptures, the acquisition of abundant stores, great power, fame,
and the excessive discharge of wind, bile, and phlegm—
The period of the minister of the Danujas occurs when Mercury is present. 82.
There is dwelling outside for one's children, happiness, and so forth; there is extreme fear born of fire and destruction, as well as bodily pain;
moreover, there is union with courtesans.
The peacock reaches the full state of Śukra. || 83 ||
Please state the results for the ten types of theft as they have been described according to the respective castes;
even in the case of minute apertures, the attainment of those same results occurs.
Or there may be reports concerning shadows, marks, and omens. || 84 ||
Chapter Twenty-Two:
The Kālacakra Daśā (The Kālacakra Period)
From Dhanisṭhā, one should count in an anti-clockwise direction (apasavya) by quarters starting from Aries up to the end of the portion of Pisces;
then, one should count in a clockwise direction (savya) from Cancer up to the end of Sagittarius.
By the path, step by step, without faltering. || 1 ||
In this manner, one should know that three asterisms each follow in sequence to the right, left, and counter-clockwise;
the duration of its *daśā* is determined by the years assigned to the lord of that respective *rāśi*.
The great ones declare the Lord to be Kālacakra. || 2 ||
Manu, Para, Sani, Dhani, Nṛpa, and Tapa, in sequence, are the years of Divākara; they are the causes for the attainment of auspicious and inauspicious results. (3)
I shall explain the statements concerning the Aśvins and other [signs] arising from the words "Aśvin" and so forth within the Kālacakra, by means of the nine rotating syllables.
The maximum lifespan here is determined by the years of the lords of the signs. || 4 ||
The city, the cows, the measured and the doubtful,
the moon among the stars, and the earth-spike (bhūśūla) are [the signs] for form, sight, treasure, and the body.
The constellation Vāṇīcastha is Dadhi. || 5 ||
The Lord of servitude, the son of Gaurī, the one who bestows wealth, the remainder of cattle and land—
may he be present in the lunar mansion of Śatabhiṣaj.
Mars and Jupiter cause suffering from children and the eyes. 6.
These statements regarding Aśvinī and Bharaṇī, as well as those concerning the asterisms beginning with Aśvinī up to Kṛttikā on the left side,
and those concerning Rohiṇī and Mṛgaśiras on the right side, will be explained in the following passages.
The words of Śvindu are indeed even more [powerful] than those of Rudra.
The cow is in the field; Śambhu is in the fortress. Of them, the collarbone is the treasure-chest and the slave-girl. The skin is the expanse; the eye is the lord of wealth.
The limbs of the women of the city are like the lotuses of the sacred bathing-place of Śiva.
The treasure of the axe, the giver, the needle of Śambhu, the wisdom of the sun, the constellation, the further shore;
at the sacred ford of Gośiva, the giver of the axe.
The song of the moon of her smile is delightful. || 9 ||

The period (daśā) arising from the *ghaṭī*s of the future [period] belonging to the lunar mansion-quarter (*nakṣatra-pāda*) should be known here according to the sequence of the previously mentioned quarters, starting from the first. It is produced from the year of its lord.
The Noble Ones have stated that such is the opinion of some. || 10 ||
The periods (daśās) of those planetary statements beginning with "Dasra" and others, which are composed of sequences of syllables, should be calculated in their respective order.
Some say that the sequence of the sentences is excellent. || 11 ||
In the sequence of the sentence, there is the "frog's leap" (*maṇḍūkagati*) and the "horse's gallop" (*aśvarapluti*) at the juncture between the *karkya* and *limīna*;
at that time, the "lion's glance" (*siṃhāvaloka*) is of three kinds.
The interval between the two decans (daśāntara) shall yield results of suffering. || 12 ||
When his maximum lifespan is reduced by the sequence of syllables in that statement, then,
during that period, the years of reduction—
And they shall state the number of months and days. || 13 ||
In these statements, they say that the measure of years is the maximum lifespan here;
[the calculation is] from Aries, subtracting the army (7) and love (5) by means of the elephant (8).
Tunda spoke again as follows: || 14 ||

The wise man should likewise apply the results previously proclaimed by me regarding the *utpanna*, *ādhāna*, *āura*, and *kṣema* periods within the great periods (*mahādaśās*) to these and other such periods. || 15 ||

After the birth asterism (janmarkṣa), there shall be the period known as Pañcamabhava; then the Utpanna-dāśā; after that, from the eighth house, the Ādhāna-dāśā; and from the [next] eighth house, the period called Kṣema-mahā.
At the conclusion of these very periods, death shall be granted to men.
For those with very short or very long lifespans, [the results are determined] at the end of the periods of the lords of the three deaths and the five asterisms.
The years for the natural periods (nisargadaśā) of the Moon, Mars, Mercury, Venus, Jupiter, the Sun, and Saturn are respectively one, two, nine, twenty, forty, fifty, and sixty.
The ripening of the results produced by nature occurs in succession through their respective periods;
some Yavanas do not accept that the period of the ascendant at the end is very powerful. (17)
Having converted the degrees of the *aṃśadaśā* into minutes, one should divide them by 2700; the remainder is the *āyuṣkalā*.
When the *satya* system is proclaimed, the years, months, days, and *nāḍīs* are obtained by dividing [the *āyuṣkalā*] by 1350. Thus are the *aṃśāyuṣ* (degrees-lifespan) calculated.

When retrograde and at its highest exaltation, this [strength] is tripled; when at its own triplicity and in the third part of its sign, it is doubled; when at its lowest debilitation, it is halved; and when in its state of blindness (mauḍhya), it is reduced to a quarter—excluding Venus and the Sun.
In all [planetary] strengths calculated as three and a half, the increase for the wicked is six parts; for the virtuous, it is a mountain (seven) in reverse order.
Then, when there is one planet in many signs, it takes away a half-share from the strength.
In the case of an enemy sign, it is reduced by one-third, except for Mars; this is the period according to the instruction of Satya.
If the ascendant is strong, it is equal to its own degree; even here, it is likewise equal to the sign of its rising. || 19 ||
Instruction for him is indeed better here;
however, many groups perform what is improper.
But in this matter, the role of a teacher lies in the act of striking [the disciple] many times.
But when there is only one [agent], that which is most abundant should be performed. || 20 ||
The Piṇḍāyurdaśā should be assigned; O Śūra, in the Śaka year, one should calculate the years of prosperity and sleep from the Sun.
In this system of Piṇḍāyuḥ, one should perform all the subtractions as previously described.

When the ascendant is malefic, one should multiply the degrees of the *bha* by the minutes of depression (*natāṅga*) and divide by the minutes of depression; this result is to be subtracted [from the *bha*].
When the *bha* is aspected by a benefic, half of this amount is to be subtracted; those who know the science of longevity understand it thus. (21)
In the system known as Paiṇḍa, they say that the strength of the ascendant's daśā is equal to its [planetary] portion (aṃśa) if the portion is strong;
however, if the ascendant is endowed with strength, it is here equal to the sign (rāśi), and not according to the portion.
If [the planet] is in its sign of fall (nīca), it should be subtracted; if it is full, it is the declared year in its exaltation (ucca) house.
O wise one, in the case of the Paiṇḍa and other [calculations], when [the result] is between two [signs], the rule of three (trairāśika) should be considered.
Maṇittha, Cāṇakya, Maya, and others declare that the lifespan called *paiṇḍa* is the primary one;
Bhadanta stated that this is not correct.
Likewise, there is the word of Varāhasūrya. || 24 ||
According to one's own school of thought, Jīvaśarman [states that] the maximum lifespan of the Sun and others here consists of their respective portions of the vowels;
for these as well, a complete subtraction must be performed.
As previously stated, the period of the ascendant should also be understood here.

The lifespan of men is declared by others to be twelve years multiplied by ten; furthermore, it is stated by others that the maximum duration for Saturn is three *bhagaṇas*. However, some have proclaimed here that in the Kali age, there is the sight of a thousand moons.
For we declare that the maximum lifespan ordained by the Vedas is indeed one hundred autumns.

At the beginning of a period (daśā), the planet possessing the greatest strength among the Ascendant, the Sun, and the Moon shall first give its results; thereafter, others situated in their quadrants (kendras) and so forth, according to their strength. However, when many planets are equal in strength, the one that bestows the longest lifespan or the most years shall act first, as directed by the influence of the year (abdasāmya).
But what is vigor here? It is that which is destroyed by the gaps between the grasping of the junctures and has reached the interior of the juncture of existence. || 27 ||
The longevity derived from the *aṃśa* (ascendant degrees) is to be calculated from the strength of the ascendant; that derived from the *piṇḍa* from the strength of the Sun;
and the natural (*naisargika*) longevity from the strength of the Moon.
We say that this applies even when the vigor of all three is equal. || 28 ||
The sum of those three [planets] here,
divided by three, should be considered as their *daśā*.
In the case of two [planets], the half-sum of their strengths shall be [the measure].
If these Jīvaśarmas are short-lived and lacking in strength. || 29 ||
The Kālacakra Dasa should be understood [to apply] when the lord of the lunar portion (candrāṃśeśa) is endowed with strength;
it is traditionally taught that the Dasa is always powerful by way of the lunar mansion (nakṣatra).
The lifespan of human elephants is sixty years doubled (one hundred and twenty); that of horses is five nights;
that of donkeys and young camels is thirty-two; and that of oxen and buffaloes is the square of five (twenty-five). The lifespan of dogs is twelve years.
It is recorded that for goats and the like, the maximum [number] is six plus ten.
Those who delight in righteous deeds, who have conquered their senses, who partake of wholesome food, who are devoted to the twice-born and the gods,
and those men in this world who maintain the grace of noble lineage and virtuous conduct—
This lifespan of theirs has been declared by those of noble intellect.
The Twenty-third Chapter:
The Praṣṭhakavarga (The Group of Eight)

In order to perceive the auspicious and inauspicious results for human beings according to the influence of the spheres of the planets, I shall here set forth the method for establishing that which is called the *aṣṭavarga*, as taught by the Great Sage. (1)

Having correctly drawn the zodiacal circle upon the ground, together with the positions of the planets and their activity at birth, one should here set forth the arrangement of the eightfold divisions (aṣṭavarga) in due order starting from each respective planet and asterism; this is called the "method of the eyes" (akṣavidhāna).
