From Saturn, Mars, and Venus in the house of a wealthy son-in-law (Putrīvansāhi), one obtains pearls; likewise, from Jupiter and Venus, one gains fortune. From Mercury, one attains the Gomatī river and supreme wealth; from the Sun, one gains desired objects; and from the Moon, [one gains] water.
Even when raised by song, there is lightness in the vessel of food that has not yet risen.

This [work] was sung by Gītā to Janaka, who was adorned with the *sāman* of Ravi; it was fashioned from the *tuṣāradīpti* (moon) with the *niṣka* of Śrīguṇita; it is constant through the months and years of Dhanas, like a pair [of seasons], from Budha;
from the *nīva* of Kaurava-sajjana, and from Bhṛguja, by the command of the one whose self is established in mystery.
In the Mandā yoga, when the moon is in its favorable transit within the Bāṇa group, it is auspicious. || 4 ||

From the Sun, the calculator of the stars, he obtained sharp rays; from the Moon, the son of the Earth, he obtained lac-dye for his subjects; from the Son of the Moon (Mercury), he obtained cattle; and from Bṛhaspati, the son of Siṭā, he obtained that [wisdom].
Who indeed was ever a cowherd to Kuruśani (Saturn)?
If Mars, having moved from its own sign at the ascendant, proceeds to the next, it bestows security during its transit. || 5 ||
From the Moon, there is a hundredfold yoga of gentleness through wealth; from Mars, great prosperity through theft;
from Jupiter, splendor; from Saturn, the destruction of cities;
from Venus, unerring policy; and from Mercury, a son who brings about the end of the great Andhaka lineage, as well as the gift of nectar to the cuckoos, arising from the ascendant.
In the month of Mūrti (Mārgaśīrṣa), during the rainy season, Jānakī is auspicious if the Moon's son (Mercury) is situated therein. || 6 ||
From Mārtaṇḍa [the Sun], to one who is ready to give a hand’s-worth of wealth; from Candra [the Moon], to one who possesses trees and a wife;
from Bhauma [Mars], to one who seeks the destruction of his master; from Budha [Mercury], to one rich in the wealth of instruction;
from the Preceptor of the Gods [Jupiter], to one who constantly gives the womb of a daughter; and from Śani [Saturn], to one who possesses his own fortune and the moon.
The illustrious wealthy ones always attain perfection from a specific white elephant for their bodies.

In the *jāti* [meter], there is *śrī* (the syllable *śrī*) in the Sun's [division]; in the Moon's, in *puragavāmandolliputra*; in the Body's, in *paure*; in Gain's, in *lābhamadālike*; in Moha's, in *kurulavaṃ*; in Dhana's, in *bhṛgoḥ*;
in Lobha's, in *tāllipare*; from Mars, in *garbhaṃ*; from Saturn, in *mahābdhau*; and in Naya, [there is *śrī*].
This Bhṛgu, who holds the small vessel of the teacher’s wisdom and is rich in pride, bestows happiness. || 8 ||
Observe the people on the streets during the Rādhā-rasa-yātrā; this collection of qualities, praiseworthy even by comparison to the Moon, Mars, and Saturn,
brings auspiciousness from Jupiter when he is in the form of a hundredfold [fortune], and from Mercury when he is intent on its preservation, starting from the point of his rising.
Others are born from the digits [of the planets]: Mercury from Bṛhaspati, Venus from the Moon, and Saturn from the Sun.
Thus, what has been stated is desired; the opposite is not desired. Due to specific distinctions, the planets should grant the ripening of the fruits of karma for living beings therein.
That which is situated in a house of increase, in a friend's sign, or in its own exaltation, grants a nourished and desired result.
There is no attainment of desired prosperity when [the Moon] is in an Apacaya house, or in its sign of debilitation, or in an Arāti or Gairnīca.
Having added eight to the group of the planets starting from Aries and subtracting the result from twelve, death occurs at one point;
[the remaining points indicate] loss, expenditure, fear, terror, and women.
The glorious *Rājyasiddhi* [yields] its fruits in due order. || 11 ||
Having designated each sign as the ascendant presided over by its respective planet and bearing that same name,
eight kinds of results arose from them.
Let them speak from that house, constrained by the power of their own nature. || 12 ||

The planets are currently situated in degrees equal to the number of signs, asterisms, and *āśakas* [occupied by] those respective planets due to their motion; likewise, the events arising from those houses [are determined].
They produce results that are both auspicious and inauspicious. || 13 ||
When the eightfold division has been made, whichever house-number a planet reaches from the sign of its own *kāraka*,
that planet— whether benefic or malefic— brings about the nourishment (*puṣṭi*) of that house.
If it is not stated, it produces the exact opposite. || 14 ||
When many [planets] occupy a single house at that time,
moving there by the power of their own dispositions,
they properly bring forth the fruits of that house's nature.
In the sense of the prior existence of that respective king, [the suffix *kvanip*] is applied after that [word denoting] the agent (*kartṛ*). || 15 ||
When the *bindu* is situated [in a house], and the *aṣṭavarga* has been cast to determine the time of the attainment of its results,
one should divide the houses there into eight parts according to their respective orbits (*kakṣā*).
Others say that their fruits [arise] in succession. || 16 ||
Regarding the Prastāra-aṣṭakavarga:
having drawn the diagram with nine lines running east-west and ten lines running north-south;
The Prastāraka diagram, consisting of eight rows and ninety-six squares, is produced from the Aṣṭakavarga. || 17 ||
The lords of the eight signs beginning with Aries, starting from the Hour (Lagna), are: the Moon, Mercury, Venus, the Sun, Mars,
Jupiter, Saturn, and Rāhu.
In due course, they shall bestow the fruit of that bindu.
When Saturn is in the first degree of the eighth part of a sign and Jupiter is in the second, there is fruit;
thus, according to the sequence of orbits, here [is the result] for the final portion.
It is taught that when [an action] is performed at the proper time, it becomes attached and yields fruit.

When the eight groups of all the planets have been cast, if the total number of dots (bindus) resulting from their addition according to the signs occupied at that time exceeds the count of eight dice (aṣṭākṣa), [then the result is auspicious].
In that deficient [year], misfortune occurs gradually. || 20 ||
As many as there are rays situated upon the auspicious mark of the cool-rayed moon,
or as many as belong to the moon within its auspicious mansion—
in this manner, that which is known here is even greater than those.
"O Svasti, misfortune has been indicated for others. || 21 ||
Having performed here the procedure for the points (akṣa) as stated in the Aṣṭavarga of the planets occupying the natal positions of the querent at the time of birth,
[one should determine] the auspicious sign and month by virtue of the conjunction of many points.
One should perform auspicious rites during the periods of the planets' positions and transits. || 22 ||
If even a malefic planet is situated in its own house, it greatly increases the bhāva;
however, if it is situated in the house of an enemy or a debilitated sign, it certainly causes the destruction of the bhāva. (23)

Even if a benefic planet is in its exaltation, it causes the loss of the house [it occupies] if it is the lord of a dusthāna; however, if it is the lord of a susthāna and situated in its exaltation, even a malefic planet brings about favorability for that house. // 24 //
Chapter Twenty-four:
The Results of the Praṣṭaka Division of Planets.

The ninth sign from the one occupied by the Sun is known as the Pitṛgṛha (the house of the ancestors); one should increase the Piṇḍaka (the sum of the points) by the numerical value of the fruits of that sign. || 1 ||

When the quotient obtained by dividing [the elapsed days] by twenty-seven moves into a lunar mansion under the son of the Sun (Saturn), at that time there will be suffering for the ancestors; of this there is no doubt.

If [the moon] is situated in the third house from that [ascendant], or if one has died equal in age to a paternal ancestor, the conjunction of the subtractive and remaining [periods] is known as the *śodhyapiṇḍa* (the subtractive aggregate). || 3 ||
During the Dasha of the lord of the Navamsha of the lord of the fourth house from the Ascendant, there is the death of the father;
or during the Dasha of the lord of the fourth house itself, one should predict a death similar to that of the father. || 4 ||
Having purified the *piṇḍa*, one should increase it by the measure of the Sun's apogee;
when the Sun has traversed [that distance], the remaining zodiacal sign is multiplied by twelve.
Furthermore, if [the planet] is situated in a trine from that, one should predict his death;
in this manner, a wise man should consider all the planets.
Having multiplied the piṇḍa by the fruits of happiness from the Moon and reduced it to its essential remainder,
there is loss of the mother when Saturn has gone there, or even when it is situated in a trine sign.

If the lord of the eighth house from the Moon is in a trine to the lord of the second house and is the ruler of the third or twelfth house, one should predict separation from the mother in that month; if it is so from the Ascendant, [separation] from the father.
One should declare the group of brothers from the results of the third house situated from Mars;
or the group of kinsmen and maternal uncles from the results of the fourth house from Mercury.

Whatever results exist for as many planets as are situated in the house of the Guru or the house of the son, with the exception of those in the houses of enemies or debilitation, the remainder are considered to be his sons. (10)
In the *aṣṭakavarga* of the Guru (Jupiter), the results remaining after subtraction—excluding the result of the malefic signs—are indeed known as his sons. (11)
If there is the birth of a wife when Venus is in its period of fruition, there will be an increase of the lineage through her; if it is small, the continuity of wealth will diminish.

Having multiplied the piṇḍa to be subtracted by Saturn from the ascendant, and divided by the results of the eighth house [or] the fourth house, the asterism remaining in the quotient is the one reached by Saturn or Jupiter; in that case, death occurs. (13)
In a year whose number equals the sum of the results from the ascendant up to Saturn, there is misfortune; likewise from the son of the Sun (Saturn),
for as many years as there are results from the ascendant up to that [Saturn].
For destruction occurs in the year equal to that conjunction. || 14 ||
Having multiplied the piṇḍa from the ascendant by the results of the eighth house and divided by the [number of] pleasures (sukhas),
one should know the result as the lifespan; however, one should calculate the time (velā) as before,
performing the subtraction of the trines (trikoṇa-śodhana).
Whatever is deficient among the three trines, one should subtract that equal amount from all three;
however, if one house is empty, one should not subtract from that trine. || 16 ||
If two of the chambers are empty, one should purify another chamber;
if all the houses are equal [in status], then one should purify everything at that time.
Having performed the purification of the single lordship and the purification of the trine, [one considers] the fivefold single lordships;
then the wise man should purify the results in the two fields. (18)
When [the result] is joined with planets but devoid of fruits, or when there is an absence of planets but an abundance of fruits,
one should subtract from this [result] that which is similar to the deficiency, provided it is free from planets.
If the planet is joined with a result greater than [the previous], one should subtract everything from the other;
when there is equality between the planet and the non-planet, everything is to be subtracted from the non-planet.
If both [the Sun and the Moon] are devoid of planets and are equal, one should discard the entire amount;
if both are conjoined with planets, it should never be subtracted.
In an empty house, one should never perform subtraction;
if there are two negative quantities, one should subtract the smaller from the larger of the two.
Having set aside what remains after subtraction, one should increase it by the measure of the zodiacal sign;
even if a planet is situated in that same sign, one should further increase it by the measure of the planet itself. || 23 ||
The multipliers for the zodiac signs and the planets are as follows: Taurus and Leo are multiplied by ten; Gemini and Virgo by eight; Libra and Aries by seven; and Virgo and Capricorn by five. (24)

The remaining [factors] are multiplied by their own measures and adorned with the ghatis of Cancer and Capricorn; these are declared as the multipliers for the signs, while the multipliers for the individual planets are stated separately. (25)
The number of Mercury is multiplied by ten, eight, seven, and five respectively for Jupiter, Venus, and Mercury;
for the remaining [planets], the planetary multiplier must be applied separately from the zodiacal multiplier. || 26 ||
Having thus multiplied and combined them, one should multiply again by seven;
when divided by twenty-seven, the years obtained therein indeed come to be.
One should multiply by twelve; the results obtained are, respectively, months, days, and ghaṭīs.
One should then subtract twenty-seven years from the maṇḍala once again.
When the planets are in conjunction, one should cause the mutual subtraction of half [the distance];
when they are in their sign of debilitation or set, one should likewise cause the subtraction of half among them. || 29 ||
In the enemy's field, there is likewise a reduction by one-third of the visible half;
in the case of an eclipse of the Sun or Moon due to the influence of the node (pāta), there is a reduction by one-third of that [reduction].
When a great number [of obstacles] is encountered during the removal, one should employ even more powerful means;
having subsequently subdued all of them, one should cause them to increase by means of the Varāṅga mantra.
There is no doubt that one who has obtained [the status of] a Mātaṅga attains a pure lifespan;
having calculated the days, months, and years as before, his planetary period (daśā) shall be determined.
In this manner, one should calculate the daśās for all the planets individually;
the path of the aṣṭavarga-daśā is the most excellent of all. || 33 ||
Bala, Bali, the asura Lavaṇa,
the passionate Murāri, Śikharīndra, Bhauma, Gaṇendra, and the asura Laghubhāva— by means of this verse [of praise], they were all liberated.
Gokarṇaraktā, however, is Puraṇarmathilī. || 34 ||
Rudra is the supreme abyss; Bhairava is the ground;
Rāgī, Valī, Bhāsvaragī, Bhaga, and Acala; and Vivasvān on the mountain, through his powerful desire to speak.
The wielder of the trident (Śiva), the founder of this sacred site, is dear to me here.
The group of eight, endowed with the fruits of all actions, is thus described;
otherwise, the knowledge of power arising from virtues and faults is difficult to discern.
Those zodiac signs that possess more than thirty degrees are givers of auspicious results;
beyond twenty-five degrees they are middling, and below that, the result is difficult.

If the fifth house has more fruits than the middle [the ascendant], in the eleventh house there is gain; if it is much diminished in the expenditure [the twelfth house], and if the ascendant has more expenditure, one becomes possessed of enjoyments and wealth. (38)

Having observed the results of the houses from the first (mūrti) to the twelfth (vyaya), one should know that excellence exists when [the strength] is greater, and one should point out defects when it is deficient. || 39 ||
Having excluded the sixth, eighth, and the two immovable signs, one should determine the others as "other" (parakalpa).
One should have all auspicious rites performed in the most excellent signs. || 40 ||
Having indeed combined the results from the ascendant up to Saturn, one should then multiply them by seven;
the result is obtained by dividing by twenty-seven.
In a year corresponding to that [planet], one may encounter suffering or disease;
thus are the results for the planets from Saturn to the Ascendant, as well as for Mars and Rāhu. (42)
In a year marked by the conjunction of auspicious planets, good fortune shall prevail;
one obtains sons, wealth, happiness, and so forth—of this there is no doubt. (43)
I have here declared the results of the eight groups in brief;
they have been explained in detail elsewhere by those of sharp intellect who are experts in that matter.
Chapter Twenty-Five:
Gulika and Other Upagrahas (Secondary Planets)
I bow to Māndī, known as Yamakaṇṭaka, who struck [the earth] with a half-blow, and who is called Kāla on earth; he who is renowned by the names Dhūma, Vyatīpāta, and Pariveṣa.
The secondary planets, Indra’s bow (the rainbow), and comets.
The movement of Rudradāsa, the pot, and the eternal expansion should be performed;
the increase and decrease of the day and night should be calculated therein.
But at night, the [planets] beginning with the fifth from the lord of the weekday [are considered]. (2)
Divya is the constant body of the khanīs;
Ruru is for the moon and Yamakaṇṭaka;
Bhaṭa is for half a prahāra and Naṭa.
The breasts are the two mines of the moon; he who knows this is victorious. || 3 ||
The foam of Time is the divine body of Rudra;
he is the dancer to be worshipped by them from the day of the Sun onwards; this is equal to the splendor of Māndiva.
In this case, it should be calculated clearly according to the method for the ascendant. || 4 ||

When the Sun is joined with thirteen degrees of the asterism Dhūmavedagṛha (Pūrvaphalgunī), there occurs the Vyatīpāta yoga; when he has moved away from that [asterism], it is Nyuta. When six asterisms have passed, there is Pariveśa; when he has moved away from this [asterism], there is Indradhanus (the rainbow) within the Maṇḍala.
When Ketu is joined here with one-eighth of a degree, and the Sun is then situated in that same single asterism; || 5 ||
In the chapter on houses (bhāvādhyāya), I have already previously declared the collective [considerations];
here, that very same firm fruit of the houses must be stated for those who are liberated [from planetary influences]. || 6 ||
Nevertheless, the specific details regarding pills and other such preparations are here being declared;
having compiled what was taught by the former masters, I have set it forth. (7)
He is a thief, cruel, devoid of discipline, and lacking in knowledge of the meaning of the Vedas and Shastras;
he is neither too stout nor deformed in his eyes, neither very intelligent nor one who has many sons;
he eats little, is deprived of happiness, is lustful, and does not live for long.
Even one who is dull-witted may become heroic, yet one who is irascible will be so when the Moon is in the ascendant.
One who quarrels does not receive flattering words;
one living in a foreign land does not obtain wealth or grain; nor does one who speaks words of dispute over subtle matters gain eloquence.
When the grandson of the Sun (Saturn) is situated in the house of wealth (the second house). || 9 ||
Endowed with qualities such as the pride and intoxication of separation, he was preoccupied with the agitation of amassing wealth through excessive anger;
yet he was free from sorrow and fear, and possessed of a broad chest.
When [the breath] is joined with the moon in the abode of the innate (sahaja). || 10 ||
If Saturn is in the fourth house, there will be a lack of friends, vehicles, and wealth;

one will be fickle-minded, lacking understanding, and short-lived. If it is in the fifth house, one will be a destroyer of many groups of enemies and will take delight in the science of spirits (bhūtavidyā).
If Gulika is situated in the sixth house, there will be a son who is virtuous and brave. || 11 ||
When Gulika is situated in the seventh house, the native is prone to quarrels, possesses many wives, is hated by the world, ungrateful, of little knowledge, and easily angered.
With impaired eyes and face and a short body, he became separated from his son when Jupiter was situated in the eighth house;
when Saturn was situated in the ninth house, he performed no auspicious deeds; and when it was situated in the tenth house, he was destitute.
One who possesses happiness, sound sleep, great splendor, and beauty when [the Moon] is situated in the second house. || 13 ||
If Gulika is situated in the twelfth house, one will be devoid of sense objects, miserable, and incur great expenditure;
or if it is in a trine from Gulika, or in the natal sign, or in a cruel Navamsha, the same results follow.

If joined with the Sun, he is a slayer of his father; if joined with the Moon, he causes suffering to his mother. If joined with Mars, there is separation from brothers; if joined with Mercury or Saturn, he is prone to madness.
If joined with Jupiter, he is a heretic; if joined with Venus, he has association with low-born women;
if joined with Saturn or Saturn’s son (Rahu), he is afflicted by leprosy and other diseases and is short-lived. || 16 ||

If Gulika is joined with Rāhu, conjoined with Ketu, afflicted by fire during the period of Saturn, and associated with a planet to be abandoned, then even one born as a king becomes a beggar for alms. || 17 ||
One should point out faults everywhere in the conjunction of Gulika;
however, one should declare auspiciousness everywhere in the conjunction of Yamakaṇṭaka.
In the bestowing of misfortune, Gulika is more powerful;
in the bestowing of auspiciousness, Yamakaṇṭaka would be so;
and all others [are powerful] in the bestowing of calamity.
They shall be endowed with the power of slowness, as well as the powers of vigor and supernatural transformation. || 19 ||

Gulika is said to be like Saturn; Yamakaṇṭaka is like Jupiter; at the time of the half-stroke (ardhaprahāra), its results are like those of Mercury, but during the [full] period, they are like those of Rāhu.
Kāla, Rāhu, Gulika, Mṛtyu, Jīvātuka, Yamakaṇṭaka,
and Ardhaprahāra are givers of auspiciousness when they occupy auspicious divisions (śubhāṅka).
If he were otherwise engaged, he might perform an evil deed. || 21 ||
Parāśara declares that those houses, such as the self (the first house), when occupied by malefics and conjoined with planets such as Mars, go to destruction.
During Dhūmā, there will be constant heat, fear of fire, and mental anguish;
during Vyatīpāta, there is danger from wild animals or the death of quadrupeds. (23)
During an eclipse, there is fear of water, water-borne disease, and imprisonment;
during a rainbow, there is injury from stones, wounds from weapons, and even death.
From Ketu, there is loss through falling or injury; from Ashani, the destruction of undertakings and fear.
One should declare the results during the period (dasha) of whichever house these [planets] occupy. || 25 ||

Short-lived, with an unpleasant face, possessing the quality of valor yet miserable and deprived of his children, agitated by enemies, with his passion shattered, he has met a death on a wicked path; he is full of faults, delighting in cruelty toward dharma and other virtues, and accompanied by a son who is likewise wicked.
In this manner, one should always declare the results of Ketu starting from the ascendant (lagna) in successive order. || 26 ||
The five sky-dwellers, beginning with Dhūma, move about unmanifest;
they are seen at certain times and places for the purpose of causing affliction to the world.
There was smoke, a mass of smoke, and some say the constellation of the tail;
a fall of meteors, the Vyatīpāta yoga, and a halo were seen. (28)
That which is seen well-known in the world is indeed remembered as Indra’s bow;
and Ketu, the comet, is the cause of affliction for the world. (29)
If the lord of the Gulika-bhava is strong, situated in a quadrant (kendraka) or a trine (trikoṇa), residing in its own house, or placed in its exaltation or a friendly sign,
[the native] becomes a leader of chariots, elephants, and horses, equal to the god of love.
He was a lord of the circle of the earth, whose fame was vast and honored. || 30 ||
Chapter Twenty-Six: The Results of the Planetary Transits (Gocara-phala)
Even though all the ascendants are present, the lunar ascendant is indeed preeminent among the planetary positions;
therefore, [one should consider] even from that current asterism...
One should declare the results according to the movements of the lords of the planets. || 1 ||

The Sun is situated in the sixth, third, and tenth houses; the Moon is in the third, tenth, sixth, seventh, and first houses; Jupiter is in the second, ninth, fifth, and fourth houses; Mars and Saturn are in the sixth and third houses;
Mercury is in the sixth, second, fourth, eighth, and tenth houses; and all [the other planets] are situated in the penultimate house.
Venus bestows auspicious results when it leaves behind the tenth, seventh, and sixth houses, just like the sun; the two serpents (Rāhu and Ketu) are likewise.
The Sun situated in the second, eleventh, or third house is declared auspicious when occupied by planets located in the fifth, ninth, fourth,
or twelfth houses.
If it is not pierced by Vyārkis, then [it is auspicious]. || 3 ||
The Moon, situated in the third, eleventh, sixth, eighth, or twelfth house from the Lagna, always bestows auspicious results;
likewise when it is in its own house, the fifth, the twelfth, the fourth, the seventh, or the ninth house.
If it is not perceived by the wise through the planets. || 4 ||
Mars situated in the third house from the ascendant (Vikrama) is auspicious,
provided that the planets occupying the twelfth, fifth,
and ninth houses do not aspect it; the same applies to Saturn.
But the upholding of the Dharma does not cease. || 5 ||
When Mercury is in its own sign, in water, in an enemy's sign, or in the eighth or twelfth house, it is not auspicious; however,
this is never the case when it is in its own triplicity, in Aries, in Taurus, or in the first or eleventh house.
If the planets are in conjunction with the lunar mansions at the time of birth. || 6 ||
When the auspicious priest of the Lord of Heaven (Jupiter) is situated in its own sign, its exaltation, or its mūlatrikoṇa,
and is not afflicted by planets moving in the sky (the other planets) in the twelfth, eighth, sixth, third, eleventh, or fifth houses, [it bestows prosperity].
If Venus is pierced by Mars, it is considered inauspicious; it destroys the eighth house, longevity, penance, and wealth.
It is likewise afflicted when planets occupy the eighth, twelfth, body (first), tenth, ninth, fifth, eleventh, or third houses from it.

In the first [house], it bestows the toil of birth and exhausts one's fortunes; in the second, it brings about anger, disease, and travel, as well as the loss of wealth, and does not grant happiness nor the utterance of its own name.
In the third, it grants the attainment of status, a collection of riches, auspiciousness, and the destruction of enemies.
In the fourth house, it bestows diseases and repeatedly causes obstacles to the enjoyment of garlands. || 9 ||
Situated in the fifth house, the Sun frequently causes agitation of wealth and bestows disease, delusion, and the like;
in the sixth house, it destroys diseases, subdues enemies, and wipes away sorrow and delusion;
situated in the seventh house, it brings about travel, danger to the stomach and anus, and a state of wretchedness for him.
Situated in the eighth house from Ruk (the fifth), it brings about quarrels, fear of the king, and distress. || 10 ||

When the Sun is in the tenth house, one encounters misfortune, distress in ascetic practice, separation from loved ones, and the suppression of mental activities; yet there is fierce success in action.
When it is in the eleventh house, there is position, honor, wealth, and the destruction of disease.
Affliction, the loss of wealth, enmity with friends, and finally fever. || 11 ||

In due order, the Moon bestows the dawning of fortune, the attainment of wealth, victory, renown, freedom from disease, pleasures, misfortune, the accomplishment of desired goals, joy, and expenditure. (12)
Mars, situated in the second house at the time of birth, produces internal grief, separation from kinsmen, diseases of blood and bile with fever, fear regarding speech, loss of wealth,
and yet brings victory, golden ornaments, and great joy.
In the fourth [house], there is displacement from one's position, abdominal pain, and suffering caused by kinsmen.
In the fifth [house], Mars brings about fever, improper anxiety, or distress caused by a son;
in the sixth, he brings the cessation of enmity and strife, as well as the alleviation of disease.
Victory, the acquisition of wealth, and favorability for all undertakings. || 14 ||

When Mars is situated in the seventh house, there is conflict with one's wife, eye disease, and abdominal ailments; in the eighth house, one is emaciated by fever and wounds, and deprived of wealth and honor;
and when Mars is located in the ninth house, there is humiliation due to the loss of wealth and other such misfortunes.
One's gait becomes slow due to the weakness of the body and the depletion of the bodily constituents. || 15 ||
When Mars is situated in the twelfth house in its transit (gocara), there will be misconduct, obstacles to actions, and exhaustion; however, there will also be an increase in wealth,
health, and lands.
The destruction of substance [occurs] through heat, fever, and other such ailments.
Loss of wealth, loss of fortune, fear of enemies, acquisition of riches, quarrels with wife, children, and kinsmen, victory, conflict,
gain of sons and wealth, then obstacles, and finally all-encompassing happiness.
The Moon (Cāndri) produces nourishment as well as the fear of defeat. || 17 ||
In the Jīva birth [Navāṃśa], one experiences departure from one's country, loss of wealth, and enmity;
yet, through the power of one's own speech, one attains riches and the happiness of one's family.
In the Duścikya [Navāṃśa], there is destruction of stability, separation from loved ones, obstacles to undertakings, and disease.
In the fourth house, there is suffering arising from kinsmen, as well as wretchedness and fear of quadrupeds.

In the sixth house, one attains the birth of a son, association with virtuous people, and favor from the king; however, in the sixth house of the minister, enemies, kinsmen, and diseases cause affliction.
One should remember that travel for auspicious purposes brings happiness through a wife and the acquisition of sons.
When Mars is in the eighth house, there is suffering due to the afflictions of the path and loss of wealth.
If Jupiter is in the ninth house (bhāgya), there is the attainment of all good fortune;
in the tenth house (karma), there is suffering regarding wealth, wife, and children;
and in the eleventh house (lābha), there is the gain of children, status, honor, and so forth.
In the letter Riḥpha, there is suffering and anxiety on account of wealth. || 20 ||
It bestows the enjoyment of all objects, the attainment of wealth, prosperity,
the increase of happiness and friends, the birth of a son, or misfortune; it indicates suffering from women, or the acquisition of fortune and happiness.
The minister of Indra’s enemy [Rāhu] brings about quarrel, fearlessness, and the attainment of wealth. || 21 ||
Illness, impurity, and the occurrence of rites; the loss of wealth and sons; the gain of position, servants, and riches;
the destruction of wife, kinsmen, and wealth; the loss of fortune, sons, and intellect;
total happiness; female ailments, fear on the road; and the destruction of one's own children, cattle, friends, and wealth, as well as disease and distress.
The son of the Sun (Saturn) indicates [events] from birth up to the eighth house in sequence, according to the strength of the signs. || 22 ||

When situated in the tenth house, [the Moon] brings about poverty, obstacles to Dharma, the dissolution of one's paternal kin, constant suffering, engagement in evil activities, loss of honor, or disease;
whereas situated in the eleventh house, it bestows happiness, the attainment of manifold wealth, and preeminent fame.
One finds rest from futile undertakings through friends, and from enemies, women, sons, disease, and at the end [of life].
The destruction of the body, the loss of wealth amidst happiness, suffering and the loss of purpose, the loss of happiness and death,
loss and gain, good fortune, and expenditure.
One should perform [the rite] starting from the birth-house in successive order. || 24 ||
Mars and the Sun occupy the first third of a sign;
Jupiter and Venus occupy the middle third of a sign;
and the Moon and Saturn occupy the final third of a sign.
The son of the Moon (Mercury) and the Serpent (Rāhu) always bestow their results at the time of ripening. || 25 ||

One should draw seven lines for the sphere of the constellations, extending upwards and likewise horizontally; then, starting from the constellation Īśa (Kṛttikā) and proceeding in order, one should count up to the constellation of the Sun (Pūrvaphalgunī).

If the Sun is associated with a malefic planet, it will surely cause death on the day of birth; fear of death in the asterism known as Ādhāna; loss of wealth during the performance of rites; and indeed, death itself. (26)
When thus pierced by malefic planets moving in the sky, death occurs;
when pierced by benefics, there is no death. Know all [the results] in this manner.
If a malefic planet is situated in the natal asterism, the asterism of the death-rite,
the destructive asterism, the adverse asterism, or the one called "slaughter," it shall produce the fear of death.
Likewise, when the [ascendant] is called auspicious, the remover of effects is twofold.
On the day of the sun's transit (saṅkrānti), at the entry of the planets, during an eclipse, or in battle;
likewise, upon the fall of a meteor or during a portentous event.
There would be the suffering of death and so forth for three births. || 29 ||
A planet that is asatphala (unfruitful) yet aspected by a benefic, or even one that is auspicious yet aspected by a malefic—
both of these two lords of the planets are rendered fruitless.
And he who has been gazed upon by his own enemy. || 30 ||
If the lord of a house is situated in an unfavorable bhāva, yet has reached its exaltation or its own domicile,
it does not cause harm provided it is placed in an excellent bhāva.
It bestows a full fruit within its spheres of influence. || 31 ||

In the *Graheśvarāruta*, those [planets] situated in auspicious *gocara* but having resorted to their debilitation (*nīca*), inimical signs (*ari*), or stupor (*mauḍhya*) are fruitless; however, those situated in inauspicious divisions (*aṅka*) are likewise so.
They bestow a bitter fruit that is no small matter. || 32 ||
Saturn, the Sun, Mars, and Jupiter, situated in the twelfth, eighth, or second houses, cause doubt regarding life, loss of position, and depletion of wealth. (33)
Mars is in the eighth from the Moon, Rahu is in the seventh, Jupiter is in the third from the Sun,
Saturn is in the fifth, and Mercury is in the fourth from the Ascendant.
One should specifically predict loss of honor, loss of wealth, and death. || 34 ||

The *aṅgagrahas* are: four on the face, one on the earth [the feet], four on the head, four on the chest, four on the right hand, six on the left foot, four on the left hand, two on the eyes, and two on the private parts.
The Sun, situated in the body according to the house of birth, produces various results: destruction, prosperity, victory, wealth, poverty, physical affliction, gain, or death. (35)

In the face of the Moon (śītāṃśu), there is extreme fear for two [houses]; on the head, security; in the ocean (the fourth house), victory over enemies for two [houses]; in the eyes (the fifth and sixth houses), wealth from the natal sign;
in the heart (the seventh house), happiness of the self for five [houses]; and in the left hand (the eighth house), opposition for three [houses], in due order.
The feet produce foreign residence in six [houses] and the acquisition of wealth in three; in the hand [they produce] gain. (36)
If Mars is in the mouth, it causes death; in the feet, conflict for six months; in the chest, victory for three months; in the left hand, fourfold subjugation;
in the head, two months of gain; in the face, excessive fear; and in the right hand, security.
The ocean, two eyes, and travel to a foreign land [are determined] from one's own natal asterism. (37)
When [the breath] reaches the head, there is grief; at the face, gain; at the hands, misfortune; at the belly, a collection of wealth; at the genitals, destruction;

and at the two feet, stability—thus it is for one honored by the lords of the gods. Furthermore, there are three [breaths] in the head, three in the face, six in the hands, five in the belly, two in the genitals, and four in the two feet.
When [the breath] reaches these places, [one experiences] grief, gain, misfortune, a mass of wealth, destruction, and likewise stability.
Likewise, Saturn gives [results] starting from its own day, and Mercury does so as well, in due order. || 38 ||
The [syllables] corresponding to earth (1), water (4), fire (3), qualities (3), Vedas (4), arrows (5), fire (3), eyes (2),
and weapons (2) are placed respectively on the face, hands, feet, and soles; in the hand, the belly, the head, the two eyes, and the back.
Having placed [the letters] in sequence starting from one's own natal asterism, together with the asterism occupied by Saturn. || 39 ||
Suffering, happiness, departure, destruction, gain, one's own enjoyment, pleasure, and death—
these are the results Saturn declares according to the sequence of the faces.
Let them speak thus regarding this very [state] of darkness and the sky-walker.
In whichever of the eight divisions there are more points, the lord of planets situated therein, according to its transit (gocara),
declares a result corresponding to that; [if it is in the twelfth or sixth house,] it speaks of auspicious results.
Or even when situated in a *randhra* (the eighth house), it bestows auspiciousness. || 41 ||
The twelfth lunar mansion belongs to Ravi (the Sun), the third to Bhūsuta (Mars), the sixth to Guru (Jupiter), and the eighth to Śani (Saturn). || 42 ||
And for these, the front-row and back-row seats have been proclaimed;
the fifth star of Śukra and the seventh of Candraja [are to be used]. (43)
For Rāhu, it is the ninth asterism, and for the Moon, the twenty-second;
one should count from the asterism occupied by the planet. In the case of *lattā*, there is suffering in the birth asterism.
If [the moon] is in the Sun's [division], there will be the loss of all wealth; in the division of Rāhu (Tamas), suffering is said to occur.
In the Jīvalattā [division], death occurs, and the destruction of kinsmen brings great fear. (45)
For Venus, there is quarrel and loss; for Mercury, however, there is misfortune.
For the Moon, there will be great loss, with the result being merely a blow from a whip.
In all cases where there is a mixture of lattās, one should declare for men a result of double, triple,
or more degrees of evil, according to the increasing number of lattās caused by the planets.
The auspicious transits (vedha) mentioned in the Sarvatobhadra diagram bring about welfare;
one should contemplate the malefic transits as being more painful and consider them according to their respective spheres of influence (gocara).
Chapter Twenty-Seven:
The Yoga of Renunciation (*pravrajyā-yoga*)
When the Khanotha is joined by four planets situated in trines, and is free from those situated in angles,
and when the Lagna is at the end of a house in a benefic portion;
And when Jupiter is in the center or in an angle, one is liberated. || 1 ||
When four or more planets are situated in a single asterism, one should declare [the result] there according to the strongest [planet];
some say that renunciation occurs in that case.
When the lord of the ascendant is conjoined with the lord of the tenth house, [the result] is equal to that of the lord of the tenth house. || 2 ||
The Moon situated in the Drekkāṇa of Saturn, aspected by Mars and Saturn, brings about asceticism;
or [the Moon] in a portion of Mars, aspected by Saturn.
Furthermore, they describe that [lagna] as being equal to its own ninth-part (navāṃśa). || 3 ||
If the lord of the birth [ascendant] is aspected by Saturn and not aspected by the remaining planets at a person's birth,
he will certainly perform his own initiation.
What was stated previously should also be considered here. || 4 ||
The Sun regards the Lord of Yogis or an initiate as a pilgrim;
the Moon, one who knows evil mantras as a follower of Baudhāyana;
Mars, one who has not entered other schools of thought as a knower of Vedānta; and the venerable Indra, the best of ascetics who follows the conduct of a Bhṛgu-linga.
Or a Vrātya, one who lives as an actor, a Śani, one who has fallen, or a heretic. || 5 ||
If the lord of the ascendant observes the Moon— which is endowed with extraordinary strength during the bright fortnight— as being devoid of strength,
then the native becomes a wretched person, suffering and consumed by grief.
Deprived of wealth and people, he obtained food and drink only with great difficulty. || 6 ||
If Rājayoga should occur during the conjunction of the planets as described by the sages,
it subsequently uproots all the ripening of inauspicious results and produces a consecrated lord of the earth who is virtuous in character.
The pair of whose lotus feet was touched by the foreheads of prostrating kings.
If four planets, including the lord of the ascendant, are strong and situated in a quadrant (kendram), a trine (trikoṇam), or another auspicious house, then there will be success in renunciation;
one should declare this especially when they are in very favorable positions due to an abundance of benefic influences.
If one were to treat the renunciation honored by the virtuous and esteemed as something else, it would be censured. || 8 ||
Chapter Twenty-Eight:
The Chapter on Conclusion (Upasaṃhārādhyāya)
The chapter on designations (saṃjñādhyāya), the chapter on strength (vīryādhyāya) known as the "maker" (kāraka) and the "divisions" (varga), then the "action-living" (karmajīvā) and the "yoga";
the yoga for kings, the nature of the zodiac signs (rāśiśīla), and [the nature] of the planets.
One whose nature has attained the ascendant of Aries and the other signs [is as follows]. || 1 ||
The state of being a wife, the birth of female children, the yoga of the child's untimely death, and then disease—
these are the states resulting from the twelfth house from that [the seventh] house.
Therefore, there would be an exit from the two types of grasping and so forth. || 2 ||
Whatever fruit belongs to the Sun and others, that same [fruit] is obtained for the houses and so forth; the periods (daśās) of the lords of the houses follow,
and then the period known as the Antardaśā of the Sun and others.
The eightfold division of Kālacakra consists of the left and the right. || 3 ||
The *Horāsāra* contains the *Aṣṭavarga*,
the chapter on *Māndya*, and the *Gocara*;
it consists of twenty-seven chapters.
In this birth, I declare this which was born of the sphere (Golaja). || 4 ||
By me, Śrī Śālivāṭija by name, a master of mantras,
an astrologer, and the foremost of the twice-born, this is indeed composed for the delight of the virtuous astronomers.
Having worshipped Mother Śakuntalā, who bestows all desired objects,
this *Phaladīpikā* was composed through her special grace.
